καλοδιδάσκαλος.shortDef: from καλός and διδάσκαλος; a teacher of the right:--teacher of good things.

καλοὶ λιμένες.shortDef: plural of καλός and λιμήν; Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete:--fair havens.

καλοποιέω.shortDef: from καλός and ποιέω; to do well, i.e. live virtuously:--well doing.

καλός.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively) good (literally or morally), i.e. valuable or virtuous (for appearance or use, and thus distinguished from ἀγαθός, which is properly intrinsic):--X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy.

κάλυμα.shortDef: from καλύπτω; a cover, i.e. veil:--vail.

καλύπτω.shortDef: akin to κλέπτω and κρύπτω; to cover up (literally or figuratively):--cover, hide.

καλῶς.shortDef: adverb from καλός; well (usually morally):--(in a) good (place), honestly, + recover, (full) well.

glosses: from a compound of κατά and the base of μυστήριον
καμμύω.shortDef: from a compound of κατά and the base of μυστήριον; to shut down, i.e. close the eyes:--close.

κάμνω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken):--faint, sick, be wearied.

κάμπτω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to bend:--bow.

κἄν.shortDef: from καί and ἐάν; and (or even) if:--and (also) if (so much as), if but, at the least, though, yet.

κανᾶ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (compare קָנָה); Cana, a place in Palestine:--Cana.

κανανίτης.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (compare קַנָּא); zealous; Cananites, an epithet:--Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from Χαναάν).

κανδάκη.shortDef: of foreign origin; Candacè, an Egyptian queen:--Candace.

κανών.shortDef: from  (a straight reed, i.e. rod); a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity):--line, rule.

glosses: of Hebrew origin (probably כָּפָר and נַחוּם)
καπερναούμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (probably כָּפָר and נַחוּם); Capernaum (i.e. Caphanachum), a place in Palestine:--Capernaum.

καπηλεύω.shortDef: from  (a huckster); to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively):--corrupt.

καππαδοκία.shortDef: of foreign origin; Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor:--Cappadocia.

καρδία.shortDef: prolonged from a primary  (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle:--(+ broken-)heart(-ed).

καρδιογνώστης.shortDef: from καρδία and γινώσκω; a heart-knower:--which knowest the hearts.

glosses: probably from the base of ἁρπάζω
καρπός.shortDef: probably from the base of ἁρπάζω; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively:--fruit.

κάρπος.shortDef: perhaps for καρπός; Carpus, probably a Christian:--Carpus.

καρποφορέω.shortDef: from καρποφόρος; to be fertile (literally or figuratively):--be (bear, bring forth) fruit(-ful).

καρτερέω.shortDef: from a derivative of κράτος (transposed); to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient):--endure.

κάρφος.shortDef: from  (to wither); a dry twig or straw:--mote.

κατά.shortDef: a primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined):--about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), … by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with. In composition it retains many of these applications, and frequently denotes opposition, distribution, or intensity.

glosses: from κατά and the base of βάσις
καταβαίνω.shortDef: from κατά and the base of βάσις; to descend (literally or figuratively):--come (get, go, step) down, fall (down).

καταβάλλω.shortDef: from κατά and βάλλω; to throw down:--cast down, lay.

καταβαρέω.shortDef: from κατά and βαρέω; to impose upon:--burden.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of the base of βάσις
καταβιβάζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of the base of βάσις; to cause to go down, i.e. precipitate:--bring (thrust) down.

καταβολή.shortDef: from καταβάλλω; a deposition, i.e. founding; figuratively, conception:--conceive, foundation.

glosses: from κατά and βραβεύω (in its original sense)
καταβραβεύω.shortDef: from κατά and βραβεύω (in its original sense); to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation):--beguile of reward.

glosses: from κατά and the base of ἄγγελος
καταγγέλλω.shortDef: from κατά and the base of ἄγγελος; to proclaim, promulgate:--declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach.

καταγινώσκω.shortDef: from κατά and γινώσκω; to note against, i.e. find fault with:--blame, condemn.

glosses: from κατά and the base of ῥήγνυμι
κατάγνυμι.shortDef: from κατά and the base of ῥήγνυμι; to rend in pieces, i.e. crack apart:--break.

κατάγω.shortDef: from κατά and ἄγω; to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel:--bring (down, forth), (bring to) land, touch.

καταγωνίζομαι.shortDef: from κατά and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome:--subdue.

καταδέω.shortDef: from κατά and δέω; to tie down, i.e. bandage (a wound):--bind up.

κατάδηλος.shortDef: from κατά intensive and δῆλος; manifest:--far more evident.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of δίκη
καταδικάζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of δίκη; to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty:--condemn.

καταδιώκω.shortDef: from κατά and διώκω; to hunt down, i.e. search for:--follow after.

καταδουλόω.shortDef: from κατά and δουλόω; to enslave utterly:--bring into bondage.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of δυνάστης
καταδυναστεύω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of δυνάστης; to exercise dominion against, i.e. oppress:--oppress.

καταισχύνω.shortDef: from κατά and αἰσχύνομαι; to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush:--confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d).

κατακαίω.shortDef: from κατά and καίω; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. consume wholly:--burn (up, utterly).

κατακαλύπτω.shortDef: from κατά and καλύπτω; to cover wholly, i.e. veil:--cover, hide.

κατακαυχάομαι.shortDef: from κατά and καυχάομαι; to exult against (i.e. over):--boast (against), glory, rejoice against.

κατάκειμαι.shortDef: from κατά and κεῖμαι; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal:--keep, lie, sit at meat (down).

κατακλάω.shortDef: from κατά and κλάω; to break down, i.e. divide:--break.

κατακλείω.shortDef: from κατά and κλείω; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. incarcerate:--shut up.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of a compound of κλῆρος and δίδωμι
κατακληροδοτέω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of a compound of κλῆρος and δίδωμι; to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate:--divide by lot.

κατακλίνω.shortDef: from κατά and κλίνω; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table:--(make) sit down (at meat).

glosses: from κατά and the base of κλύδων
κατακλύζω.shortDef: from κατά and the base of κλύδων; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge:--overflow.

κατακολουθέω.shortDef: from κατά and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany closely:--follow (after).

κατακόπτω.shortDef: from κατά and κόπτω; to chop down, i.e. mangle:--cut.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of κρημνός
κατακρημνίζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of κρημνός; to precipitate down:--cast down headlong.

κατάκριμα.shortDef: from κατακρίνω; an adverse sentence (the verdict):--condemnation.

κατακρίνω.shortDef: from κατά and κρίνω; to judge against, i.e. sentence:--condemn, damn.

κατακυριεύω.shortDef: from κατά and κυριεύω; to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate:--exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.

καταλαλέω.shortDef: from κατάλαλος; to be a traducer, i.e. to slander:--speak against (evil of).

glosses: from κατά and the base of λαλέω
κατάλαλος.shortDef: from κατά and the base of λαλέω; talkative against, i.e. a slanderer:--backbiter.

καταλαμβάνω.shortDef: from κατά and λαμβάνω; to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively):--apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.

glosses: from κατά and λέγω (in its original meaning)
καταλέγω.shortDef: from κατά and λέγω (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol:--take into the number.

κατάλειμμα.shortDef: from καταλείπω; a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few:--remnant.

καταλείπω.shortDef: from κατά and λείπω; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining:--forsake, leave, reserve.

καταλιθάζω.shortDef: from κατά and λιθάζω; to stone down, i.e. to death:--stone.

καταλλαγή.shortDef: from καταλλάσσω; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor:--atonement, reconciliation(-ing).

καταλλάσσω.shortDef: from κατά and ἀλλάσσω; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference:--reconcile.

κατάλοιπος.shortDef: from κατά and λοιποί; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest):--residue.

κατάλυμα.shortDef: from καταλύω; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place:-- guestchamber, inn.

καταλύω.shortDef: from κατά and λύω; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare κατάλυμα) to halt for the night:--destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down.

καταμανθάνω.shortDef: from κατά and μανθάνω; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully:--consider.

καταμαρτυρέω.shortDef: from κατά and μαρτυρέω; to testify against:--witness against.

καταμένω.shortDef: from κατά and μένω; to stay fully, i.e. reside:--abide.

glosses: from κατά and accusative case plural feminine of μόνος (with χώρα implied)
καταμόνας.shortDef: from κατά and accusative case plural feminine of μόνος (with χώρα implied); according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately:--alone.

κατανάθεμα.shortDef: from κατά (intensive) and ἀνάθεμα; an imprecation:--curse.

καταναθεματίζω.shortDef: from κατά (intensive) and ἀναθεματίζω; to imprecate:--curse.

καταναλίσκω.shortDef: from κατά and ἀναλίσκω; to consume utterly:--consume.

καταναρκάω.shortDef: from κατά and  (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive):--be burdensome (chargeable).

κατανεύω.shortDef: from κατά and νεύω; to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make signs to:--beckon.

κατανοέω.shortDef: from κατά and νοιέω; to observe fully:--behold, consider, discover, perceive.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of ἀντί
καταντάω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet against, i.e. arrive at (literally or figuratively):--attain, come.

κατάνυξις.shortDef: from κατανύσσω; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with νεύω or even with νύξ)) stupor (lethargy):--slumber.

κατανύσσω.shortDef: from κατά and νύσσω; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick"):--prick.

καταξιόω.shortDef: from κατά and ἀξιόω; to deem entirely deserving:--(ac-)count worthy.

καταπατέω.shortDef: from κατά and πατέω; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain:--trample, tread (down, underfoot).

κατάπαυσις.shortDef: from καταπαύω; reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode:--rest.

καταπαύω.shortDef: from κατά and παύω; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist:--cease, (give) rest(-rain).

glosses: from a compound of κατά and a congener of πέτομαι
καταπέτασμα.shortDef: from a compound of κατά and a congener of πέτομαι; something spread thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place) in the Jewish Temple:--vail.

καταπίνω.shortDef: from κατά and πίνω; to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or figuratively):--devour, drown, swallow (up).

καταπίπτω.shortDef: from κατά and πίπτω; to fall down:--fall (down).

καταπλέω.shortDef: from κατά and πλέω; to sail down upon a place, i.e. to land at:--arrive.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of πόνος
καταπονέω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of πόνος; to labor down, i.e. wear with toil (figuratively, harass):--oppress, vex.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of the same as Πόντος
καταποντίζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of the same as Πόντος; to plunge down, i.e. submerge:--drown, sink.

κατάρα.shortDef: from κατά (intensive) and ἀρά; imprecation, execration:--curse(-d, ing).

καταράομαι.shortDef: middle voice from κατάρα; to execrate; by analogy, to doom:--curse.

καταργέω.shortDef: from κατά and ἀργέω; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively:--abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.

καταριθμέω.shortDef: from κατά and ἀριθμέω; to reckon among:--number with.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of ἄρτιος
καταρτίζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of ἄρτιος; to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust:--fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.

κατασείω.shortDef: from κατά and σείω; to sway downward, i.e. make a signal:--beckon.

κατασκάπτω.shortDef: from κατά and σκάπτω; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy:--dig down, ruin.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of σκεῦος
κατασκευάζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of σκεῦος; to prepare thoroughly (properly, by external equipment; whereas ἑτοιμάζω refers rather to internal fitness); by implication, to construct, create:--build, make, ordain, prepare.

κατασκηνόω.shortDef: from κατά and σκηνόω; to camp down, i.e. haunt; figuratively, to remain:--lodge, rest.

κατασκήνωσις.shortDef: from κατασκηνόω; an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch:--nest.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of σκιά
κατασκιάζω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of σκιά; to overshade, i.e. cover:--shadow.

κατασκοπέω.shortDef: from κατάσκοπος; to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously:--spy out.

glosses: from κατά (intensive) and σκοπός (in the sense of a watcher)
κατάσκοπος.shortDef: from κατά (intensive) and σκοπός (in the sense of a watcher); a reconnoiterer:--spy.

glosses: middle voice from κατά and σοφίζω
κατασοφίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from κατά and σοφίζω; to be crafty against, i.e. circumvent:--deal subtilly with.

καταστέλλω.shortDef: from κατά and στέλλω; to put down, i.e. quell:--appease, quiet.

κατάστημα.shortDef: from καθίστημι; properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively) demeanor:--behaviour.

καταστολή.shortDef: from καταστέλλω; a deposit, i.e. (specially) costume:--apparel.

καταστρέφω.shortDef: from κατά and στρέφω; to turn upside down, i.e. upset:--overthrow.

καταστρηνιάω.shortDef: from κατά and στρηνιάω; to become voluptuous against:--begin to wax wanton against.

καταστροφή.shortDef: from καταστρέφω; an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively, apostasy:--overthrow, subverting.

καταστρώννυμι.shortDef: from κατά and στρώννυμι; to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate (slay):--overthrow.

κατασύρω.shortDef: from κατά and σύρω; to drag down, i.e. arrest judicially:--hale.

κατασφάττω.shortDef: from κατά and σφάζω; to kill down, i.e. slaughter:--slay.

κατασφραγίζω.shortDef: from κατά and σφραγίζω; to seal closely:--seal.

κατάσχεσις.shortDef: from κατέχω; a holding down, i.e. occupancy:--possession.

κατατίθημι.shortDef: from κατά and τίθημι; to place down, i.e. deposit (literally or figuratively):--do, lay, shew.

glosses: from a compound of κατά and  (to cut)
κατατομή.shortDef: from a compound of κατά and  (to cut); a cutting down (off), i.e. mutilation (ironically):--concision. Compare ἀποκόπτω.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of τόξον
κατατοξεύω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of τόξον; to shoot down with an arrow or other missile:--thrust through.

κατατρέχω.shortDef: from κατά and τρέχω; to run down, i.e. hasten from a tower:--run down.

glosses: from κατά and φέρω (including its alternate)
καταφέρω.shortDef: from κατά and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote:--fall, give, sink down.

καταφεύγω.shortDef: from κατά and φεύγω; to flee down (away):--flee.

καταφθείρω.shortDef: from κατά and φθείρω; to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or (figuratively) to deprave; --corrupt, utterly perish.

καταφρονέω.shortDef: from κατά and φρονέω; to think against, i.e. disesteem:--despise.

καταχέω.shortDef: from κατά and cheo (to pour); to pour down (out):--pour.

καταχθόνιος.shortDef: from κατά and  (the ground); subterranean, i.e. infernal (belonging to the world of departed spirits):--under the earth.

καταχράομαι.shortDef: from κατά and χράομαι; to overuse, i.e. misuse:--abuse.

καταψύχω.shortDef: from κατά and ψύχω; to cool down (off), i.e. refresh:--cool.

κατείδωλος.shortDef: from κατά (intensively) and εἴδωλον; utterly idolatrous:--wholly given to idolatry.

κατέναντι.shortDef: from κατά and ἔναντι; directly opposite:--before, over against.

κατενώπιον.shortDef: from κατά and ἐνώπιον; directly in front of:--before (the presence of), in the sight of.

κατεξουσιάζω.shortDef: from κατά and ἐξουσιάζω; to have (wield) full privilege over:--exercise authority.

κατεργάζομαι.shortDef: from κατά and ἐργάζομαι; to work fully, i.e. accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion:--cause, to (deed), perform, work (out).

glosses: from κατά and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate)
κατέρχομαι.shortDef: from κατά and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to come (or go) down (literally or figuratively):--come (down), depart, descend, go down, land.

glosses: from κατά and ἐσθίω (including its alternate)
κατεσθίω.shortDef: from κατά and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to eat down, i.e. devour (literally or figuratively):--devour.

κατευθύνω.shortDef: from κατά and εὐθύνω; to straighten fully, i.e. (figuratively) direct:--guide, direct.

κατεφίστημι.shortDef: from κατά and ἐφίστημι; to stand over against, i.e. rush upon (assault):--make insurrection against.

κατέχω.shortDef: from κατά and ἔχω; to hold down (fast), in various applications (literally or figuratively):--have, hold (fast), keep (in memory), let, X make toward, possess, retain, seize on, stay, take, withhold.

κατηγορέω.shortDef: from κατήγορος; to be a plaintiff, i.e. to charge with some offence:--accuse, object.

κατηγορία.shortDef: from κατήγορος; a complaint ("category"), i.e. criminal charge:--accusation (X -ed).

κατήγορος.shortDef: from κατά and ἀγορά; against one in the assembly, i.e. a complainant at law; specially, Satan:--accuser.

glosses: from a compound of κατά and perhaps a derivative of the base of φαίνω (meaning downcast in look)
κατήφεια.shortDef: from a compound of κατά and perhaps a derivative of the base of φαίνω (meaning downcast in look); demureness, i.e. (by implication) sadness:--heaviness.

κατηχέω.shortDef: from κατά and ἦχος; to sound down into the ears, i.e. (by implication) to indoctrinate ("catechize") or (genitive case) to apprise of:--inform, instruct, teach.

glosses: from κατά and a derivative of ἰός
κατιόω.shortDef: from κατά and a derivative of ἰός; to rust down, i.e. corrode:--canker.

κατισχύω.shortDef: from κατά and ἰσχύω; to overpower:--prevail (against).

κατοικέω.shortDef: from κατά and οἰκέω; to house permanently, i.e. reside (literally or figuratively):--dwell(-er), inhabitant(-ter).

κατοίκησις.shortDef: from κατοικέω; residence (properly, the act; but by implication, concretely, the mansion):--dwelling.

κατοικητήριον.shortDef: from a derivative of κατοικέω; a dwelling-place:--habitation.

glosses: middle voice from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (compare ἔσοπτρον)
κατοπτρίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (compare ἔσοπτρον); to mirror oneself, i.e. to see reflected (figuratively):--behold as in a glass.

glosses: from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀρθός (compare διόρθωσις)
κατόρθωμα.shortDef: from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀρθός (compare διόρθωσις); something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration):--very worthy deed.

κάτω.shortDef: (compare κατώτερος); adverb from κατά; downwards:--beneath, bottom, down, under.

κατώτερος.shortDef: comparative from κάτω; inferior (locally, of Hades):--lower.

καῦμα.shortDef: from καίω; properly, a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a glow:--heat.

καυσόω.shortDef: from καῦσις; to set on fire:--fervent heat.

καυτηριάζω.shortDef: from a derivative of καίω; to brand ("cauterize"), i.e. (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively):--sear with a hot iron.

glosses: from some (obsolete) base akin to that of  (to boast) and εὔχομαι
καυχάομαι.shortDef: from some (obsolete) base akin to that of  (to boast) and εὔχομαι; to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense):--(make) boast, glory, joy, rejoice.

καύχημα.shortDef: from καυχάομαι; a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in a good or a bad sense:--boasting, (whereof) to glory (of), glorying, rejoice(-ing).

καύχησις.shortDef: from καυχάομαι; boasting (properly, the act; by implication, the object), in a good or a bad sense:--boasting, whereof I may glory, glorying, rejoicing.

κεγχρεαί.shortDef: probably from kegchros (millet); Cenchreæ, a port of Corinth:--Cencrea.

κεδρών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (קִדְרוֹן); Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem:--Cedron.

glosses: middle voice of a primary verb
κεῖμαι.shortDef: middle voice of a primary verb; to lie outstretched (literally or figuratively):--be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie. Compare τίθημι.

κειρία.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a swathe, i.e. winding-sheet:--graveclothes.

κέλευμα.shortDef: from κελεύω; a cry of incitement:--shout.

κελεύω.shortDef: from a primary  (to urge on); "hail"; to incite by word, i.e. order:--bid, (at, give) command(-ment).

κενοδοξία.shortDef: from κενόδοξος; empty glorying, i.e. self-conceit:--vain-glory.

κενόδοξος.shortDef: from κενός and δόξα; vainly glorifying, i.e. self-conceited:--desirous of vain-glory.

κενός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; empty (literally or figuratively):--empty, (in) vain.

glosses: from a presumed compound of κενός and φωνή
κενοφωνία.shortDef: from a presumed compound of κενός and φωνή; empty sounding, i.e. fruitless discussion:--vain.

κενόω.shortDef: from κενός; to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify:--make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain.

κέντρον.shortDef: from  (to prick); a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse):--prick, sting.

κεντυρίων.shortDef: of Latin origin; a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred soldiers:--centurion.

κενῶς.shortDef: adverb from κενός; vainly, i.e. to no purpose:--in vain.

glosses: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of κέρας
κεραία.shortDef: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of κέρας; something horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively, the least particle):--tittle.

κεραμικός.shortDef: from κέραμος; made of clay, i.e. earthen:--of a potter.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of κέραμος
κεράμιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of κέραμος; an earthenware vessel, i.e. jar:--pitcher.

glosses: probably from the base of κεράννυμι (through the idea of mixing clay and water)
κέραμος.shortDef: probably from the base of κεράννυμι (through the idea of mixing clay and water); earthenware, i.e. a tile (by analogy, a thin roof or awning):--tiling.

glosses: prolonged form of a more primary   (which is used in certain tenses)
κεράννυμι.shortDef: prolonged form of a more primary   (which is used in certain tenses); to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for drinking):--fill, pour out. Compare μίγνυμι.

glosses: from a primary  (the hair of the head)
κέρας.shortDef: from a primary  (the hair of the head); a horn (literally or figuratively):--horn.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of κέρας
κεράτιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of κέρας; something horned, i.e. (specially) the pod of the carob-tree:--husk.

κερδαίνω.shortDef: from κέρδος; to gain (literally or figuratively):--(get) gain, win.

κέρδος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; gain (pecuniary or genitive case):--gain, lucre.

κέρμα.shortDef: from κείρω; a clipping (bit), i.e. (specially) a coin:--money.

κερματιστής.shortDef: from a derivative of κέρμα; a handler of coins, i.e. money-broker:--changer of money.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of κεφαλή
κεφάλαιον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of κεφαλή; a principal thing, i.e. main point; specially, an amount (of money):--sum.

κεφαλαιόω.shortDef: from the same as κεφάλαιον; (specially) to strike on the head:--wound in the head.

glosses: from the primary  (in the sense of seizing)
κεφαλή.shortDef: from the primary  (in the sense of seizing); the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively:--head.

κεφαλίς.shortDef: from κεφαλή; properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled):--volume.

κῆνσος.shortDef: of Latin origin; properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by implication) a tax:--tribute.

κηπουρός.shortDef: from κῆπος and  (a warden); a garden-keeper, i.e. gardener:--gardener.

κηρίον.shortDef: diminutive from  (wax); a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb:--(honey-)comb.

κήρυγμα.shortDef: from κηρύσσω; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication, the gospel itself):--preaching.

κῆρυξ.shortDef: from κηρύσσω; a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the gospel):--preacher.

κηρύσσω.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel):--preacher(-er), proclaim, publish.

glosses: probably from the base of χάσμα
κῆτος.shortDef: probably from the base of χάσμα; a huge fish (as gaping for prey):--whale.

κηφᾶς.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (compare כֵּף); the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a surname of Peter:--Cephas.

κιβωτός.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a box, i.e. the sacred ark and that of Noah:--ark.

κιθαρίζω.shortDef: from κιθάρα; to play on a lyre:--harp.

glosses: from κιθάρα and a derivative of the same as ᾠδή
κιθαρῳδός.shortDef: from κιθάρα and a derivative of the same as ᾠδή; a lyre-singer(-player), i.e. harpist:--harper.

κιλικία.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor:--Cilicia.

κινδυνεύω.shortDef: from κίνδυνος; to undergo peril:--be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy.

κινέω.shortDef: from  (poetic for , to go); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively:--(re-)move(-r), way.

κίς.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (קִישׁ); Cis (i.e. Kish), an Israelite:--Cis.

κλάδος.shortDef: from κλάω; a twig or bough (as if broken off):--branch.

κλαίω.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; to sob, i.e. wail aloud (whereas 1145 is rather to cry silently):--bewail, weep.

κλαύδη.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Claude, an island near Crete:--Clauda.

κλαυδία.shortDef: feminine of Κλαύδιος; Claudia, a Christian woman:--Claudia.

κλαύδιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans:--Claudius.

κλαυθμός.shortDef: from κλαίω; lamentation:--wailing, weeping, X wept.

κλάω.shortDef: a primary verb; to break (specially, of bread):--break.

κλείς.shortDef: from κλείω; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively:--key.

κλείω.shortDef: a primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively):--shut (up).

κλέμμα.shortDef: from κλέπτω; stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act):--theft.

glosses: probably contracted from  (compound of κλέος and πατήρ)
κλεόπας.shortDef: probably contracted from  (compound of κλέος and πατήρ); Cleopas, a Christian:--Cleopas.

glosses: from a shorter form of καλέω
κλέος.shortDef: from a shorter form of καλέω; renown (as if being called):--glory.

κλέπτης.shortDef: from κλέπτω; a stealer (literally or figuratively):--thief. Compare λῃστής.

κλῆμα.shortDef: from κλάω; a limb or shoot (as if broken off):--branch.

κλήμης.shortDef: of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a Christian:--Clement.

κληρονομέω.shortDef: from κληρονόμος; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively):--be heir, (obtain by) inherit(-ance).

κληρονομία.shortDef: from κληρονόμος; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession:--inheritance.

glosses: from κλῆρος and the base of νόμος (in its original sense of partitioning
κληρονόμος.shortDef: from κλῆρος and the base of νόμος (in its original sense of partitioning, i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e. inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a possessor:--heir.

glosses: probably from κλάω (through the idea of using bits of wood
κλῆρος.shortDef: probably from κλάω (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose; a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively):--heritage, inheritance, lot, part.

κληρόω.shortDef: from κλῆρος; to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege):--obtain an inheritance.

glosses: from a shorter form of καλέω
κλῆσις.shortDef: from a shorter form of καλέω; an invitation (figuratively):--calling.

κλητός.shortDef: from the same as κλῆσις; invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a saint:--called.

κλίβανος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in:--oven.

κλίμα.shortDef: from κλίνω; a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country:--part, region.

κλίνη.shortDef: from κλίνω; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating):--bed, table.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of κλίνη
κλινίδιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of κλίνη; a pallet or little couch:--bed.

κλίνω.shortDef: a primary verb; to slant or slope, i.e. incline or recline (literally or figuratively):--bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away.

κλισία.shortDef: from a derivative of κλίνω; properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and specially), a party at a meal:--company.

κλύδων.shortDef: from  (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively):--raging, wave.

κλυδωνίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from κλύδων; to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to fluctuate:--toss to and fro.

κλωπᾶς.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (corresponding to אַחְאָב); Clopas, an Israelite:--Cleophas.

κνήθω.shortDef: from a primary  (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle:--X itching.

κνίδος.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor:--Cnidus.

κοδράντης.shortDef: of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as:--farthing.

κοιλία.shortDef: from  ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart:--belly, womb.

κοιμάω.shortDef: from κεῖμαι; to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to slumber; figuratively, to decease:--(be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead.

κοίμησις.shortDef: from κοιμάω; sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose:--taking of rest.

κοινός.shortDef: probably from σύν; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane:--common, defiled, unclean, unholy.

κοινόω.shortDef: from κοινός; to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially):--call common, defile, pollute, unclean.

κοινωνέω.shortDef: from κοινωνός; to share with others (objectively or subjectively):--communicate, distribute, be partaker.

κοινωνία.shortDef: from κοινωνός; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction:--(to) communicate(-ation), communion, (contri-)distribution, fellowship.

κοινωνικός.shortDef: from κοινωνός; communicative, i.e. (pecuniarily) liberal:--willing to communicate.

κοινωνός.shortDef: from κοινός; a sharer, i.e. associate:--companion, X fellowship, partaker, partner.

κοίτη.shortDef: from κεῖμαι; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm:--bed, chambering, X conceive.

glosses: from κόκκος (from the kernel-shape of the insect)
κόκκινος.shortDef: from κόκκος (from the kernel-shape of the insect); crimson-colored:--scarlet (colour, coloured).

κόκκος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed:--corn, grain.

κολάζω.shortDef: from  (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction):--punish.

κολακεία.shortDef: from a derivative of  (a fawner); flattery:-- X flattering.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of κολάζω
κολαφίζω.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of κολάζω; to rap with the fist:--buffet.

κολλάω.shortDef: from  ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively):--cleave, join (self), keep company.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a cake
κολλούριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a cake; prob akin to the base of κολλάω); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster:-- eyesalve.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of  (a small coin
κολλυβιστής.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of  (a small coin; probably akin to κολλούριον); a coin-dealer:--(money-)changer.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of κολάζω
κολοβόω.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of κολάζω; to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge:--shorten.

κολοσσαί.shortDef: apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossæ, a place in Asia Minor:--Colosse.

κολοσσαεύς.shortDef: from Κολοσσαί; a Colossæan, (i.e. inhabitant of Colossæ:--Colossian.

κόλπος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay:--bosom, creek.

κολυμβάω.shortDef: from  (a diver); to plunge into water:--swim.

κολυμβήθρα.shortDef: from κολυμβάω; a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming):--pool.

κολωνία.shortDef: of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans:--colony.

κομάω.shortDef: from κόμη; to wear tresses of hair:--have long hair.

glosses: apparently from the same as κομίζω
κόμη.shortDef: apparently from the same as κομίζω; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from θρίξ; which properly denotes merely the scalp):--hair.

κομίζω.shortDef: from a primary  (to tend, i.e. take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain):--bring, receive.

glosses: neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning
κομψότερον.shortDef: neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. nice); figuratively, convalescent:--+ began to amend.

κονιάω.shortDef: from  (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash:--whiten.

glosses: from the base of κονιάω and ornumi (to "rouse")
κονιορτός.shortDef: from the base of κονιάω and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about):--dust.

κοπάζω.shortDef: from κόπος; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax:--cease.

κοπετός.shortDef: from κόπτω; mourning (properly, by beating the breast):--lamentation.

κοπιάω.shortDef: from a derivative of κόπος; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard:--(bestow) labour, toil, be wearied.

κόπος.shortDef: from κόπτω; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains:--labour, + trouble, weariness.

κοπρία.shortDef: from  (ordure; perhaps akin to κόπτω); manure:--dung(-hill).

κόπτω.shortDef: a primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief:--cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of τομώτερος.

κόραξ.shortDef: perhaps from κορέννυμι; a crow (from its voracity):--raven.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a maiden)
κοράσιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a maiden); a (little) girl:--damsel, maid.

glosses: of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (קׇרְבָּן)
κορβᾶν.shortDef: of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (קׇרְבָּן); a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where the contribution boxes stood:--Corban, treasury.

κορέ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (קֹרַח); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite:--Core.

κορέννυμι.shortDef: a primary verb; to cram, i.e. glut or sate:--eat enough, full.

κορίνθιος.shortDef: from Κόρινθος; a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth:--Corinthian.

κόρινθος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece:--Corinth.

κορνήλιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman:--Cornelius.

κόρος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (כֹּר); a cor, i.e. a specific measure:--measure.

κοσμέω.shortDef: from κόσμος; to put in proper order, i.e. decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick):--adorn, garnish, trim.

κοσμικός.shortDef: from κόσμος (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt):--worldly.

κόσμιος.shortDef: from κόσμος (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. decorous:--of good behaviour, modest.

κοσμοκράτωρ.shortDef: from κόσμος and κρατέω; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan:--ruler.

glosses: probably from the base of κομίζω
κόσμος.shortDef: probably from the base of κομίζω; orderly arrangement, i.e. decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)):--adorning, world.

κούαρτος.shortDef: of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian:--Quartus.

κουστωδία.shortDef: of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry:--watch.

κράββατος.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; a mattress:--bed.

κράζω.shortDef: a primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat):--cry (out).

glosses: probably from the same as ἁρπάζω
κραιπάλη.shortDef: probably from the same as ἁρπάζω; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut):--surfeiting.

glosses: diminutive of a derivative of the base of κέρας
κρανίον.shortDef: diminutive of a derivative of the base of κέρας; a skull ("cranium"):--Calvary, skull.

κράσπεδον.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel:--border, hem.

κραταιόω.shortDef: from κραταιός; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor:--be strengthened, be (wax) strong.

κρατέω.shortDef: from κράτος; to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or figuratively):--hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by).

glosses: superlative of a derivative of κράτος
κράτιστος.shortDef: superlative of a derivative of κράτος; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable:--most excellent (noble).

κράτος.shortDef: perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively):--dominion, might(-ily), power, strength.

κραυγή.shortDef: from κράζω; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief):--clamour, cry(-ing).

glosses: neuter of an alternate form of κρείττων
κρεῖσσον.shortDef: neuter of an alternate form of κρείττων; (as noun) better, i.e. greater advantage:--better.

glosses: comparative of a derivative of κράτος
κρείττων.shortDef: comparative of a derivative of κράτος; stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. nobler:--best, better.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary verb
κρεμάννυμι.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang:--hang.

κρημνός.shortDef: from κρεμάννυμι; overhanging, i.e. a precipice:--steep place.

κρής.shortDef: from Κρήτη; a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete:--Crete, Cretian.

κρήσκης.shortDef: of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian:--Crescens.

κρήτη.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean:--Crete.

κρίμα.shortDef: from κρίνω; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")):--avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.

κρίνον.shortDef: perhaps a prim word; a lily:--lily.

κρίνω.shortDef: properly, to distinguish, i.e. decide (mentally or judicially); by implication, to try, condemn, punish:--avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.

κρίσπος.shortDef: of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian:--Crispus.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of κριτής
κριτήριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of κριτής; a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal:--to judge, judgment (seat).

κριτής.shortDef: from κρίνω; a judge (genitive case or specially):--judge.

κρούω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to rap:--knock.

κρύπτη.shortDef: feminine of κρυπτός; a hidden place, i.e. cellar ("crypt"):--secret.

κρυπτός.shortDef: from κρύπτω; concealed, i.e. private:--hid(-den), inward(-ly), secret.

κρύπτω.shortDef: a primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering):--hide (self), keep secret, secret(-ly).

κρυσταλλίζω.shortDef: from κρύσταλλος; to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize"):--be clear as crystal.

κρύσταλλος.shortDef: from a derivative of  (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal":--crystal.

κτάομαι.shortDef: a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own):--obtain, possess, provide, purchase.

κτῆμα.shortDef: from κτάομαι; an acquirement, i.e. estate:--possession.

κτῆνος.shortDef: from κτάομαι; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal:--beast.

glosses: probably akin to κτάομαι (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer)
κτίζω.shortDef: probably akin to κτάομαι (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. found (form originally):--create, Creator, make.

κτίσις.shortDef: from κτίζω; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively):--building, creation, creature, ordinance.

κτίσμα.shortDef: from κτίζω; an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created thing):--creature.

κτίστης.shortDef: from κτίζω; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things):--Creator.

κυβεία.shortDef: from  (a "cube", i.e. die for playing); gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud:--sleight.

κυβέρνησις.shortDef: from  (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church):--government.

κυβερνήτης.shortDef: from the same as κυβέρνησις; helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain:--(ship) master.

glosses: adverb from the same as κύκλῳ
κυκλόθεν.shortDef: adverb from the same as κύκλῳ; from the circle, i.e. all around:--(round) about.

κυκλόω.shortDef: from the same as κύκλῳ; to encircle, i.e. surround:--compass (about), come (stand) round about.

glosses: as if dative case of  (a ring
κύκλῳ.shortDef: as if dative case of  (a ring, "cycle"; akin to κυλιόω); i.e. in a circle (by implication, of ἐν), i.e. (adverbially) all around:--round about.

κύλισμα.shortDef: from κυλιόω; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth:--wallowing.

glosses: from the base of κῦμα (through the idea of circularity
κυλιόω.shortDef: from the base of κῦμα (through the idea of circularity; compare κύκλῳ, εἱλίσσω); to roll about:--wallow.

κυλλός.shortDef: from the same as κυλιόω; rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands):--maimed.

κῦμα.shortDef: from  (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling):--wave.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of κῦμα
κύμβαλον.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of κῦμα; a "cymbal" (as hollow):--cymbal.

κύμινον.shortDef: of foreign origin (compare כַּמֹּן); dill or fennel ("cummin"):--cummin.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of κύων
κυνάριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of κύων; a puppy:--dog.

κύπριος.shortDef: from Κύπρος; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus:--of Cyprus.

κύπρος.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cyprus.

glosses: probably from the base of κῦμα
κύπτω.shortDef: probably from the base of κῦμα; to bend forward:--stoop (down).

κυρηναῖος.shortDef: from Κυρήνη; i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene:--of Cyrene, Cyrenian.

κυρήνη.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa:--Cyrene.

κυρήνιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman:--Cyrenius.

κυρία.shortDef: feminine of κύριος; Cyria, a Christian woman:--lady.

κυριακός.shortDef: from κύριος; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus):--Lord's.

κυριεύω.shortDef: from κύριος; to rule:--have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over.

κύριος.shortDef: from  (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title):-- God, Lord, master, Sir.

κυριότης.shortDef: from κύριος; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers:--dominion, government.

κυρόω.shortDef: from the same as κύριος; to make authoritative, i.e. ratify:--confirm.

κύων.shortDef: a primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively):--dog.

κῶλον.shortDef: from the base of κολάζω; a limb of the body (as if lopped):--carcase.

κωλύω.shortDef: from the base of κολάζω; to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or act):--forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.

κώμη.shortDef: from κεῖμαι; a hamlet (as if laid down):--town, village.

κωμόπολις.shortDef: from κώμη and πόλις; an unwalled city:--town.

κῶμος.shortDef: from κεῖμαι; a carousal (as if letting loose):--revelling, rioting.

glosses: apparently a derivative of the base of κέντρον and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι
κώνωψ.shortDef: apparently a derivative of the base of κέντρον and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis):--gnat.

κώς.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cos.

κωσάμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (compare קֶסֶם); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite:--Cosam.

κωφός.shortDef: from κόπτω; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb):--deaf, dumb, speechless.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary verb
λαγχάνω.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot:--his lot be, cast lots, obtain.

λάζαρος.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin (אֶלְעָזָר); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary):--Lazarus.

λαῖλαψ.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall):--storm, tempest.

glosses: a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb
λαλέω.shortDef: a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. utter words:--preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare λέγω.

glosses: of Hebrew origin (מָה with prepositional prefix)
λαμά.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מָה with prepositional prefix); lama (i.e. why):--lama.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary verb
λαμβάνω.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas δέχομαι is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while αἱρέομαι is more violent, to seize or remove)):--accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).

λάμεχ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (לֶמֶךְ); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch:--Lamech.

λαμπάς.shortDef: from λάμπω; a "lamp" or flambeau:--lamp, light, torch.

λαμπρός.shortDef: from the same as λαμπάς; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance):--bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white.

λαμπρῶς.shortDef: adverb from λαμπρός; brilliantly, i.e. figuratively, luxuriously:--sumptuously.

λάμπω.shortDef: a primary verb; to beam, i.e. radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively):--give light, shine.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary verb
λανθάνω.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly:--be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.

glosses: from a compound of  (a stone) and the base of ξηρός (in its original sense of scraping)
λαξευτός.shortDef: from a compound of  (a stone) and the base of ξηρός (in its original sense of scraping); rock-quarried:--hewn in stone.

λαός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from δῆμος, which denotes one's own populace):--people.

glosses: from a compound of λαός and δίκη
λαοδίκεια.shortDef: from a compound of λαός and δίκη; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor:--Laodicea.

λαοδικεύς.shortDef: from Λαοδίκεια; a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia:--Laodicean.

λασαία.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Lasæa, a place in Crete:--Lasea.

glosses: a strengthened form of a primary verb
λάσχω.shortDef: a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall):--burst asunder.

glosses: from the same as the first part of λαξευτός and the base of τομώτερος
λατομέω.shortDef: from the same as the first part of λαξευτός and the base of τομώτερος; to quarry:--hew.

λατρεία.shortDef: from λατρεύω; ministration of God, i.e. worship:--(divine) service.

λατρεύω.shortDef: from  (a hired menial); to minister (to God), i.e. render religious homage:--serve, do the service, worship(-per).

λεββαῖος.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Lebbæus, a Christian:--Lebbæus.

λεγεών.shortDef: of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively):--legion.

λέγω.shortDef: a primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas ἔπω and φημί generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while ῥέω is properly to break silence merely, and λαλέω means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean:--ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter.

λεῖος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; smooth, i.e. "level":--smooth.

λείπω.shortDef: a primary verb; to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail or be absent:--be destitute (wanting), lack.

λειτουργέω.shortDef: from λειτουργός; to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve):--minister.

λειτουργία.shortDef: from λειτουργέω; public function (as priest ("liturgy") or almsgiver):--ministration(-try), service.

λειτουργικός.shortDef: from the same as λειτουργέω; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. beneficient:--ministering.

glosses: from a derivative of λαός and ἔργον
λειτουργός.shortDef: from a derivative of λαός and ἔργον; a public servant, i.e. a functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man):--minister(-ed).

λέντιον.shortDef: of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. apron:--towel.

λέπρα.shortDef: from the same as λεπίς; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy":--leprosy.

λεπρός.shortDef: from the same as λέπρα; scaly, i.e. leprous (a leper):--leper.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of the same as λεπίς
λεπτόν.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of the same as λεπίς; something scaled (light), i.e. a small coin:--mite.

λευΐ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (לֵוִי); Levi, the name of three Israelites:--Levi. Compare Λευΐς.

λευΐς.shortDef: a form of Λευΐ; Lewis (i.e. Levi), a Christian:--Levi.

λευΐτης.shortDef: from Λευΐ; a Levite, i.e. descendant of Levi:--Levite.

λευϊτικός.shortDef: from Λευΐτης; Levitic, i.e. relating to the Levites:--Levitical.

λευκαίνω.shortDef: from λευκός; to whiten:--make white, whiten.

ληνός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a trough, i.e. wine-vat:--winepress.

λῆρος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. an incredible story:--idle tale.

λίαν.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; much (adverbially):--exceeding, great(-ly), sore, very (+ chiefest).

λίβανος.shortDef: of foreign origin (לְבוֹנָה); the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself:--frankincense.

λιβανωτός.shortDef: from λίβανος; frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it:--censer.

λιβερτῖνος.shortDef: of Latin origin; a Roman freedman:--Libertine.

λιβύη.shortDef: probably from λίψ; Libye, a region of Africa:--Libya.

λίθινος.shortDef: from λίθος; stony, i.e. made of stone:--of stone.

glosses: from a compound of λίθος and βάλλω
λιθοβολέω.shortDef: from a compound of λίθος and βάλλω; to throw stones, i.e. lapidate:--stone, cast stones.

λίθος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively):--(mill-, stumbling-)stone.

glosses: from λίθος and a derivative of στρώννυμι
λιθόστρωτος.shortDef: from λίθος and a derivative of στρώννυμι; stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed:--Pavement.

λικμάω.shortDef: from , the equivalent of  (a winnowing fan or basket); to winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate:--grind to powder.

λιμήν.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a harbor:--haven. Compare Καλοὶ Λιμένες.

glosses: probably from λιμήν (through the idea of nearness of shore)
λίμνη.shortDef: probably from λιμήν (through the idea of nearness of shore); a pond (large or small):--lake.

glosses: probably from λείπω (through the idea of destitution)
λιμός.shortDef: probably from λείπω (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food:--dearth, famine, hunger.

λίνον.shortDef: probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen":--linen.

λίνος.shortDef: perhaps from λίνον; Linus, a Christian:--Linus.

λίτρα.shortDef: of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight:--pound.

λίψ.shortDef: probably from  (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter):--southwest.

λογία.shortDef: from λόγος (in the commercial sense); a contribution:--collection, gathering.

λογίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from λόγος; to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally or figuratively):--conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).

λογικός.shortDef: from λόγος; rational ("logical"):--reasonable, of the word.

λόγιον.shortDef: neuter of λόγιος; an utterance (of God):--oracle.

λόγιος.shortDef: from λόγος; fluent, i.e. an orator:--eloquent.

λογισμός.shortDef: from λογίζομαι; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit):--imagination, thought.

glosses: from a compound of λόγος and μάχομαι
λογομαχέω.shortDef: from a compound of λόγος and μάχομαι; to be disputatious (on trifles):--strive about words.

λογομαχία.shortDef: from the same as λογομαχέω; disputation about trifles ("logomachy"):--strife of words.

λόγος.shortDef: from λέγω; something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ):--account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work.

λοιδορέω.shortDef: from λοίδορος; to reproach, i.e. vilify:--revile.

λοιδορία.shortDef: from λοίδορος; slander or vituperation:--railing, reproach(-fully).

λοίδορος.shortDef: from  (mischief); abusive, i.e. a blackguard:--railer, reviler.

λοιμός.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally, the disease, or figuratively, a pest):--pestilence(-t).

glosses: masculine plural of a derivative of λείπω
λοιποί.shortDef: masculine plural of a derivative of λείπω; remaining ones:--other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest.

glosses: neuter singular of the same as λοιποί
λοιπόν.shortDef: neuter singular of the same as λοιποί; something remaining (adverbially):--besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then.

glosses: genitive case singular of the same as λοιποί
λοιποῦ.shortDef: genitive case singular of the same as λοιποί; remaining time:--from henceforth.

λουκᾶς.shortDef: contracted from Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian:--Lucas, Luke.

λούκιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian:--Lucius.

λουτρόν.shortDef: from λούω; a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism:--washing.

λούω.shortDef: a primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas νίπτω means to wet a part only, and πλύνω to wash, cleanse garments exclusively):--wash.

λύδδα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (לֹד); Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine:--Lydda.

λυδία.shortDef: properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor); Lydia, a Christian woman:--Lydia.

λυκαονία.shortDef: perhaps remotely from λύκος; Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor:--Lycaonia.

glosses: adverb from a derivative of Λυκαονία
λυκαονιστί.shortDef: adverb from a derivative of Λυκαονία; Lycaonistically, i.e. in the language of the Lycaonians:--in the speech of Lycaonia.

λυκία.shortDef: probably remotely from λύκος; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor:--Lycia.

glosses: perhaps akin to the base of λευκός (from the whitish hair)
λύκος.shortDef: perhaps akin to the base of λευκός (from the whitish hair); a wolf:--wolf.

glosses: middle voice from a probably derivative of λύω (meaning filth)
λυμαίνομαι.shortDef: middle voice from a probably derivative of λύω (meaning filth); properly, to soil, i.e. (figuratively) insult (maltreat):--make havock of.

λυπέω.shortDef: from λύπη; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad:--cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry.

λύπη.shortDef: apparently a primary word; sadness:--grief, grievous, + grudgingly, heaviness, sorrow.

λυσανίας.shortDef: from λύσις and  (trouble); grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene:--Lysanias.

λυσίας.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman:--Lysias.

λύσις.shortDef: from λύω; a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce:--to be loosed.

glosses: third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of λύσις and τέλος
λυσιτελεῖ.shortDef: third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of λύσις and τέλος; impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e. is advantageous:--it is better.

λύστρα.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor:--Lystra.

λύτρον.shortDef: from λύω; something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price (figuratively, atonement):--ransom.

λυτρόω.shortDef: from λύτρον; to ransom (literally or figuratively):--redeem.

λύτρωσις.shortDef: from λυτρόω; a ransoming (figuratively):--+ redeemed, redemption.

λυχνία.shortDef: from λύχνος; a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively):--candlestick.

λύχνος.shortDef: from the base of λευκός; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively):--candle, light.

λύω.shortDef: a primary verb; to "loosen" (literally or figuratively):--break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off. Compare ῥήγνυμι.

λωΐς.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman:--Lois.

λώτ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (לוֹט); Lot, a patriarch:--Lot.

μαάθ.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite:--Maath.

μαγδαλά.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (compare מִגְדָּל); the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine:--Magdala.

glosses: feminine of a derivative of Μαγδαλά
μαγδαληνή.shortDef: feminine of a derivative of Μαγδαλά; a female Magdalene, i.e. inhabitant of Magdala:--Magdalene.

μαγεύω.shortDef: from μάγος; to practice magic:--use sorcery.

μάγος.shortDef: of foreign origin (רַב־מָג); a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician:--sorcerer, wise man.

μαγώγ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מָגוֹג); Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party:--Magog.

μαδιάν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מִדְיָן); Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia:--Madian.

μαθητεύω.shortDef: from μαθητής; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar:--be disciple, instruct, teach.

μαθητής.shortDef: from μανθάνω; a learner, i.e. pupil:--disciple.

μαθήτρια.shortDef: feminine from μαθητής; a female pupil:--disciple.

μαθουσάλα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מְתוּשֶׁלַח); Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an antediluvian:--Mathusala.

μαϊνάν.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin; Mainan, an Israelite:--Mainan.

glosses: middle voice from a primary  (to long for
μαίνομαι.shortDef: middle voice from a primary  (to long for; through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac":--be beside self (mad).

μακαρίζω.shortDef: from μακάριος; to beatify, i.e. pronounce (or esteem) fortunate:--call blessed, count happy.

glosses: a prolonged form of the poetical  (meaning the same)
μακάριος.shortDef: a prolonged form of the poetical  (meaning the same); supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off:-- blessed, happy(X -ier).

μακαρισμός.shortDef: from μακαρίζω; beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune:--blessedness.

μακεδονία.shortDef: from Μακεδών; Macedonia, a region of Greece:--Macedonia.

μακεδών.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of Macedonia:--of Macedonia, Macedonian.

μάκελλον.shortDef: of Latin origin (macellum); a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop:--shambles.

glosses: feminine accusative case singular of μακρός (ὁδός being implied)
μακράν.shortDef: feminine accusative case singular of μακρός (ὁδός being implied); at a distance (literally or figuratively):--(a-)far (off), good (great) way off.

μακρόθεν.shortDef: adverb from μακρός; from a distance or afar:--afar off, from far.

μακροθυμέω.shortDef: from the same as μακροθυμώς; to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient:--bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure.

μακροθυμία.shortDef: from the same as μακροθυμώς; longanimity, i.e. (objectively) forbearance or (subjectively) fortitude:--longsuffering, patience.

glosses: adverb of a compound of μακρός and θυμός
μακροθυμώς.shortDef: adverb of a compound of μακρός and θυμός; with long (enduring) temper, i.e. leniently:--patiently.

μακρός.shortDef: from μῆκος; long (in place (distant) or time (neuter plural)):--far, long.

μακροχρόνιος.shortDef: from μακρός and χρόνος; long-timed, i.e. long-lived:--live long.

μαλακός.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; soft, i.e. fine (clothing); figuratively, a catamite:--effeminate, soft.

μαλελεήλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מַהֲלַלְאֵל); Maleleel (i.e. Mahalalel), an antediluvian:--Maleleel.

glosses: neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb  (very)
μάλιστα.shortDef: neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb  (very); (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly:--chiefly, most of all, (e-)specially.

glosses: neuter of the comparative of the same as μάλιστα
μᾶλλον.shortDef: neuter of the comparative of the same as μάλιστα; (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather:--+ better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather.

μάλχος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מֶלֶךְ); Malchus, an Israelite:--Malchus.

μαμμωνᾶς.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. wealth, personified); mammonas, i.e. avarice (deified):--mammon.

μαναήν.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Manaën, a Christian:--Manaen.

μανασσῆς.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מְנַשֶּׁה); Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an Israelite:--Manasses.

μανθάνω.shortDef: prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, , is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn (in any way):--learn, understand.

μανία.shortDef: from μαίνομαι; craziness:--(+ make) X mad.

μάννα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מָן); manna (i.e. man), an edible gum:--manna.

glosses: from a derivative of μαίνομαι (meaning a prophet
μαντεύομαι.shortDef: from a derivative of μαίνομαι (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration); to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of foretelling:--by soothsaying.

μαραίνω.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away:--fade away.

glosses: of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come)
μαρὰν ἀθά.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); maranatha, i.e. an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment:--Maran-atha.

μάρθα.shortDef: probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); Martha, a Christian woman:--Martha.

μαρία.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מִרְיָם); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females:-- Mary.

μάρκος.shortDef: of Latin origin; Marcus, a Christian:--Marcus, Mark.

μαρτυρέω.shortDef: from μάρτυς; to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively):--charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness.

μαρτυρία.shortDef: from μάρτυς; evidence given (judicially or genitive case):--record, report, testimony, witness.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of μάρτυς
μαρτύριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of μάρτυς; something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle):--to be testified, testimony, witness.

μαρτύρομαι.shortDef: middle voice from μάρτυς; to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation):--take to record, testify.

μάρτυς.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr":-- martyr, record, witness.

glosses: from a primary  (to handle or squeeze)
μασσάομαι.shortDef: from a primary  (to handle or squeeze); to chew:--gnaw.

μαστιγόω.shortDef: from μάστιξ; to flog (literally or figuratively):--scourge.

glosses: probably from the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of contact)
μάστιξ.shortDef: probably from the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of contact); a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease):--plague, scourging.

μαστός.shortDef: from the base of μασσάομαι; a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded up):--pap.

ματαιολογία.shortDef: from ματαιολόγος; random talk, i.e. babble:--vain jangling.

ματαιολόγος.shortDef: from μάταιος and λέγω; an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler:--vain talker.

μάταιος.shortDef: from the base of μάτην; empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol:--vain, vanity.

ματαιότης.shortDef: from μάταιος; inutility; figuratively, transientness; morally, depravity:--vanity.

ματαιόω.shortDef: from μάταιος; to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous:--become vain.

glosses: accusative case of a derivative of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of tentative manipulation
μάτην.shortDef: accusative case of a derivative of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose:--in vain.

ματθαῖος.shortDef: a shorter form of Ματταθίας; Matthæus (i.e. Matthitjah), an Israelite and a Christian:--Matthew.

ματθάν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מַתָּן); Matthan (i.e. Mattan), an Israelite:--Matthan.

glosses: probably a shortened form of Ματταθίας
ματθάτ.shortDef: probably a shortened form of Ματταθίας; Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites:--Mathat.

glosses: apparently a shortened form of Ματταθίας
ματθίας.shortDef: apparently a shortened form of Ματταθίας; Matthias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite:--Matthias.

glosses: probably a shortened form of Ματταθίας (compare מַתַּתָּה)
ματταθά.shortDef: probably a shortened form of Ματταθίας (compare מַתַּתָּה); Mattatha (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite:--Mattatha.

ματταθίας.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מַתִּתְיָה); Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite and a Christian:--Mattathias.

glosses: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of μάχη
μάχαιρα.shortDef: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of μάχη; a knife, i.e. dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment:--sword.

μάχη.shortDef: from μάχομαι; a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy:--fighting, strive, striving.

glosses: middle voice of an apparently primary verb
μάχομαι.shortDef: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute:--fight, strive.

glosses: a shorter (and probably original) form of ἐμέ
μέ.shortDef: a shorter (and probably original) form of ἐμέ; me:--I, me, my.

glosses: from a compound of μέγας and  (to boast
μεγαλαυχέω.shortDef: from a compound of μέγας and  (to boast; akin to αὐξάνω and καυχάομαι); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic):--boast great things.

μεγαλεῖος.shortDef: from μέγας; magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection:--great things, wonderful works.

μεγαλειότης.shortDef: from μεγαλεῖος; superbness, i.e. glory or splendor:--magnificence, majesty, mighty power.

μεγαλοπρεπής.shortDef: from μέγας and πρέπω; befitting greatness or magnificence (majestic):--excellent.

μεγαλύνω.shortDef: from μέγας; to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol:--enlarge, magnify, shew great.

μεγαλωσύνη.shortDef: from μέγας; greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God himself):--majesty.

μέγας.shortDef: (including the prolonged forms, feminine , plural , etc.; compare also μέγιστος, μείζων); big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application):--(+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years.

μεγιστᾶνες.shortDef: plural from μέγιστος; grandees:--great men, lords.

μέγιστος.shortDef: superlative of μέγας; greatest or very great:--exceeding great.

μεθερμηνεύω.shortDef: from μετά and ἑρμηνεύω; to explain over, i.e. translate:--(by) interpret(-ation).

μέθη.shortDef: apparently a primary word; an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication) intoxication:--drunkenness.

μεθίστημι.shortDef: from μετά and ἵστημι; to transfer, i.e. carry away, depose or (figuratively) exchange, seduce:--put out, remove, translate, turn away.

glosses: from a compound of μετά and ὁδεύω (compare "method")
μεθοδεία.shortDef: from a compound of μετά and ὁδεύω (compare "method"); travelling over, i.e. travesty (trickery):--wile, lie in wait.

μεθόριος.shortDef: from μετά and ὅριον; bounded alongside, i.e. contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier):--border.

μεθύσκω.shortDef: a prolonged (transitive) form of μεθύω; to intoxicate:--be drunk(-en).

μέθυσος.shortDef: from μεθύω; tipsy, i.e. (as noun) a sot:--drunkard.

μεθύω.shortDef: from another form of μέθη; to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk:--drink well, make (be) drunk(-en).

μεῖζον.shortDef: neuter of μείζων; (adverbially) in greater degree:--the more.

μειζότερος.shortDef: continued comparative of μείζων; still larger (figuratively):--greater.

μείζων.shortDef: irregular comparative of μέγας; larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age):--elder, greater(-est), more.

μέλαν.shortDef: neuter of μέλας as noun; ink:--ink.

μελεᾶς.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Meleas, an Israelite:--Meleas.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of μέλω
μελετάω.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of μέλω; to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind:--imagine, (pre-)meditate.

μελίσσιος.shortDef: from μέλι; relating to honey, i.e. bee (comb):--honeycomb.

μελίτη.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean:--Melita.

glosses: a strengthened form of μέλω (through the idea of expectation)
μέλλω.shortDef: a strengthened form of μέλω (through the idea of expectation); to intend, i.e. be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation):--about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend, was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry, which was for, will, would, be yet.

μέλος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a limb or part of the body:--member.

glosses: of Hebrew origin (מֶלֶךְ with pronominal suffix
μελχί.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מֶלֶךְ with pronominal suffix, my king); Melchi (i.e. Malki), the name of two Israelites:--Melchi.

μελχισεδέκ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch:--Melchisedec.

μέλω.shortDef: a primary verb; to be of interest to, i.e. to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters):--(take) care.

glosses: middle voice of an apparently primary verb
μέμφομαι.shortDef: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame:--find fault.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of μέμφομαι and  (fate
μεμψίμοιρος.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of μέμφομαι and  (fate; akin to the base of μέρος); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented):--complainer.

μέν.shortDef: a primary particle; properly, indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with δέ (this one, the former, etc.):--even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily. Often compounded with other particles in an intensive or asseverative sense.

glosses: from μέν and οὖν and γέ
μενοῦνγε.shortDef: from μέν and οὖν and γέ; so then at least:--nay but, yea doubtless (rather, verily).

μέντοι.shortDef: from μέν and τοί; indeed though, i.e. however:--also, but, howbeit, nevertheless, yet.

μένω.shortDef: a primary verb; to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy):--abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own.

μερίζω.shortDef: from μέρος; to part, i.e. (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or (figuratively) to disunite, differ:--deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give participle

glosses: from μερίζω (through the idea of distraction)
μέριμνα.shortDef: from μερίζω (through the idea of distraction); solicitude:--care.

μεριμνάω.shortDef: from μέριμνα; to be anxious about:--(be, have) care(-ful), take thought.

μερίς.shortDef: feminine of μέρος; a portion, i.e. province, share or (abstractly) participation:--part (X -akers).

μερισμός.shortDef: from μερίζω; a separation or distribution:--dividing asunder, gift.

glosses: from an obsolete but more primary form of  (to get as a section or allotment)
μέρος.shortDef: from an obsolete but more primary form of  (to get as a section or allotment); a division or share (literally or figuratively, in a wide application):--behalf, course, coast, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort(-what).

μεσημβρία.shortDef: from μέσος and ἡμέρα; midday; by implication, the south:--noon, south.

μεσιτεύω.shortDef: from μεσίτης; to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety):--confirm.

μεσίτης.shortDef: from μέσος; a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor):--mediator.

glosses: neuter of compound of μέσος and νύξ
μεσονύκτιον.shortDef: neuter of compound of μέσος and νύξ; midnight (especially as a watch):--midnight.

μεσοποταμία.shortDef: from μέσος and ποταμός; Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם), a region of Asia:--Mesopotamia.

μέσος.shortDef: from μετά; middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun):--among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way.

μεσότοιχον.shortDef: from μέσος and τοῖχος; a partition (figuratively):--middle wall.

glosses: from a presumed compound of μέσος and οὐρανός
μεσουράνημα.shortDef: from a presumed compound of μέσος and οὐρανός; mid-sky:--midst of heaven.

μεσόω.shortDef: from μέσος; to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way over:--be about the midst.

μεσσίας.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מָשִׁיחַ); the Messias (i.e. Mashiach), or Christ:--Messias.

μεστός.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; replete (literally or figuratively):--full.

μεστόω.shortDef: from μεστός; to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate:--fill.

μετά.shortDef: a primary preposition (often used adverbially); properly, denoting accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according to the case (genitive association, or accusative succession) with which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between ἀπό or ἐκ and εἰς or πρός; less intimate than ἐν and less close than σύν):--after(-ward), X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-)on, + our, X and setting, since, (un-)to, + together, when, with (+ -out). Often used in composition, in substantially the same relations of participation or proximity, and transfer or sequence.

glosses: from μετά and the base of βάσις
μεταβαίνω.shortDef: from μετά and the base of βάσις; to change place:--depart, go, pass, remove.

μεταβάλλω.shortDef: from μετά and βάλλω; to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion:--change mind.

μετάγω.shortDef: from μετά and ἁρμόζω; to lead over, i.e. transfer (direct):--turn about.

μεταδίδωμι.shortDef: from μετά and δίδωμι; to give over, i.e. share:--give, impart.

μετάθεσις.shortDef: from μετατίθημι; transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law):--change, removing, translation.

μεταίρω.shortDef: from μετά and αἴρω; to betake oneself, i.e. remove (locally):--depart.

μετακαλέω.shortDef: from μετά and καλέω; to call elsewhere, i.e. summon:--call (for, hither).

μετακινέω.shortDef: from μετά and κινέω; to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove (figuratively):--move away.

μεταλαμβάνω.shortDef: from μετά and λαμβάνω; to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use):--eat, have, be partaker, receive, take.

μεταλλάσσω.shortDef: from μετά and ἀλλάσσω; to exchange:--change.

glosses: from μετά and the middle voice of μέλω
μεταμέλλομαι.shortDef: from μετά and the middle voice of μέλω; to care afterwards, i.e. regret:--repent (self).

μεταμορφόω.shortDef: from μετά and μορφόω; to transform (literally or figuratively, "metamorphose"):--change, transfigure, transform.

μετανοέω.shortDef: from μετά and νοιέω; to think differently or afterwards, i.e. reconsider (morally, feel compunction):--repent.

μετάνοια.shortDef: from μετανοέω; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's) decision):--repentance.

glosses: from μετά and a form of σύν
μεταξύ.shortDef: from μετά and a form of σύν; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining:--between, mean while, next.

μεταπέμπω.shortDef: from μετά and πέμπω; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite:--call (send) for.

μεταστρέφω.shortDef: from μετά and στρέφω; to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively) corrupt:--pervert, turn.

glosses: from μετά and a derivative of σχῆμα
