μετασχηματίζω.shortDef: from μετά and a derivative of σχῆμα; to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation):--transfer, transform (self).

μετατίθημι.shortDef: from μετά and τίθημι; to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert:--carry over, change, remove, translate, turn.

μετέχω.shortDef: from μετά and ἔχω; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink):--be partaker, pertain, take part, use.

glosses: from a compound of μετά and a collateral form of αἴρω or perhaps rather ἀήρ (compare "meteor")
μετεωρίζω.shortDef: from a compound of μετά and a collateral form of αἴρω or perhaps rather ἀήρ (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious):--be of doubtful mind.

glosses: from a derivative of a compound of μετά and οἶκος
μετοικεσία.shortDef: from a derivative of a compound of μετά and οἶκος; a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation:--X brought, carried(-ying) away (in-)to.

μετοικίζω.shortDef: from the same as μετοικεσία; to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile:--carry away, remove into.

μέτοχος.shortDef: from μετέχω; participant, i.e. (as noun) a sharer; by implication, an associate:--fellow, partaker, partner.

μετρέω.shortDef: from μέτρον; to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule):--figuratively, to estimate:--measure, mete.

μετρητής.shortDef: from μετρέω; a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids:--firkin.

glosses: from a compound of the base of μετρίως and πάθος
μετριοπαθέω.shortDef: from a compound of the base of μετρίως and πάθος; to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently):--have compassion.

glosses: adverb from a derivative of μέτρον
μετρίως.shortDef: adverb from a derivative of μέτρον; moderately, i.e. slightly:--a little.

μέτρον.shortDef: an apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree):-- measure.

μέτωπον.shortDef: from μετά and ops (the face); the forehead (as opposite the countenance):--forehead.

μέχρι.shortDef: from μῆκος; as far as, i.e. up to a certain point (as a preposition, of extent (denoting the terminus, whereas ἄχρι refers especially to the space of time or place intervening) or conjunction):--till, (un-)to, until.

glosses: a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas οὐ expresses an absolute denial)
μή.shortDef: a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas οὐ expresses an absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas οὐ expects an affirmative one)) whether:--any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without. Often used in compounds in substantially the same relations. See also ἐὰν μή, ἵνα μή, οὐ μή, μῆκος, μηκύνω, μήν, μὴ οὐκ.

ἐὰν μή.shortDef: i.e. ἐάν and μή; if not, i.e. unless:--X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not.

ἵνα μή.shortDef: i.e. ἵνα and μή; in order (or so) that not:--albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing)).

οὐ μή.shortDef: i.e. οὐ and μή; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all:--any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare μὴ οὐκ.

glosses: adverb from a compound of μή and  (somebody)
μηδαμῶς.shortDef: adverb from a compound of μή and  (somebody); by no means:--not so.

μηδέ.shortDef: from μή and δέ; but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor:--neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as).

μηδείς.shortDef: from μή and εἷς; not even one (man, woman, thing):--any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay.

μηδέποτε.shortDef: from μηδέ and ποτέ; not even ever:--never.

μηδέπω.shortDef: from μηδέ and -πω; not even yet:--not yet.

μῆδος.shortDef: of foreign origin (compare מָדַי); a Median, or inhabitant of Media:--Mede.

μηκέτι.shortDef: from μή and ἔτι; no further:--any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more.

μῆκος.shortDef: probably akin to μέγας; length (literally or figuratively) length.

μηκύνω.shortDef: from μῆκος; to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge:--grow up.

glosses: probably from the same base as μασσάομαι and μνάομαι (i.e.
μηνύω.shortDef: probably from the same base as μασσάομαι and μνάομαι (i.e. , to strive); to disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind), i.e. report, declare, intimate:--shew, tell.

μὴ οὐκ.shortDef: i.e. μή and οὐ; as interrogative and negative, is it not that?:--neither (followed by no), + never, not. Compare οὐ μή.

μήποτε.shortDef: from μή and ποτέ; not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps):--if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not.

μήπω.shortDef: from μή and -πω; not yet:--not yet.

μήπως.shortDef: from μή and -πώς; lest somehow:--lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps).

μηρός.shortDef: perhaps a primary word; a thigh:--thigh.

μήτε.shortDef: from μή and τέ; not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even:--neither, (n-)or, so as much.

μήτηρ.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote):--mother.

glosses: from μή and the neuter of τὶς
μήτι.shortDef: from μή and the neuter of τὶς; whether at all:--not (the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question).

μήτιγε.shortDef: from μήτι and γέ; not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still):--how much more.

μήτις.shortDef: from μή and τὶς; whether any:--any (sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence).

glosses: from μήτηρ and the base of ἅλων
μητραλῴας.shortDef: from μήτηρ and the base of ἅλων; a mother-thresher, i.e. matricide:--murderer of mothers.

μητρόπολις.shortDef: from μήτηρ and πόλις; a mother city, i.e. "metropolis":--chiefest city.

μία.shortDef: irregular feminine of εἷς; one or first:--a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other.

μιαίνω.shortDef: perhaps a primary verb; to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate (ceremonially or morally):--defile.

glosses: masculine or neuter singular of μικρός (as noun)
μικρόν.shortDef: masculine or neuter singular of μικρός (as noun); a small space of time or degree:--a (little) (while).

μικρός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; small (in size, quantity, number or (figuratively) dignity):--least, less, little, small.

μίλητος.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Miletus, a city of Asia Minor:--Miletus.

μίλιον.shortDef: of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile":--mile.

glosses: a prolonged form of μνάομαι (from which some of the tenses are borrowed)
μιμνήσκω.shortDef: a prolonged form of μνάομαι (from which some of the tenses are borrowed); to remind, i.e. (middle voice) to recall to mind:--be mindful, remember.

μισέω.shortDef: from a primary  (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by extension, to love less:--hate(-ful).

μισθαποδοσία.shortDef: from μισθαποδότης; requital (good or bad):--recompence of reward.

μισθαποδότης.shortDef: from μισθόω and ἀποδίδωμι; a renumerator:--rewarder.

μισθός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad:--hire, reward, wages.

μισθόω.shortDef: from μισθός; to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire:--hire.

μίσθωμα.shortDef: from μισθόω; a rented building:--hired house.

μισθωτός.shortDef: from μισθόω; a wage-worker (good or bad):--hired servant, hireling.

μιτυλήνη.shortDef: for  (abounding in shellfish); Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos:--Mitylene.

μιχαήλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מִיכָאֵל); Michael, an archangel:--Michael.

μνᾶ.shortDef: of Latin origin; a mna (i.e. mina), a certain weight:-- pound.

glosses: middle voice of a derivative of μένω or perhaps of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp)
μνάομαι.shortDef: middle voice of a derivative of μένω or perhaps of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); to bear in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish:--be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance. Compare μιμνήσκω.

μνάσων.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Mnason, a Christian:--Mnason.

μνεία.shortDef: from μνάομαι or μιμνήσκω; recollection; by implication, recital:--mention, remembrance.

μνῆμα.shortDef: from μνάομαι; a memorial, i.e. sepulchral monument (burial-place):--grave, sepulchre, tomb.

μνημεῖον.shortDef: from μνήμη; a remembrance, i.e. cenotaph (place of interment):--grave, sepulchre, tomb.

μνημονεύω.shortDef: from a derivative of μνήμη; to exercise memory, i.e. recollect; by implication, to punish; also to rehearse:--make mention; be mindful, remember.

μνημόσυνον.shortDef: from μνημονεύω; a reminder (memorandum), i.e. record:--memorial.

μνηστεύω.shortDef: from a derivative of μνάομαι; to give a souvenir (engagement present), i.e. betroth:--espouse.

μογιλάλος.shortDef: from μόγις and λαλέω; hardly talking, i.e. dumb (tongue-tied):--having an impediment in his speech.

μόγις.shortDef: adverb from a primary  (toil); with difficulty:--hardly.

μόδιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil):--bushel.

μοί.shortDef: the simpler form of ἐμοί; to me:--I, me, mine, my.

glosses: a prolonged form of the feminine of μοιχός
μοιχαλίς.shortDef: a prolonged form of the feminine of μοιχός; an adulteress (literally or figuratively):--adulteress(-ous, -y).

μοιχάω.shortDef: from μοιχός; (middle voice) to commit adultery:--commit adultery.

μοιχεύω.shortDef: from μοιχός; to commit adultery:--commit adultery.

μοιχός.shortDef: perhaps a primary word; a (male) paramour; figuratively, apostate:--adulterer.

μόλις.shortDef: probably by variation for μόγις; with difficulty:--hardly, scarce(-ly), + with much work.

μολόχ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (מֹלֶךְ); Moloch (i.e. Molek), an idol:--Moloch.

μολυσμός.shortDef: from μολύνω; a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality:--filthiness.

μομφή.shortDef: from μέμφομαι; blame, i.e. (by implication), a fault:--quarrel.

μονή.shortDef: from μένω; a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place):--abode, mansion.

μονογενής.shortDef: from μόνος and γίνομαι; only-born, i.e. sole:--only (begotten, child).

μόνον.shortDef: neuter of μόνος as adverb; merely:--alone, but, only.

μόνος.shortDef: probably from μένω; remaining, i.e. sole or single; by implication, mere:--alone, only, by themselves.

μονόφθαλμος.shortDef: from μόνος and ὀφθαλμός; one-eyed:--with one eye.

μονόω.shortDef: from μόνος; to isolate, i.e. bereave:--be desolate.

glosses: perhaps from the base of μέρος (through the idea of adjustment of parts)
μορφή.shortDef: perhaps from the base of μέρος (through the idea of adjustment of parts); shape; figuratively, nature:--form.

μορφόω.shortDef: from the same as μορφή; to fashion (figuratively):--form.

μόρφωσις.shortDef: from μορφόω; formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or (concretely) formula):--form.

μοσχοποιέω.shortDef: from μόσχος and ποιέω; to fabricate the image of a bullock:--make a calf.

μόσχος.shortDef: probably strengthened for  (a shoot); a young bullock:--calf.

μόχθος.shortDef: from the base of μόγις; toil, i.e. (by implication) sadness:--painfulness, travail.

μοῦ.shortDef: the simpler form of ἐμοῦ; of me:--I, me, mine (own), my.

μουσικός.shortDef: from  (a Muse); "musical", i.e. (as noun) a minstrel:--musician.

μυελός.shortDef: perhaps a primary word; the marrow:--marrow.

μυέω.shortDef: from the base of μυστήριον; to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach:--instruct.

glosses: perhaps from the same as μυέω (through the idea of tuition)
μῦθος.shortDef: perhaps from the same as μυέω (through the idea of tuition); a tale, i.e. fiction ("myth"):--fable.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of  ( to "moo")
μυκάομαι.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of  ( to "moo"); to bellow (roar):--roar.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of μυκάομαι (meaning snout
μυκτηρίζω.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of μυκάομαι (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds); to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule:--mock.

μυλικός.shortDef: from μύλος; belonging to a mill:--mill(-stone).

glosses: probably ultimately from the base of μόλις (through the idea of hardship)
μύλος.shortDef: probably ultimately from the base of μόλις (through the idea of hardship); a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder (millstone):--millstone.

μύρα.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor:--Myra.

μυριάς.shortDef: from μύριοι; a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite number:--ten thousand.

μυρίζω.shortDef: from μύρον; to apply (perfumed) unguent to:--anoint.

glosses: plural of an apparently primary word (properly
μύριοι.shortDef: plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many); ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many:--ten thousand.

μύρον.shortDef: probably of foreign origin (compare מֹר, σμύρνα); "myrrh", i.e. (by implication) perfumed oil:--ointment.

μυσία.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor:--Mysia.

glosses: from a derivative of  (to shut the mouth)
μυστήριον.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to shut the mouth); a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites):--mystery.

glosses: from a compound of the base of μυστήριον and  (the face
μυωπάζω.shortDef: from a compound of the base of μυστήριον and  (the face; from ὀπτάνομαι); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly):-- cannot see far off.

μώλωψ.shortDef: from  ("moil"; probably akin to the base of μόλις) and probably  (the face; from ὀπτάνομαι); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark:--stripe.

μωμάομαι.shortDef: from μῶμος; to carp at, i.e. censure (discredit):--blame.

μῶμος.shortDef: perhaps from μέμφομαι; a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person:--blemish.

μωραίνω.shortDef: from μωρός; to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act) as a simpleton:--become fool, make foolish, lose savour.

glosses: from a compound of μωρός and λέγω
μωρολογία.shortDef: from a compound of μωρός and λέγω; silly talk, i.e. buffoonery:--foolish talking.

glosses: probably from the base of μυστήριον
μωρός.shortDef: probably from the base of μυστήριον; dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e. heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd:--fool(-ish, X -ishness).

μωσεύς.shortDef: of Hebrew  origin; (מֹשֶׁה); Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver:--Moses.

ναασσών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נַחְשׁוֹן); Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an Israelite:--Naasson.

ναγγαί.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin (compare נֹגַהּ); Nangæ (i.e. perhaps Nogach), an Israelite:--Nagge.

ναζαρέθ.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine:--Nazareth.

ναζαρηνός.shortDef: from Ναζαρέθ; a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth:--of Nazareth.

ναζωραῖος.shortDef: from Ναζαρέθ; a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian:--Nazarene, of Nazareth.

ναθάν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נָתָן); Nathan, an Israelite:--Nathan.

ναθαναήλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נְתַנְאֵל); Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian:--Nathanael.

glosses: a primary particle of strong affirmation
ναί.shortDef: a primary particle of strong affirmation; yes:--even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes.

ναΐν.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin (compare נָאָה); Nain, a place in Palestine:--Nain.

ναός.shortDef: from a primary  (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple :--shrine, temple. Compare ἱερόν.

ναούμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נַחוּם); Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite:--Naum.

glosses: a flower of the same name
νάρκισσος.shortDef: a flower of the same name, from  (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman:--Narcissus.

glosses: from a compound of ναῦς and ἄγω
ναυαγέω.shortDef: from a compound of ναῦς and ἄγω; to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively:--make (suffer) shipwreck.

ναύκληρος.shortDef: from ναῦς and κλῆρος ("clerk"); a captain:--owner of a ship.

ναῦς.shortDef: from  or  (to float); a boat (of any size):--ship.

ναύτης.shortDef: from ναῦς; a boatman, i.e. seaman:--sailor, shipman.

ναχώρ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נָחוֹר); Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham:--Nachor.

νεανίας.shortDef: from a derivative of νέος; a youth (up to about forty years):--young man.

νεανίσκος.shortDef: from the same as νεανίας; a youth (under forty):--young man.

νεάπολις.shortDef: from νέος and πόλις; new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia:--Neapolis.

νεεμάν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נַעֲמָן); Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian:--Naaman.

νεκρός.shortDef: from an apparently primary  (a corpse); dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun):--dead.

νεκρόω.shortDef: from νεκρός; to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue:--be dead, mortify.

νέκρωσις.shortDef: from νεκρόω; decease; figuratively, impotency:--deadness, dying.

νέος.shortDef: including the comparative  ; a primary word; "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate:--new, young.

glosses: from νέος and a derivative of φύω
νεόφυτος.shortDef: from νέος and a derivative of φύω; newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"):--novice.

νέρων.shortDef: of Latin origin; Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor:--Nero.

νεύω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to "nod", i.e. (by analogy), signal:--beckon.

νεφέλη.shortDef: from νέφος; properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud:--cloud.

νεφθαλείμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נַפְתָּלִי); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine:--Nephthalim.

νέφος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a cloud:--cloud.

νεφρός.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind:--reins.

glosses: from a form of ναός and  (to sweep)
νεωκόρος.shortDef: from a form of ναός and  (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary:--worshipper.

νεωτερικός.shortDef: from the comparative of νέος; appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile:--youthful.

glosses: probably an intensive form of ναί
νή.shortDef: probably an intensive form of ναί; a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as:--I protest by.

νηπιάζω.shortDef: from νήπιος; to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently:--be a child.

glosses: from an obsolete particle  (implying negation) and ἔπος
νήπιος.shortDef: from an obsolete particle  (implying negation) and ἔπος; not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian:--babe, child (+ -ish).

glosses: apparently from a derivative of the base of ναῦς (meaning wet)
νηρεύς.shortDef: apparently from a derivative of the base of ναῦς (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian:--Nereus.

νηρί.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נֵרִיָּה); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite:--Neri.

glosses: probably from the base of ναῦς
νῆσος.shortDef: probably from the base of ναῦς; an island:--island, isle.

νηστεία.shortDef: from νηστεύω; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement:-- fast(-ing).

νηστεύω.shortDef: from νῆστις; to abstain from food (religiously):--fast.

glosses: from the inseparable negative particle  (not) and ἐσθίω
νῆστις.shortDef: from the inseparable negative particle  (not) and ἐσθίω; not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously):--fasting.

νήφω.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet:--be sober, watch.

νίγερ.shortDef: of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian:--Niger.

νικάνωρ.shortDef: probably from νικάω; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian:--Nicanor.

νικάω.shortDef: from νίκη; to subdue (literally or figuratively):--conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory.

νίκη.shortDef: apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success:--victory.

νικόδημος.shortDef: from νῖκος and δῆμος; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite:--Nicodemus.

νικολαΐτης.shortDef: from Νικόλαος; a Nicolaïte, i.e. adherent of Nicolaüs:--Nicolaitane.

νικόλαος.shortDef: from νῖκος and λαός; victorious over the people; Nicolaüs, a heretic:--Nicolaus.

νικόπολις.shortDef: from νῖκος and πόλις; victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia:--Nicopolis.

νῖκος.shortDef: from νίκη; a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication) triumph:--victory.

νινευΐ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נִינְוֵה); Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria:--Nineve.

νινευΐτης.shortDef: from Νινευΐ; a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh:--of Nineve, Ninevite.

νοιέω.shortDef: from νοῦς; to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed:--consider, perceive, think, understand.

νόημα.shortDef: from νοιέω; a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself:--device, mind, thought.

νόθος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son:--bastard.

glosses: feminine from the same as νόμος
νομή.shortDef: feminine from the same as νόμος; pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage:--X eat, pasture.

νομίζω.shortDef: from νόμος; properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard:-- suppose, thing, be wont.

νομικός.shortDef: from νόμος; according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law:--about the law, lawyer.

glosses: adverb from a derivative of νόμος
νομίμως.shortDef: adverb from a derivative of νόμος; legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists):--lawfully.

νόμισμα.shortDef: from νομίζω; what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin:--money.

νομοδιδάσκαλος.shortDef: from νόμος and διδάσκαλος; an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi:--doctor (teacher) of the law.

νομοθεσία.shortDef: from νομοθέτης; legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code):--giving of the law.

νομοθετέω.shortDef: from νομοθέτης; to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them):--establish, receive the law.

glosses: from νόμος and a derivative of τίθημι
νομοθέτης.shortDef: from νόμος and a derivative of τίθημι; a legislator:--lawgiver.

νόμος.shortDef: from a primary  (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle):--law.

νοσέω.shortDef: from νόσος; to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon):--dote.

νόσος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability):--disease, infirmity, sickness.

νοσφίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from  (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle:--keep back, purloin.

νότος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself:--south (wind).

glosses: from νοῦς and a derivative of τίθημι
νουθεσία.shortDef: from νοῦς and a derivative of τίθημι; calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning:--admonition.

νουθετέω.shortDef: from the same as νουθεσία; to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently:--admonish, warn.

glosses: feminine of a compound of νέος and μήν (as noun by implication
νουμηνία.shortDef: feminine of a compound of νέος and μήν (as noun by implication, of ἡμέρα); the festival of new moon:--new moon.

glosses: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of νοῦς and ἔχω
νουνεχῶς.shortDef: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of νοῦς and ἔχω; in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently:--discreetly.

glosses: probably from the base of γινώσκω
νοῦς.shortDef: probably from the base of γινώσκω; the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning:--mind, understanding. Compare ψυχή.

glosses: probably contracted for a compound of νύμφη and δῶρον
νυμφᾶς.shortDef: probably contracted for a compound of νύμφη and δῶρον; nymph-given (i.e. -born); Nymphas, a Christian:--Nymphas.

glosses: from a primary but obsolete verb  (to veil as a bride
νύμφη.shortDef: from a primary but obsolete verb  (to veil as a bride; compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife:--bride, daughter in law.

νυμφίος.shortDef: from νύμφη; a bride-groom (literally or figuratively):--bridegroom.

glosses: a primary particle of present time
νῦν.shortDef: a primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate:--henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time). See also τανῦν, νυνί.

glosses: from neuter plural of ὁ and νῦν
τανῦν.shortDef: from neuter plural of ὁ and νῦν; the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present:--(but) now.

glosses: a prolonged form of νῦν for emphasis
νυνί.shortDef: a prolonged form of νῦν for emphasis; just now:--now.

νύσσω.shortDef: apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge"):--pierce.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of νεύω
νυστάζω.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of νεύω; to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay:--slumber.

νυχθήμερον.shortDef: from νύξ and ἡμέρα; a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours:--night and day.

νῶε.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (נֹחַ); Noë, (i.e. Noäch), a patriarch:--Noe.

νωθρός.shortDef: from a derivative of νόθος; sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid:--dull, slothful.

ξενία.shortDef: from ξένος; hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment:--lodging.

ξενίζω.shortDef: from ξένος; to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange:--entertain, lodge, (think it) strange.

glosses: from a compound of ξένος and δέχομαι
ξενοδοχέω.shortDef: from a compound of ξένος and δέχομαι; to be hospitable:--lodge strangers.

ξένος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer:--host, strange(-r).

ξέστης.shortDef: as if from  (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher):--pot.

ξηραίνω.shortDef: from ξηρός; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature:--dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).

glosses: from the base of ξέστης (through the idea of scorching)
ξηρός.shortDef: from the base of ξέστης (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water):--dry land, withered.

glosses: from another form of the base of ξέστης
ξύλον.shortDef: from another form of the base of ξέστης; timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance:--staff, stocks, tree, wood.

glosses: from a derivative of the same as ξύλον (meaning a razor)
ξυράω.shortDef: from a derivative of the same as ξύλον (meaning a razor); to shave or "shear" the hair:--shave.

ὁ.shortDef: the definite article; the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom):--the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc.

glosses: probably from the same as ἀγκάλη
ὄγκος.shortDef: probably from the same as ἀγκάλη; a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance):--weight.

ὅδε.shortDef: from ὁ and δέ; the same, i.e. this or that one (plural these or those); often used as a personal pronoun:--he, she, such, these, thus.

ὁδηγέω.shortDef: from ὁδηγός; to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach)):--guide, lead.

ὁδηγός.shortDef: from ὁδός and ἡγέομαι; a conductor (literally or figuratively (teacher)):--guide, leader.

glosses: from a compound of ὁδός and πορεύομαι
ὁδοιπορέω.shortDef: from a compound of ὁδός and πορεύομαι; to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel:--go on a journey.

ὁδοιπορία.shortDef: from the same as ὁδοιπορέω; travel:--journey(-ing).

ὁδός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a road; by implication, a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means:--journey, (high-)way.

glosses: perhaps from the base of ἐσθίω
ὀδούς.shortDef: perhaps from the base of ἐσθίω; a "tooth":--tooth.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of δύνω
ὀδυρμός.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of δύνω; moaning, i.e. lamentation:--mourning.

glosses: from the neuter of ὅς and the third person singular present indicative of εἰμί
ὅ ἐστι.shortDef: from the neuter of ὅς and the third person singular present indicative of εἰμί; which is:--called, which is (make), that is (to say).

ὀζίας.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (עֻזִּיָּה); Ozias (i.e. Uzzijah), an Israelite:--Ozias.

glosses: a primary verb (in a strengthened form)
ὄζω.shortDef: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to scent (usually an ill "odor"):--stink.

glosses: from ὅς with the directive enclitic of source
ὅθεν.shortDef: from ὅς with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction):--from thence, (from) whence, where(-by, -fore, -upon).

ὀθόνη.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail:--sheet.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of ὀθόνη
ὀθόνιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of ὀθόνη; a linen bandage:--linen clothes.

οἰκεῖος.shortDef: from οἶκος; domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent:--(those) of the (his own) house(-hold).

οἰκέτης.shortDef: from οἰκέω; a fellow resident, i.e. menial domestic:--(household) servant.

οἰκέω.shortDef: from οἶκος; to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit:--dwell. See also οἰκουμένη.

οἴκημα.shortDef: from οἰκέω; a tenement, i.e. (specially), a jail:--prison.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of οἰκέω (equivalent to οἴκημα)
οἰκητήριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of οἰκέω (equivalent to οἴκημα); a residence (literally or figuratively):--habitation, house.

οἰκία.shortDef: from οἶκος; properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics):--home, house(-hold).

οἰκιακός.shortDef: from οἰκία; familiar, i.e. (as noun) relatives:--they (them) of (his own) household.

οἰκοδεσποτέω.shortDef: from οἰκοδεσπότης; to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family:--guide the house.

οἰκοδεσπότης.shortDef: from οἶκος and δεσπότης; the head of a family:--goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house.

οἰκοδομέω.shortDef: from the same as οἰκοδομή; to be a house-builder, i.e. construct or (figuratively) confirm:--(be in) build(-er, -ing, up), edify, embolden.

glosses: feminine (abstract) of a compound of οἶκος and the base of δῶμα
οἰκοδομή.shortDef: feminine (abstract) of a compound of οἶκος and the base of δῶμα; architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation:--building, edify(-ication, -ing).

οἰκοδομία.shortDef: from the same as οἰκοδομή; confirmation:--edifying.

οἰκονομέω.shortDef: from οἰκονόμος; to manage (a house, i.e. an estate):--be steward.

οἰκονομία.shortDef: from οἰκονόμος; administration (of a household or estate); specially, a (religious) "economy":--dispensation, stewardship.

glosses: from οἶκος and the base of νόμος
οἰκονόμος.shortDef: from οἶκος and the base of νόμος; a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel):--chamberlain, governor, steward.

οἶκος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively):--home, house(-hold), temple.

glosses: feminine participle present passive of οἰκέω (as noun
οἰκουμένη.shortDef: feminine participle present passive of οἰκέω (as noun, by implication, of γῆ); land, i.e. the (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the Roman empire:--earth, world.

οἰκουρός.shortDef: from οἶκος and  (a guard; be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper"):--keeper at home.

οἰκτείρω.shortDef: from  (pity); to exercise pity:--have compassion on.

οἰκτίρμων.shortDef: from οἰκτείρω; compassionate:--merciful, of tender mercy.

glosses: from οἶνος and a derivative of the alternate of πίνω
οἰνοπότης.shortDef: from οἶνος and a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; a tippler:--winebibber.

glosses: a primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (יַיִן))
οἶνος.shortDef: a primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (יַיִן)); "wine" (literally or figuratively):--wine.

glosses: from οἶνος and a form of the base of φλύαρος
οἰνοφλυγία.shortDef: from οἶνος and a form of the base of φλύαρος; an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness):--excess of wine.

οἴομαι.shortDef: middle voice apparently from οἷος; to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion):--suppose, think.

οἷος.shortDef: probably akin to ὁ, ὅς, and ὅσος; such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so:--so (as), such as, what (manner of), which.

ὀκνηρός.shortDef: from ὀκνέω; tardy, i.e. indolent; (figuratively) irksome:--grievous, slothful.

ὀκταήμερος.shortDef: from ὀκτώ and ἡμέρα; an eight-day old person or act:--the eighth day.

ὄλεθρος.shortDef: from a primary  (to destroy; a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment:--destruction.

ὀλιγόπιστος.shortDef: from ὀλίγος and πίστις; incredulous, i.e. lacking confidence (in Christ):--of little faith.

ὀλίγος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat:--+ almost, brief(-ly), few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while.

ὀλιγόψυχος.shortDef: from ὀλίγος and ψυχή; little-spirited, i.e. faint-hearted:--feebleminded.

glosses: from a compound of ὀλίγος and  ("care")
ὀλιγωρέω.shortDef: from a compound of ὀλίγος and  ("care"); to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem:--despise.

ὀλοθρευτής.shortDef: from ὀλοθρεύω; a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent:--destroyer.

ὀλοθρεύω.shortDef: from ὄλεθρος; to spoil, i.e. slay:--destroy.

glosses: from a derivative of a compound of ὅλος and a derivative of καίω
ὁλοκαύτωμα.shortDef: from a derivative of a compound of ὅλος and a derivative of καίω; a wholly-consumed sacrifice ("holocaust"):--(whole) burnt offering.

ὁλοκληρία.shortDef: from ὁλόκληρος; integrity, i.e. physical wholeness:--perfect soundness.

ὁλόκληρος.shortDef: from ὅλος and κλῆρος; complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body):--entire, whole.

ὀλολύζω.shortDef: a reduplicated primary verb; to "howl" or "halloo", i.e. shriek:--howl.

ὅλος.shortDef: a primary word; "whole" or "all", i.e. complete (in extent, amount, time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb:--all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole.

ὁλοτελής.shortDef: from ὅλος and τέλος; complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect:--wholly.

ὀλυμπᾶς.shortDef: probably a contraction from  (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended); Olympas, a Christian:--Olympas.

ὄλυνθος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; an unripe (because out of season) fig:--untimely fig.

ὅλως.shortDef: adverb from ὅλος; completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means:--at all, commonly, utterly.

ὄμβρος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a thunder storm:--shower.

ὁμιλέω.shortDef: from ὅμιλος; to be in company with, i.e. (by implication) to converse:--commune, talk.

ὁμιλία.shortDef: from ὅμιλος; companionship ("homily"), i.e. (by implication) intercourse:--communication.

glosses: from the base of ὁμοῦ and a derivative of the alternate of αἱρέομαι (meaning a crowd)
ὅμιλος.shortDef: from the base of ὁμοῦ and a derivative of the alternate of αἱρέομαι (meaning a crowd); association together, i.e. a multitude:--company.

ὄμμα.shortDef: from ὀπτάνομαι; a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye:--eye.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary
ὀμνύω.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary,                         but obsolete , for which                         another prolonged form            is used in certain tenses; to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath:--swear.

glosses: adverb from a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and θυμός
ὁμοθυμαδόν.shortDef: adverb from a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and θυμός; unanimously:--with one accord (mind).

glosses: from ὅμοιος and the alternate of πάσχω
ὁμοιοπαθής.shortDef: from ὅμοιος and the alternate of πάσχω; similarly affected:--of (subject to) like passions.

ὅμοιος.shortDef: from the base of ὁμοῦ; similar (in appearance or character):--like, + manner.

ὁμοιόω.shortDef: from ὅμοιος; to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar:--be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble.

ὁμοίωμα.shortDef: from ὁμοιόω; a form; abstractly, resemblance:--made like to, likeness, shape, similitude.

glosses: from a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and λόγος
ὁμολογέω.shortDef: from a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and λόγος; to assent, i.e. covenant, acknowledge:--con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise.

ὁμολογία.shortDef: from the same as ὁμολογέω; acknowledgment:--con- (pro-)fession, professed.

glosses: adverb of present passive participle of ὁμολογέω
ὁμολογουμένως.shortDef: adverb of present passive participle of ὁμολογέω; confessedly:--without controversy.

glosses: from the base of ὁμοῦ and τέχνη
ὁμότεχνος.shortDef: from the base of ὁμοῦ and τέχνη; a fellow-artificer:--of the same craft.

ὁμοῦ.shortDef: genitive case of  (the same; akin to ἅμα) as adverb; at the same place or time:--together.

glosses: from the base of ὁμοῦ and φρήν
ὁμόφρων.shortDef: from the base of ὁμοῦ and φρήν; like-minded, i.e. harmonious:--of one mind.

glosses: adverb from the base of ὁμοῦ
ὅμως.shortDef: adverb from the base of ὁμοῦ; at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally) notwithstanding, yet still:--and even, nevertheless, though but.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of ὄνος
ὀνάριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of ὄνος; a little ass:--young ass.

ὀνειδίζω.shortDef: from ὄνειδος; to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt:--cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid.

glosses: probably akin to the base of ὄνομα
ὄνειδος.shortDef: probably akin to the base of ὄνομα; notoriety, i.e. a taunt (disgrace):--reproach.

ὀνήσιμος.shortDef: from ὀνίνημι; profitable; Onesimus, a Christian:--Onesimus.

glosses: from a derivative of ὀνίνημι and φόρος
ὀνησίφορος.shortDef: from a derivative of ὀνίνημι and φόρος; profit-bearer; Onesiphorus, a Christian:--Onespiphorus.

ὀνικός.shortDef: from ὄνος; belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass):--millstone.

glosses: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (
ὀνίνημι.shortDef: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (, to slur); for which another prolonged form () is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of ὄνομα through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from:--have joy.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of the base of γινώσκω (compare ὀνίνημι)
ὄνομα.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of the base of γινώσκω (compare ὀνίνημι); a "name" (literally or figuratively) (authority, character):--called, (+ sur-)name(-d).

ὀνομάζω.shortDef: from ὄνομα; to name, i.e. assign an appellation; by extension, to utter, mention, profess:--call, name.

ὄνος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a donkey:--an ass.

glosses: adverb of the oblique cases of ὤν
ὄντως.shortDef: adverb of the oblique cases of ὤν; really:--certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily.

ὄξος.shortDef: from ὀξύς; vinegar, i.e. sour wine:--vinegar.

glosses: probably akin to the base of ἀκμήν ("acid")
ὀξύς.shortDef: probably akin to the base of ἀκμήν ("acid"); keen; by analogy, rapid:--sharp, swift.

ὀπή.shortDef: probably from ὀπτάνομαι; a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water):--cave, place.

ὄπισθεν.shortDef: from  (regard; from ὀπτάνομαι) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of place or time):--after, backside, behind.

glosses: from the same as ὄπισθεν with enclitic of direction
ὀπίσω.shortDef: from the same as ὄπισθεν with enclitic of direction; to the back, i.e. aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun):--after, back(-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow.

ὁπλίζω.shortDef: from ὅπλον; to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively)):--arm self.

glosses: probably from a primary  (to be busy about)
ὅπλον.shortDef: probably from a primary  (to be busy about); an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war):--armour, instrument, weapon.

ὁποῖος.shortDef: from ὅς and ποῖος; of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent τοιοῦτος of quality):--what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever.

ὁπότε.shortDef: from ὅς and ποτέ; what(-ever) then, i.e. (of time) as soon as:--when.

ὅπου.shortDef: from ὅς and πού; what(-ever) where, i.e. at whichever spot:--in what place, where(-as, -soever), whither (+ soever).

glosses: a (middle voice) prolonged form of the primary (middle voice)
ὀπτάνομαι.shortDef: a (middle voice) prolonged form of the primary (middle voice)        ;    which is used for it in certain                                   tenses; and both as alternate of                                   ὁράω; to gaze (i.e. with wide-open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from βλέπω, which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from εἴδω, which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while θεάομαι, and still more emphatically its intensive θεωρέω, signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and σκοπέω a watching from a distance):--appear, look, see, shew self.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of ὀπτάνομαι
ὀπτασία.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; visuality, i.e. (concretely) an apparition:--vision.

glosses: from an obsolete verb akin to  (to "steep")
ὀπτός.shortDef: from an obsolete verb akin to  (to "steep"); cooked, i.e. roasted:--broiled.

glosses: apparently from the base of ὀψέ and ὥρα
ὀπώρα.shortDef: apparently from the base of ὀψέ and ὥρα; properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit:--fruit.

ὅπως.shortDef: from ὅς and πῶς; what(-ever) how, i.e. in the manner that (as adverb or conjunction of coincidence, intentional or actual):--because, how, (so) that, to, when.

ὅραμα.shortDef: from ὁράω; something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural):--sight, vision.

ὅρασις.shortDef: from ὁράω; the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance:--sight, vision.

ὁρατός.shortDef: from ὁράω; gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen:--visible.

ὁράω.shortDef: properly, to stare at (compare ὀπτάνομαι), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear:--behold, perceive, see, take heed.

ὀργή.shortDef: from ὀρέγομαι; properly, desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), i.e. (by analogy), violent passion (ire, or (justifiable) abhorrence); by implication punishment:--anger, indignation, vengeance, wrath.

ὀργίζω.shortDef: from ὀργή; to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated:--be angry (wroth).

ὀργυιά.shortDef: from ὀρέγομαι; a stretch of the arms, i.e. a fathom:--fathom.

glosses: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare ὄρος)
ὀρέγομαι.shortDef: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare ὄρος); to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for):--covet after, desire.

ὀρεινός.shortDef: from ὄρος; mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of χώρα) the Highlands (of Judæa):--hill country.

ὄρεξις.shortDef: from ὀρέγομαι; excitement of the mind, i.e. longing after:--lust.

glosses: from a compound of ὀρθός and πούς
ὀρθοποδέω.shortDef: from a compound of ὀρθός and πούς; to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward:--walk uprightly.

glosses: probably from the base of ὄρος
ὀρθός.shortDef: probably from the base of ὄρος; right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct:--straight, upright.

glosses: from a compound of ὀρθός and the base of τομώτερος
ὀρθοτομέω.shortDef: from a compound of ὀρθός and the base of τομώτερος, to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message):--rightly divide.

ὀρθρίζω.shortDef: from ὄρθρος; to use the dawn, i.e. (by implication) to repair betimes:--come early in the morning.

ὀρθρινός.shortDef: from ὄρθρος; relating to the dawn, i.e. matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day):--morning.

ὄρθριος.shortDef: from ὄρθρος; in the dawn, i.e. up at day-break:--early.

ὄρθρος.shortDef: from the same as ὄρος; dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn:--early in the morning.

ὀρθῶς.shortDef: adverb from ὀρθός; in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally):--plain, right(-ly).

ὁρίζω.shortDef: from ὅριον; to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify:--declare, determine, limit, ordain.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary  (a bound or limit)
ὅριον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary  (a bound or limit); a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region):--border, coast.

ὁρκίζω.shortDef: from ὅρκος; to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin:--adjure, charge.

ὅρκος.shortDef: from  (a fence; perhaps akin to ὅριον); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath):--oath.

glosses: from a compound of ὅρκος and a derivative of ὀμνύω
ὁρκωμοσία.shortDef: from a compound of ὅρκος and a derivative of ὀμνύω; asseveration on oath:--oath.

ὁρμάω.shortDef: from ὁρμή; to start, spur or urge on, i.e. (reflexively) to dash or plunge:--run (violently), rush.

ὁρμή.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a violent impulse, i.e. onset:--assault.

ὅρμημα.shortDef: from ὁρμή; an attack, i.e. (abstractly) precipitancy:--violence.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of ὄρνις
ὄρνεον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of ὄρνις; a birdling:--bird, fowl.

glosses: probably from a prolonged form of the base of ὄρος
ὄρνις.shortDef: probably from a prolonged form of the base of ὄρος; a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl):--hen.

glosses: from a compound of the base of ὅριον and a derivative of τίθημι
ὁροθεσία.shortDef: from a compound of the base of ὅριον and a derivative of τίθημι; a limit-placing, i.e. (concretely) boundary-line:--bound.

glosses: probably from an obsolete  (to rise or "rear"
ὄρος.shortDef: probably from an obsolete  (to rise or "rear"; perhaps akin to αἴρω; compare ὄρνις); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain):--hill, mount(-ain).

ὀρύσσω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to "burrow" in the ground, i.e. dig:--dig.

ὀρφανός.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; bereaved ("orphan"), i.e. parentless:--comfortless, fatherless.

glosses: middle voice from  (a row or ring)
ὀρχέομαι.shortDef: middle voice from  (a row or ring); to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion):--dance.

glosses: probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article ὁ)
ὅς.shortDef: probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article ὁ); the relatively (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that:--one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who(-m, -se), etc. See also οὗ.

ὁσάκις.shortDef: multiple adverb from ὅς; how (i.e. with ἄν, so) many times as:--as oft(-en) as.

ὅσιος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; properly, right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from 1342, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from ἱερός, which denotes formal consecration; and from ἅγιος, which relates to purity from defilement), i.e. hallowed (pious, sacred, sure):--holy, mercy, shalt be. 342

ὀσμή.shortDef: from ὄζω; fragrance (literally or figuratively):--odour, savour.

ὅσος.shortDef: by reduplication from ὅς; as (much, great, long, etc.) as:--all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), (in-)asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who(-soever).

ὅσπερ.shortDef: from ὅς and περ; who especially:--whomsoever.

ὅστις.shortDef: from ὅς and τὶς; which some, i.e. any that; also (definite) which same:--X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what(-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who(-soever). Compare ὅτι.

ὀστράκινος.shortDef: from  ("oyster") (a tile, i.e. terra cotta); earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail:--of earth, earthen.

ὄσφρησις.shortDef: from a derivative of ὄζω; smell (the sense):--smelling.

ὀσφῦς.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power:--loin.

ὅταν.shortDef: from ὅτε and ἄν; whenever (implying hypothesis or more or less uncertainty); also causatively (conjunctionally) inasmuch as:--as long (soon) as, that, + till, when(-soever), while.

ὅτε.shortDef: from ὅς and τέ; at which (thing) too, i.e. when:--after (that), as soon as, that, when, while.

ὅτι.shortDef: neuter of ὅστις as conjunction; demonstrative, that (sometimes redundant); causative, because:--as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why.

glosses: for the genitive case of ὅστις (as adverb)
ὅτου.shortDef: for the genitive case of ὅστις (as adverb); during which same time, i.e. whilst:--whiles.

οὐ.shortDef: a primary word; the absolute negative (compare μή) adverb; no or not:--+ long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but. See also οὐ μή, μῆκος.

glosses: genitive case of ὅς as adverb
οὗ.shortDef: genitive case of ὅς as adverb; at which place, i.e. where:--where(-in), whither(-soever).

οὐαί.shortDef: a primary exclamation of grief; "woe":--alas, woe.

οὐδαμῶς.shortDef: adverb from (the feminine) of οὐδείς; by no means:--not.

οὐδέ.shortDef: from οὐ and δέ; not however, i.e. neither, nor, not even:--neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even, so much as), + nothing, so much as.

οὐδείς.shortDef: from οὐδέ and εἷς; not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing:--any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought.

οὐδέποτε.shortDef: from οὐδέ and ποτέ; not even at any time, i.e. never at all:--neither at any time, never, nothing at any time.

οὐδέπω.shortDef: from οὐδέ and -πω; not even yet:--as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet.

οὐκέτι.shortDef: from οὐ and ἔτι; not yet, no longer:--after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter) not, no longer (more), not as yet (now), now no more (not), yet (not).

οὐκοῦν.shortDef: from οὐ and οὖν; is it not therefore that, i.e. (affirmatively) hence or so:--then.

οὖν.shortDef: apparently a primary word; (adverbially) certainly, or (conjunctionally) accordingly:--and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore.

οὔπω.shortDef: from οὐ and -πω; not yet:--hitherto not, (no…) as yet, not yet.

οὐρά.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a tail:--tail.

οὐράνιος.shortDef: from οὐρανός; celestial, i.e. belonging to or coming from the sky:--heavenly.

glosses: from οὐρανός and the enclitic of source
οὐρανόθεν.shortDef: from οὐρανός and the enclitic of source; from the sky:--from heaven.

glosses: perhaps from the same as ὄρος (through the idea of elevation)
οὐρανός.shortDef: perhaps from the same as ὄρος (through the idea of elevation); the sky; by extension, heaven (as the abode of God); by implication, happiness, power, eternity; specially, the Gospel (Christianity):--air, heaven(-ly), sky.

οὐρβανός.shortDef: of Latin origin; Urbanus (of the city, "urbane"), a Christian:--Urbanus.

οὐρίας.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (אוּרִיָּה); Urias (i.e. Urijah), a Hittite:--Urias.

οὖς.shortDef: apparently a primary word; the ear (physically or mentally):--ear.

οὐσία.shortDef: from the feminine of ὤν; substance, i.e. property (possessions):--goods, substance.

οὔτε.shortDef: from οὐ and τέ; not too, i.e. neither or nor; by analogy, not even:--neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing.

glosses: from the article ὁ and αὐτός
οὗτος.shortDef: from the article ὁ and αὐτός; the he (she or it), i.e. this or that (often with article repeated):--he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, woman), which, who.

οὕτω.shortDef: adverb from οὗτος; in this way (referring to what precedes or follows):--after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like(-wise), no more, on this fashion(-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what.

οὐχί.shortDef: intensive of οὐ; not indeed:--nay, not.

ὀφειλέτης.shortDef: from ὀφείλω; an ower, i.e. person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor (against God):--debtor, which owed, sinner.

ὀφειλή.shortDef: from ὀφείλω; indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty:--debt, due.

ὀφείλημα.shortDef: from (the alternate of) ὀφείλω; something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault:--debt.

glosses: probably from the base of ὄφελος (through the idea of accruing)
ὀφείλω.shortDef: probably from the base of ὄφελος (through the idea of accruing); to owe (pecuniarily); figuratively, to be under obligation (ought, must, should); morally, to fail in duty:--behove, be bound, (be) debt(-or), (be) due(-ty), be guilty (indebted), (must) need(-s), ought, owe, should. See also ὄφελον.

glosses: first person singular of a past tense of ὀφείλω
ὄφελον.shortDef: first person singular of a past tense of ὀφείλω; I ought (wish), i.e. (interjection) oh that!:--would (to God).

ὄφελος.shortDef: from  (to heap up, i.e. accumulate or benefit); gain:--advantageth, profit.

ὀφθαλμοδουλεία.shortDef: from ὀφθαλμός and δουλεία; sight-labor, i.e. that needs watching (remissness):--eye-service.

ὀφθαλμός.shortDef: from ὀπτάνομαι; the eye (literally or figuratively); by implication, vision; figuratively, envy (from the jealous side-glance):--eye, sight.

glosses: probably from ὀπτάνομαι (through the idea of sharpness of vision)
ὄφις.shortDef: probably from ὀπτάνομαι (through the idea of sharpness of vision); a snake, figuratively, (as a type of sly cunning) an artful malicious person, especially Satan:--serpent.

glosses: perhaps from ὀπτάνομαι (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision)
ὀφρῦς.shortDef: perhaps from ὀπτάνομαι (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); the eye-"brow" or forehead, i.e. (figuratively) the brink of a precipice:--brow.

ὀχλέω.shortDef: from ὄχλος; to mob, i.e. (by implication) to harass:--vex.

ὀχλοποιέω.shortDef: from ὄχλος and ποιέω; to make a crowd, i.e. raise a public disturbance:--gather a company.

glosses: from a derivative of ἔχω (meaning a vehicle)
ὄχλος.shortDef: from a derivative of ἔχω (meaning a vehicle); a throng (as borne along); by implication, the rabble; by extension, a class of people; figuratively, a riot:--company, multitude, number (of people), people, press.

glosses: from a remote derivative of ἔχω (meaning to fortify
ὀχύρωμα.shortDef: from a remote derivative of ἔχω (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely); a castle (figuratively, argument):--stronghold.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of ὀπτός
ὀψάριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of ὀπτός; a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), i.e. (specially), fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment):--fish.

glosses: from the same as ὀπίσω (through the idea of backwardness)
ὀψέ.shortDef: from the same as ὀπίσω (through the idea of backwardness); (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day:--(at) even, in the end.

ὄψιος.shortDef: from ὀψέ; late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve):--even(-ing, (-tide)).

ὄψις.shortDef: from ὀπτάνομαι; properly, sight (the act), i.e. (by implication) the visage, an external show:--appearance, countenance, face.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as ὀψάριον
ὀψώνιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as ὀψάριον; rations for a soldier, i.e. (by extension) his stipend or pay:-- wages.

ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος.lemma: ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος
ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος.translit: ho ṑn kaí ho ēn kaí ho erchómenos
ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος.pronunciation: ho own kahee ho ane kahee ho er-khom'-en-os
glosses: a phrase combining ὁ with the present participle and imperfect of εἰμί and the present participle of ἔρχομαι by means of καί
ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος.shortDef: a phrase combining ὁ with the present participle and imperfect of εἰμί and the present participle of ἔρχομαι by means of καί; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ:--which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be).

παγίς.shortDef: from πήγνυμι; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation):--snare.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of πάθος
πάθημα.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of πάθος; something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence:-- affection, affliction, motion, suffering.

παθητός.shortDef: from the same as πάθημα; liable (i.e. doomed) to experience pain:--suffer.

πάθος.shortDef: from the alternate of πάσχω; properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence):-- (inordinate) affection, lust.

glosses: from παῖς and a reduplicated form of ἄγω
παιδαγωγός.shortDef: from παῖς and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("pædagogue")):-- instructor, schoolmaster.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of παῖς
παιδάριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of παῖς; a little boy:--child, lad.

παιδεία.shortDef: from παιδεύω; tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction:--chastening, chastisement, instruction, nurture.

παιδευτής.shortDef: from παιδεύω; a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner:--which corrected, instructor.

παιδεύω.shortDef: from παῖς; to train up a child, i.e. educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment):--chasten(-ise), instruct, learn, teach.

παιδιόθεν.shortDef: adverb (of source) from παιδίον; from infancy:--of a child.

παιδίον.shortDef: neuter diminutive of παῖς; a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian:--(little, young) child, damsel.

παιδίσκη.shortDef: feminine diminutive of παῖς; a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant:--bondmaid(-woman), damsel, maid(-en).

παίζω.shortDef: from παῖς; to sport (as a boy):--play.

παῖς.shortDef: perhaps from παίω; a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God):--child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man.

παίω.shortDef: a primary verb; to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than τύπτω); specially, to sting (as a scorpion):--smite, strike.

glosses: feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation
πακατιανή.shortDef: feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia:--Pacatiana.

glosses: probably another form for πάλιν (through the idea of retrocession)
πάλαι.shortDef: probably another form for πάλιν (through the idea of retrocession); (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient:--any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past.

παλαιός.shortDef: from πάλαι; antique, i.e. not recent, worn out:--old.

παλαιόω.shortDef: from παλαιός; to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete:--decay, make (wax) old.

πάλη.shortDef: from  (to vibrate; another form for βάλλω); wrestling:--+ wrestle.

παλιγγενεσία.shortDef: from πάλιν and γένεσις; (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration:--regeneration.

glosses: probably from the same as πάλη (through the idea of oscillatory repetition)
πάλιν.shortDef: probably from the same as πάλη (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand:--again.

glosses: dative case (adverb) of a compound of πᾶς and πλῆθος
παμπληθεί.shortDef: dative case (adverb) of a compound of πᾶς and πλῆθος; in full multitude, i.e. concertedly or simultaneously:--all at once.

πάμπολυς.shortDef: from πᾶς and πολύς; full many, i.e. immense:--very great.

glosses: from a compound of πᾶς and πυρά
παμφυλία.shortDef: from a compound of πᾶς and πυρά; every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (χώρα being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor:--Pamphylia.

glosses: neuter of a presumed compound of πᾶς and a derivative of δέχομαι
πανδοχεῖον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed compound of πᾶς and a derivative of δέχομαι; all-receptive, i.e. a public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan):--inn.

πανδοχεύς.shortDef: from the same as πανδοχεῖον; an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai):--host.

glosses: from πᾶς and a derivative of ἀγορά
πανήγυρις.shortDef: from πᾶς and a derivative of ἀγορά; a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship:--general assembly.

πανοικί.shortDef: adverb from πᾶς and οἶκος; with the whole family:--with all his house.

glosses: from a compound of πᾶς and ὅπλον
πανοπλία.shortDef: from a compound of πᾶς and ὅπλον; full armor ("panoply"):--all (whole) armour.

πανουργία.shortDef: from πανοῦργος; adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry:--(cunning) craftiness, subtilty.

πανοῦργος.shortDef: from πᾶς and ἔργον; all-working, i.e. adroit (shrewd):--crafty.

πανταχόθεν.shortDef: adverb (of source) from πανταχοῦ; from all directions:--from every quarter.

glosses: genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of πᾶς
πανταχοῦ.shortDef: genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of πᾶς; universally:--in all places, everywhere.

παντελής.shortDef: from πᾶς and τέλος; full-ended, i.e. entire (neuter as noun, completion):--+ in (no) wise, uttermost.

πάντοθεν.shortDef: adverb (of source) from πᾶς; from (i.e. on) all sides:--on every side, round about.

παντοκράτωρ.shortDef: from πᾶς and κράτος; the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign):--Almighty, Omnipotent.

πάντοτε.shortDef: from πᾶς and ὅτε; every when, i.e. at all times:--alway(-s), ever(-more).

πάντως.shortDef: adverb from πᾶς; entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event:--by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely.

παρά.shortDef: a primary preposition; properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of):--above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with. In compounds it retains the same variety of application.

glosses: from παρά and the base of βάσις
παραβαίνω.shortDef: from παρά and the base of βάσις; to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command:--(by) transgress(-ion).

παραβάλλω.shortDef: from παρά and βάλλω; to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken:--arrive, compare.

glosses: from παρά and the middle voice of βιάζω
παραβιάζομαι.shortDef: from παρά and the middle voice of βιάζω; to force contrary to (nature), i.e. compel (by entreaty):--constrain.

παραβολή.shortDef: from παραβάλλω; a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage:--comparison, figure, parable, proverb.

glosses: from παρά and the middle voice of βουλεύω
παραβουλεύομαι.shortDef: from παρά and the middle voice of βουλεύω; to misconsult, i.e. disregard:--not (to) regard(-ing).

glosses: from παρά and the base of ἄγγελος
παραγγέλλω.shortDef: from παρά and the base of ἄγγελος; to transmit a message, i.e. (by implication) to enjoin:--(give in) charge, (give) command(-ment), declare.

παραγίνομαι.shortDef: from παρά and γίνομαι; to become near, i.e. approach (have arrived); by implication, to appear publicly:--come, go, be present.

παράγω.shortDef: from παρά and ἄγω; to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away:--depart, pass (away, by, forth).

παραδειγματίζω.shortDef: from παρά and δειγματίζω; to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy:--make a public example, put to an open shame.

παράδεισος.shortDef: of Oriental origin (compare פַּרְדֵּס); a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise"):--paradise.

παραδέχομαι.shortDef: from παρά and δέχομαι; to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in:--receive.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and διατρίβω
παραδιατριβή.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and διατρίβω; misemployment, i.e. meddlesomeness:--perverse disputing.

παραδίδωμι.shortDef: from παρά and δίδωμι; to surrender, i.e yield up, intrust, transmit:--betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend.

glosses: from παρά and δόξα (in the sense of seeming)
παράδοξος.shortDef: from παρά and δόξα (in the sense of seeming); contrary to expectation, i.e. extraordinary ("paradox"):--strange.

παράδοσις.shortDef: from παραδίδωμι; transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law:--ordinance, tradition.

παραζηλόω.shortDef: from παρά and ζηλόω; to stimulate alongside, i.e. excite to rivalry:--provoke to emulation (jealousy).

παραθαλάσσιος.shortDef: from παρά and θάλασσα; along the sea, i.e. maritime (lacustrine):--upon the sea coast.

παραθεωρέω.shortDef: from παρά and θεωρέω; to overlook or disregard:--neglect.

παραθήκη.shortDef: from παρατίθημι; a deposit, i.e. (figuratively) trust:--committed unto.

παραινέω.shortDef: from παρά and αἰνέω; to mispraise, i.e. recommend or advise (a different course):--admonish, exhort.

glosses: from παρά and the middle voice of αἰτέω
παραιτέομαι.shortDef: from παρά and the middle voice of αἰτέω; to beg off, i.e. deprecate, decline, shun:--avoid, (make) excuse, intreat, refuse, reject.

παρακαθίζω.shortDef: from παρά and καθίζω; to sit down near:--sit.

παρακαλέω.shortDef: from παρά and καλέω; to call near, i.e. invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation):--beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray.

παρακαλύπτω.shortDef: from παρά and καλύπτω; to cover alongside, i.e. veil (figuratively):--hide.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and κατατίθημι
παρακαταθήκη.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and κατατίθημι; something put down alongside, i.e. a deposit (sacred trust):--that (thing) which is committed (un-)to (trust).

παράκειμαι.shortDef: from παρά and κεῖμαι; to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy):--be present.

παράκλησις.shortDef: from παρακαλέω; imploration, hortation, solace:--comfort, consolation, exhortation, intreaty.

παρακοή.shortDef: from παρακούω; inattention, i.e. (by implication) disobedience:--disobedience.

παρακολουθέω.shortDef: from παρά and ἀκολουθέω; to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to:--attain, follow, fully know, have understanding.

παρακούω.shortDef: from παρά and ἀκούω; to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey:--neglect to hear.

παρακύπτω.shortDef: from παρά and κύπτω; to bend beside, i.e. lean over (so as to peer within):--look (into), stoop down.

παραλαμβάνω.shortDef: from παρά and λαμβάνω; to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn:--receive, take (unto, with).

glosses: from παρά and the middle voice of λέγω (in its original sense)
παραλέγομαι.shortDef: from παρά and the middle voice of λέγω (in its original sense); (specially), to lay one's course near, i.e. sail past:--pass, sail by.

παράλιος.shortDef: from παρά and ἅλς; beside the salt (sea), i.e. maritime:--sea coast.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and ἀλλάσσω
παραλλαγή.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and ἀλλάσσω; transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness:--variableness.

παραλογίζομαι.shortDef: from παρά and λογίζομαι; to misreckon, i.e. delude:--beguile, deceive.

παραλυτικός.shortDef: from a derivative of παραλύω; as if dissolved, i.e. "paralytic":--that had (sick of) the palsy.

παραλύω.shortDef: from παρά and λύω; to loosen beside, i.e. relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled):--feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy.

παραμένω.shortDef: from παρά and μένω; to stay near, i.e. remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere):--abide, continue.

glosses: from παρά and the middle voice of a derivative of μῦθος
παραμυθέομαι.shortDef: from παρά and the middle voice of a derivative of μῦθος; to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console:--comfort.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and νόμος
παρανομέω.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and νόμος; to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress:--contrary to law.

παρανομία.shortDef: from the same as παρανομέω; transgression:--iniquity.

παραπικραίνω.shortDef: from παρά and πικραίνω; to embitter alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--provoke.

παραπίπτω.shortDef: from παρά and πίπτω; to fall aside, i.e. (figuratively) to apostatize:--fall away.

παραπλέω.shortDef: from παρά and πλέω; to sail near:--sail by.

glosses: neuter of a compound of παρά and the base of πλησίον (as adverb)
παραπλήσιον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of παρά and the base of πλησίον (as adverb); close by, i.e. (figuratively) almost:--nigh unto.

glosses: adverb from the same as παραπλήσιον
παραπλησίως.shortDef: adverb from the same as παραπλήσιον; in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly:--likewise.

παραπορεύομαι.shortDef: from παρά and πορεύομαι; to travel near:--go, pass (by).

παράπτωμα.shortDef: from παραπίπτω; a side-slip (lapse or deviation), i.e. (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression:--fall, fault, offence, sin, trespass.

glosses: from παρά and the alternate of ῥέω
παραῤῥυέω.shortDef: from παρά and the alternate of ῥέω; to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss):--let slip.

glosses: from παρά and the base of σημαίνω
παράσημος.shortDef: from παρά and the base of σημαίνω; side-marked, i.e. labelled (with a badge (figure-head) of a ship):--sign.

glosses: from παρά and a derivative of σκεῦος
παρασκευάζω.shortDef: from παρά and a derivative of σκεῦος; to furnish aside, i.e. get ready:--prepare self, be (make) ready.

παρατείνω.shortDef: from παρά and teino (to stretch); to extend along, i.e. prolong (in point of time):--continue.

παρατηρέω.shortDef: from παρά and τηρέω; to inspect alongside, i.e. note insidiously or scrupulously:--observe, watch.

παρατήρησις.shortDef: from παρατηρέω; inspection, i.e. ocular evidence:--obervation.

παρατίθημι.shortDef: from παρά and τίθημι; to place alongside, i.e. present (food, truth); by implication, to deposit (as a trust or for protection):--allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before.

παρατυγχάνω.shortDef: from παρά and τυγχάνω; to chance near, i.e. fall in with:--meet with.

glosses: from παρά and a derivative of αὐτός
παραυτίκα.shortDef: from παρά and a derivative of αὐτός; at the very instant, i.e. momentary:--but for a moment.

glosses: from παρά and φέρω (including its alternate forms)
παραφέρω.shortDef: from παρά and φέρω (including its alternate forms); to bear along or aside, i.e. carry off (literally or figuratively); by implication, to avert:--remove, take away.

παραφρονέω.shortDef: from παρά and φρονέω; to misthink, i.e. be insane (silly):--as a fool.

παραχειμάζω.shortDef: from παρά and χειμάζω; to winter near, i.e. stay with over the rainy season:--winter.

παραχειμασία.shortDef: from παραχειμάζω; a wintering over:--winter in.

glosses: from παρά and χρῆμα (in its original sense)
παραχρῆμα.shortDef: from παρά and χρῆμα (in its original sense); at the thing itself, i.e. instantly:--forthwith, immediately, presently, straightway, soon.

glosses: from παρά and εἰμί (including its various forms)
πάρειμι.shortDef: from παρά and εἰμί (including its various forms); to be near, i.e. at hand; neuter present participle (singular) time being, or (plural) property:--come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present.

παρεισάγω.shortDef: from παρά and εἰσάγω; to lead in aside, i.e. introduce surreptitiously:--privily bring in.

παρείσακτος.shortDef: from παρεισάγω; smuggled in:--unawares brought in.

glosses: from παρά and a compound of εἰς and δύνω
παρεισδύνω.shortDef: from παρά and a compound of εἰς and δύνω; to settle in alongside, i.e. lodge stealthily:--creep in unawares.

παρεισέρχομαι.shortDef: from παρά and εἰσέρχομαι; to come in alongside, i.e. supervene additionally or steathily:--come in privily, enter.

παρεισφέρω.shortDef: from παρά and εἰσφέρω; to bear in alongside, i.e. introduce simultaneously:--give.

παρεκτός.shortDef: from παρά and ἐκτός; near outside, i.e. besides:--except, saving, without.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and ἐμβάλλω
παρεμβολή.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and ἐμβάλλω; a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), i.e. (specially), battle-array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia):--army, camp, castle.

παρενοχλέω.shortDef: from παρά and ἐνοχλέω; to harass further, i.e. annoy:--trouble.

glosses: from παρά and the base of ἐπιδημέω
παρεπίδημος.shortDef: from παρά and the base of ἐπιδημέω; an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner:--pilgrim, stranger.

παρέρχομαι.shortDef: from παρά and ἔρχομαι; to come near or aside, i.e. to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert:--come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress.

παρέχω.shortDef: from παρά and ἔχω; to hold near, i.e. present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion:--bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and a derivative of ἀγορά (meaning to harangue an assembly)
παρηγορία.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and a derivative of ἀγορά (meaning to harangue an assembly); an address alongside, i.e. (specially), consolation:--comfort.

παρθένος.shortDef: of unknown origin; a maiden; by implication, an unmarried daughter:--virgin.

πάρθος.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; a Parthian, i.e. inhabitant of Parthia:--Parthian.

παρίημι.shortDef: from παρά and hiemi (to send); to let by, i.e. relax:--hang down.

παρίστημι.shortDef: from παρά and ἵστημι; to stand beside, i.e. (transitively) to exhibit, proffer, (specially), recommend, (figuratively) substantiate; or (intransitively) to be at hand (or ready), aid:--assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew, stand (before, by, here, up, with), yield.

glosses: probably by contraction for  (a derivative of a compound of παρά and μένω)
παρμενᾶς.shortDef: probably by contraction for  (a derivative of a compound of παρά and μένω); constant; Parmenas, a Christian:--Parmenas.

πάροδος.shortDef: from παρά and ὁδός; a by-road, i.e. (actively) a route:--way.

παροικέω.shortDef: from παρά and οἰκέω; to dwell near, i.e. reside as a foreigner:--sojourn in, be a stranger.

παροικία.shortDef: from πάροικος; foreign residence:--sojourning, X as strangers.

πάροικος.shortDef: from παρά and οἶκος; having a home near, i.e. (as noun) a by-dweller (alien resident):--foreigner, sojourn, stranger.

glosses: from a compound of παρά and perhaps a derivative of οἴομαι
παροιμία.shortDef: from a compound of παρά and perhaps a derivative of οἴομαι; apparently a state alongside of supposition, i.e. (concretely) an adage; specially, an enigmatical or fictitious illustration:--parable, proverb.

πάροινος.shortDef: from παρά and οἶνος; staying near wine, i.e. tippling (a toper):--given to wine.

παροίχομαι.shortDef: from παρά and  (to depart); to escape along, i.e. be gone:--past.

παρομοιάζω.shortDef: from παρόμοιος; to resemble:--be like unto.

παρόμοιος.shortDef: from παρά and ὅμοιος; alike nearly, i.e. similar:--like.

glosses: from παρά and a derivative of ὀξύς
παροξύνω.shortDef: from παρά and a derivative of ὀξύς; to sharpen alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--easily provoke, stir.

παροξυσμός.shortDef: from παροξύνω ("paroxysm"); incitement (to good), or dispute (in anger):--contention, provoke unto.

παροργίζω.shortDef: from παρά and ὀργίζω; to anger alongside, i.e. enrage:--anger, provoke to wrath.

παροτρύνω.shortDef: from παρά and  (to spur); to urge along, i.e. stimulate (to hostility):--stir up.

glosses: from the present participle of πάρειμι
παρουσία.shortDef: from the present participle of πάρειμι; a being near, i.e. advent (often, return; specially, of Christ to punish Jerusalem, or finally the wicked); (by implication) physically, aspect:--coming, presence.

glosses: from παρά and the base of ὀψάριον
παροψίς.shortDef: from παρά and the base of ὀψάριον; a side-dish (the receptacle):--platter.

glosses: from πᾶς and a derivative of ῥέω
παῤῥησία.shortDef: from πᾶς and a derivative of ῥέω; all out-spokenness, i.e. frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance:--bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness).

παῤῥησιάζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from παῤῥησία; to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor:--be (wax) bold, (preach, speak) boldly.

glosses: including all the forms of declension
πᾶς.shortDef: including all the forms of declension; apparently a primary word; all, any, every, the whole:--all (manner of, means), alway(-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as many as, + no(-thing), X thoroughly, whatsoever, whole, whosoever.
