σαβαώθ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (צָבָא in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God:--sabaoth.

σαββατισμός.shortDef: from a derivative of σάββατον; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven):--rest.

σάββατον.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שַׁבָּת); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications:--sabbath (day), week.

glosses: from a derivative of  (to equip) meaning furniture
σαγήνη.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing:--net.

σαδδουκαῖος.shortDef: probably from Σαδώκ; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite:--Sadducee.

σαδώκ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (צָדוֹק); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite:--Sadoc.

σαίνω.shortDef: akin to σείω; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb):--move.

σάκκος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שַׂק); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief):-- sackcloth.

σαλά.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שֶׁלַח); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch :--Sala.

σαλαθιήλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite:--Salathiel.

glosses: probably from σάλος (from the surge on the shore)
σαλαμίς.shortDef: probably from σάλος (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus:--Salamis.

glosses: probably from the same as σαλεύω
σαλείμ.shortDef: probably from the same as σαλεύω; Salim, a place in Palestine:--Salim.

σαλεύω.shortDef: from σάλος; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite:--move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.

σαλήμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שָׁלֵם); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine:--Salem.

σαλμών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שַׂלְמוֹן); Salmon, an Israelite:--Salmon.

glosses: perhaps of similar origin to Σαλαμίς
σαλμώνη.shortDef: perhaps of similar origin to Σαλαμίς; Salmone, a place in Crete:--Salmone.

glosses: probably from the base of σαίνω
σάλος.shortDef: probably from the base of σαίνω; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow:--wave.

glosses: perhaps from σάλος (through the idea of quavering or reverberation)
σάλπιγξ.shortDef: perhaps from σάλος (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet:--trump(-et).

σαλπίζω.shortDef: from σάλπιγξ; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively):--(which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).

glosses: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from שָׁלוֹם)
σαλώμη.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from שָׁלוֹם); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess:--Salome.

σαμάρεια.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שֹׁמְרוֹן); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine:--Samaria.

σαμαρείτης.shortDef: from Σαμάρεια; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria:--Samaritan.

σαμαρεῖτις.shortDef: feminine of Σαμαρείτης; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria:--of Samaria.

σαμοθρᾴκη.shortDef: from Σάμος and  (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean:--Samothracia.

σάμος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Samos.

σαμουήλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שְׁמוּאֵל); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite:--Samuel.

σαμψών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְשׁוֹן); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite:--Samson.

σανδάλιον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of  (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad:--sandal.

σαούλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שָׁאוּל); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul. Compare Σαῦλος.

σαπρός.shortDef: from σήπω; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):--bad, corrupt. Compare πονηρός.

σαπφείρη.shortDef: feminine of σάπφειρος; Sapphire, an Israelitess:--Sapphira.

σάπφειρος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (סַפִּיר); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem:--sapphire.

σαργάνη.shortDef: apparently of Hebrew origin (שָׂרַג); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work:--basket.

σάρδεις.shortDef: plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor:--Sardis.

σάρδινος.shortDef: from the same as σάρδιος; sardine (λίθος being implied), i.e. a gem, so called:--sardine.

σάρδιος.shortDef: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called:--sardius.

glosses: from the base of σάρδιος and  (the nail of a finger
σαρδόνυξ.shortDef: from the base of σάρδιος and  (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called:-- sardonyx.

σάρεπτα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (צָרְפַת); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine:--Sarepta.

σαρκικός.shortDef: from σάρξ; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate:--carnal, fleshly.

σάρκινος.shortDef: from σάρξ; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft:--fleshly.

glosses: probably from the base of σαρόω
σάρξ.shortDef: probably from the base of σαρόω; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such):--carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly).

σαρούχ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שְׂרוּג); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch:--Saruch.

glosses: from a derivative of  (to brush off
σαρόω.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to brush off; akin to σύρω); meaning a broom; to sweep:--sweep.

σάῤῥα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שָׂרָה); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham:--Sara, Sarah.

σάρων.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שָׁרוֹן); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine:--Saron.

σατᾶν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שָׂטָן); Satan, i.e. the devil:--Satan. Compare Σατανᾶς.

glosses: of Chaldee origin corresponding to מַעְבָּד (with the definite affix)
σατανᾶς.shortDef: of Chaldee origin corresponding to מַעְבָּד (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil:--Satan.

σάτον.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (סְאָה); a certain measure for things dry:--measure.

σαῦλος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin, the same as Σαούλ; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul.

glosses: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb
σβέννυμι.shortDef: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively):--go out, quench.

σέ.shortDef: accusative case singular of σύ; thee:--thee, thou, X thy house.

glosses: genitive case from σέ and αὐτός
σεαυτοῦ.shortDef: genitive case from σέ and αὐτός,                             also dative case of the same,        ,  and accusative case        , likewise contracted        ,        ,     and        ,    respectively; of (with, to) thyself:--thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).

glosses: middle voice from a derivative of σέβομαι
σεβάζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from a derivative of σέβομαι; to venerate, i.e. adore:--worship.

σέβασμα.shortDef: from σεβάζομαι; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc):--devotion, that is worshipped.

σεβαστός.shortDef: from σεβάζομαι; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial:--Augustus(-').

glosses: middle voice of an apparently primary verb
σέβομαι.shortDef: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore:--devout, religious, worship.

glosses: probably from σύρω through its congener  (to fasten
σειρά.shortDef: probably from σύρω through its congener  (to fasten; akin to αἱρέομαι); a chain (as binding or drawing):--chain.

σεισμός.shortDef: from σείω; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake:--earthquake, tempest.

σείω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern):--move, quake, shake.

σεκοῦνδος.shortDef: of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian:--Secundus.

σελεύκεια.shortDef: from  (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria:--Seleucia.

σελήνη.shortDef: from  (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon:--moon.

glosses: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of σελήνη
σεληνιάζομαι.shortDef: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of σελήνη; to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy:--be a lunatic.

σεμεΐ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעִי); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite:--Semei.

σεμίδαλις.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour:--fine flour.

σεμνός.shortDef: from σέβομαι; venerable, i.e. honorable:--grave, honest.

σεμνότης.shortDef: from σεμνός; venerableness, i.e. probity:--gravity, honesty.

σέργιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman:--Sergius.

σήθ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁת); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch:--Seth.

σήμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁם); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch:-- Sem.

σημαίνω.shortDef: from  (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate:--signify.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of σημαίνω
σημεῖον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of σημαίνω; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally:--miracle, sign, token, wonder.

σημειόω.shortDef: from σημεῖον; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance):--note.

glosses: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ὁ  (t changed to s) and ἡμέρα
σήμερον.shortDef: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ὁ  (t changed to s) and ἡμέρα; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto):--this (to-)day.

σήπω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish:--be corrupted.

glosses: from  (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured
σηρικός.shortDef: from  (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric):--silk.

σής.shortDef: apparently of Hebrew origin (סָס); a moth:--moth.

glosses: from σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω
σητόβρωτος.shortDef: from σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; moth-eaten:--motheaten.

σθενόω.shortDef: from  (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of ἵστημι); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power):--strengthen.

σιαγών.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face:--cheek.

σιγάω.shortDef: from σιγή; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively):--keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.

σιγή.shortDef: apparently from  (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence:--silence. Compare σιωπάω.

σιδήρεος.shortDef: from σίδηρος; made of iron:--(of) iron.

σιδών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (צִידוֹן); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine:--Sidon.

σιδώνιος.shortDef: from Σιδών; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon:--of Sidon.

σικάριος.shortDef: of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans):--murderer. Compare φονεύς.

σίκερα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor:--strong drink.

σίλας.shortDef: contraction for Σιλουανός; Silas, a Christian:--Silas.

σιλουανός.shortDef: of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian:--Silvanus. Compare Σίλας.

σιλωάμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שִׁלֹחַ); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem:--Siloam.

σιμικίνθιον.shortDef: of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron):--apron.

σίμων.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעוֹן); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites:--Simon. Compare Συμεών.

σινᾶ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (סִינַי); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia:--Sina.

σίναπι.shortDef: perhaps from  (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant):--mustard.

σινδών.shortDef: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it):--(fine) linen (cloth).

σιτευτός.shortDef: from a derivative of σῖτος; grain-fed, i.e. fattened:--fatted.

σιτιστός.shortDef: from a derivative of σῖτος; grained, i.e. fatted:--fatling.

σιτόμετρον.shortDef: from σῖτος and μέτρον; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food):--portion of meat.

σῖτος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat:--corn, wheat.

σιών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (צִיּוֹן); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant):--Sion.

σιωπάω.shortDef: from  (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from σιγή, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water):--dumb, (hold) peace.

σκανδαλίζω.shortDef: from σκάνδαλον; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure):--(make to) offend.

σκάνδαλον.shortDef: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of κάμπτω; a  trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin):--occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.

σκάπτω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to dig:--dig.

σκέλος.shortDef: apparently from  (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank):--leg.

σκέπασμα.shortDef: from a derivative of  (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of σκοπός through the idea of noticeableness); clothing:--raiment.

σκευᾶς.shortDef: apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite:--Sceva.

σκευή.shortDef: from σκεῦος; furniture, i.e. spare tackle:--tackling.

σκεῦος.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]):--goods, sail, stuff, vessel.

glosses: apparently akin to σκεῦος and σκιά
σκηνή.shortDef: apparently akin to σκεῦος and σκιά; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively):--habitation, tabernacle.

σκηνοπηγία.shortDef: from σκῆνος and πήγνυμι; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes):--tabernacles.

σκηνοποιός.shortDef: from σκηνή and ποιέω; a manufacturer of tents:--tent-maker.

σκῆνος.shortDef: from σκηνή; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit):--tabernacle.

σκηνόω.shortDef: from σκῆνος; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion):-- dwell.

σκήνωμα.shortDef: from σκηνόω; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul):-- tabernacle.

σκιά.shortDef: apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)):-- shadow.

σκιρτάω.shortDef: akin to  (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus):--leap (for joy).

glosses: feminine of a compound of σκληρός and καρδία
σκληροκαρδία.shortDef: feminine of a compound of σκληρός and καρδία; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception:--hardness of heart.

σκληρός.shortDef: from the base of σκέλος; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe):--fierce, hard.

σκληροτράχηλος.shortDef: from σκληρός and τράχηλος; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate:--stiffnecked.

σκληρύνω.shortDef: from σκληρός; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn:--harden.

σκολιός.shortDef: from the base of σκέλος; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse:--crooked, froward, untoward.

glosses: perhaps from the base of σκέλος and ὀπτάνομαι
σκόλοψ.shortDef: perhaps from the base of σκέλος and ὀπτάνομαι; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability):--thorn.

σκοπέω.shortDef: from σκοπός; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard:--consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.

σκοπός.shortDef: from  (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to σκάπτω through the idea of concealment; compare σκέπασμα); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal:--mark.

glosses: apparently from the same as σκορπίος (through the idea of penetrating)
σκορπίζω.shortDef: apparently from the same as σκορπίος (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal:--disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).

glosses: probably from an obsolete  (perhaps strengthened from the base of σκοπός and meaning to pierce)
σκορπίος.shortDef: probably from an obsolete  (perhaps strengthened from the base of σκοπός and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting):--scorpion.

σκοτεινός.shortDef: from σκότος; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted:--dark, full of darkness.

σκοτία.shortDef: from σκότος; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively):--dark(-ness).

σκοτίζω.shortDef: from σκότος; to obscure (literally or figuratively):--darken.

σκότος.shortDef: from the base of σκιά; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively):--darkness.

σκοτόω.shortDef: from σκότος; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively):--be full of darkness.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of εἰς and κύων and βάλλω
σκύβαλον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of εἰς and κύων and βάλλω; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure):--dung.

σκύθης.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage:--Scythian.

glosses: from  (sullen) and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι
σκυθρωπός.shortDef: from  (sullen) and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance:--of a sad countenance.

σκύλλω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass:--trouble(self).

σκῦλον.shortDef: neuter from σκύλλω; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty:--spoil.

glosses: from σκώληξ and a derivative of βιβρώσκω
σκωληκόβρωτος.shortDef: from σκώληξ and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots:--eaten of worms.

σκώληξ.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm:--worm.

σμάραγδος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called:--emerald.

σμύρνα.shortDef: the same as σμύρνα; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor:--Smyrna.

σμυρνίζω.shortDef: from Σμύρνα; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic):--mingle with myrrh.

σόδομα.shortDef: plural of Hebrew origin (סְדֹם); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine:--Sodom.

σοί.shortDef: dative case of σύ; to thee:--thee, thine own, thou, thy.

σολομών.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שְׁלֹמֹה); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David:--Solomon.

glosses: probably akin to the base of σωρεύω
σορός.shortDef: probably akin to the base of σωρεύω; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier:--bier.

σοῦ.shortDef: genitive case of σύ; of thee, thy:--X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.

σουδάριον.shortDef: of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse):--handkerchief, napkin.

σουσάννα.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שׁוּשַׁן feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess:--Susanna.

σοφία.shortDef: from σοφός; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual):--wisdom.

σοφίζω.shortDef: from σοφός; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error:--cunningly devised, make wise.

σοφός.shortDef: akin to  (clear); wise (in a most general application):--wise. Compare φρόνιμος.

σπανία.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe:--Spain.

σπαράσσω.shortDef: prolongation from  (to grasp; apparently strengthened from σπάω through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy:--rend, tear.

σπαργανόω.shortDef: from  (a strip; from a derivative of the base of σπαράσσω meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom):--wrap in swaddling clothes.

σπαταλάω.shortDef: from  (luxury); to be voluptuous:--live in pleasure, be wanton.

σπεῖρα.shortDef: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of αἱρέομαι in the sense of its cognate εἱλίσσω; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors):--band.

glosses: probably strengthened from σπάω (through the idea of extending)
σπείρω.shortDef: probably strengthened from σπάω (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively):--sow(- er), receive seed.

σπεκουλάτωρ.shortDef: of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman):--executioner.

σπένδω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"):--(be ready to) be offered.

σπέρμα.shortDef: from σπείρω; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting):--issue, seed.

σπερμολόγος.shortDef: from σπέρμα and λέγω; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk):--babbler.

σπεύδω.shortDef: probably strengthened from πούς; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly:--(make, with) haste unto.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a grotto)
σπήλαιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort:--cave, den.

σπιλάς.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea:--spot (by confusion with σπίλος).

σπιλόω.shortDef: from σπίλος; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively):--defile, spot.

σπίλος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace:--spot.

σπλαγχνίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from σπλάγχνον; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity:--have (be moved with) compassion.

σπλάγχνον.shortDef: probably strengthened from  (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy:--bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.

σπορά.shortDef: from σπείρω; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage:--seed.

σπόριμος.shortDef: from σπόρος; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field:--corn(-field).

σπόρος.shortDef: from σπείρω; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown):--seed (X sown).

σπουδάζω.shortDef: from σπουδή; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest:--do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.

σπουδαιότερον.shortDef: neuter of σπουδαιότερος as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly:--very diligently.

σπουδαιότερος.shortDef: comparative of σπουδαῖος; more prompt, more earnest:--more diligent (forward).

σπουδαιοτέρως.shortDef: adverb from σπουδαιότερος; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise:--more carefully.

σπουδαίως.shortDef: adverb from σπουδαῖος; earnestly, promptly:--diligently, instantly.

σπουδή.shortDef: from σπεύδω; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness:--business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste.

σπυρίς.shortDef: from σπείρω (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle:--basket.

glosses: from the base of ἵστημι (as fixed)
στάδιον.shortDef: from the base of ἵστημι (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course:--furlong, race.

glosses: from the base of ἵστημι (as stationary)
στάμνος.shortDef: from the base of ἵστημι (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank:--pot.

στάσις.shortDef: from the base of ἵστημι; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy:--dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.

στατήρ.shortDef: from the base of καύχησις; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin:--piece of money.

σταυρός.shortDef: from the base of ἵστημι; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ:--cross.

σταυρόω.shortDef: from σταυρός; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness:--crucify.

glosses: probably from the base of στέφανος
σταφυλή.shortDef: probably from the base of στέφανος; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined):--grapes.

στάχυς.shortDef: the same as στάχυς; Stachys, a Christian:--Stachys.

glosses: strengthened from a primary  (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building)
στέγη.shortDef: strengthened from a primary  (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof:--roof.

στέγω.shortDef: from στέγη; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently):--(for-)bear, suffer.

glosses: a contraction from στερεός (as stiff and unnatural)
στείρος.shortDef: a contraction from στερεός (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile":--barren.

glosses: probably strengthened from the base of ἵστημι
στέλλω.shortDef: probably strengthened from the base of ἵστημι; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with):--avoid, withdraw self.

στέμμα.shortDef: from the base of στέφανος; a wreath for show:--garland.

στενάζω.shortDef: from στενός; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly:--with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.

glosses: probably from the base of ἵστημι
στενός.shortDef: probably from the base of ἵστημι; narrow (from obstacles standing close about):--strait.

στενοχωρέω.shortDef: from the same as στενοχωρία; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp:--distress, straiten.

glosses: from a compound of στενός and χώρα
στενοχωρία.shortDef: from a compound of στενός and χώρα; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity:--anguish, distress.

στερεός.shortDef: from ἵστημι; stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively):--stedfast, strong, sure.

στερεόω.shortDef: from στερεός; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively):--establish, receive strength, make strong.

στερέωμα.shortDef: from στερεόω; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability):--stedfastness.

στεφανᾶς.shortDef: probably contraction for  (crowned; from στεφανόω); Stephanas, a Christian:--Stephanas.

στέφανος.shortDef: the same as στέφανος; Stephanus, a Christian:--Stephen.

στεφανόω.shortDef: from στέφανος; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively):--crown.

στῆθος.shortDef: from ἵστημι (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest:--breast.

glosses: from the perfect tense of ἵστημι
στήκω.shortDef: from the perfect tense of ἵστημι; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere:--stand (fast).

glosses: from a presumed derivative of ἵστημι (like στερεός)
στηρίζω.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of ἵστημι (like στερεός); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm:--fix, (e-)stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.

στίγμα.shortDef: from a primary  (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service:--mark.

στιγμή.shortDef: feminine of στίγμα; a point of time, i.e. an instant:--moment.

στίλβω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. flash intensely:--shining.

στοά.shortDef: probably from ἵστημι; a colonnade or interior piazza:--porch.

στοιβάς.shortDef: from a primary  (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed:--branch.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of στοιχέω
στοιχεῖον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of στοιχέω; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively):--element, principle, rudiment.

glosses: from a derivative of  (to range in regular line)
στοιχέω.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety:--walk (orderly).

στολή.shortDef: from στέλλω; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity):--long clothing (garment), (long) robe.

glosses: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of τομώτερος
στόμα.shortDef: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of τομώτερος; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon):--edge, face, mouth.

στόμαχος.shortDef: from στόμα; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach":--stomach.

στρατεία.shortDef: from στρατεύομαι; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger):--warfare.

στράτευμα.shortDef: from στρατεύομαι; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic):--army, soldier, man of war.

glosses: middle voice from the base of στρατιά
στρατεύομαι.shortDef: middle voice from the base of στρατιά; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations:--soldier, (go to) war(-fare).

glosses: from the base of στρατιά and ἄγω or ἡγέομαι
στρατηγός.shortDef: from the base of στρατιά and ἄγω or ἡγέομαι; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens:--captain, magistrate.

glosses: feminine of a derivative of  (an army
στρατιά.shortDef: feminine of a derivative of  (an army; from the base of στρώννυμι, as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries:--host.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of the same as στρατιά
στρατιώτης.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of the same as στρατιά; a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively):--soldier.

glosses: from a compound of the base of στρατιά and λέγω (in its original sense)
στρατολογέω.shortDef: from a compound of the base of στρατιά and λέγω (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army:--choose to be a soldier.

στρατοπεδάρχης.shortDef: from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Prætorian præfect:--captain of the guard.

glosses: from the base of στρατιά and the same as πεδινός
στρατόπεδον.shortDef: from the base of στρατιά and the same as πεδινός; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops:--army.

στρεβλόω.shortDef: from a derivative of στρέφω; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert:-- wrest.

glosses: strengthened from the base of τροπή
στρέφω.shortDef: strengthened from the base of τροπή; to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively):--convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).

glosses: from a presumed derivative of στρῆνος
στρηνιάω.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of στρῆνος; to be luxurious:--live deliciously.

στρῆνος.shortDef: akin to στερεός; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness):--delicacy.

στρουθίον.shortDef: diminutive of  (a sparrow); a little sparrow:--sparrow.

στρώννυμι.shortDef: prolongation from a still simpler        , (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to στερεός through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch):--make bed, furnish, spread, strew.

glosses: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary  (to hate)
στυγνητός.shortDef: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary  (to hate); hated, i.e. odious:--hateful.

στυγνάζω.shortDef: from the same as στυγνητός; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech):--lower, be sad.

στῦλος.shortDef: from  (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of ἵστημι); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support:--pillar.

στωϊκός.shortDef: from στοά; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy:--Stoick.

glosses: the personal pronoun of the second person singular
σύ.shortDef: the personal pronoun of the second person singular; thou:-- thou. See also σέ, σοί, σοῦ; and for the plural ὑμᾶς, ὑμεῖς, ὑμῖν, ὑμῶν.

συγγενής.shortDef: from σύν and γένος; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman:--cousin, kin(-sfolk, -sman).

glosses: from a compound of σύν and γινώσκω
συγγνώμη.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and γινώσκω; fellow knowledge, i.e. concession:--permission.

συγκάθημαι.shortDef: from σύν and κάθημαι; to seat oneself in company with:--sit with.

συγκαθίζω.shortDef: from σύν and καθίζω; to give (or take) a seat in company with:--(make) sit (down) together.

συγκακοπαθέω.shortDef: from σύν and κακοπαθέω; to suffer hardship in company with:--be partaker of afflictions.

συγκακουχέω.shortDef: from σύν and κακουχέω; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together:--suffer affliction with.

συγκαλέω.shortDef: from σύν and καλέω; to convoke:--call together.

συγκαλύπτω.shortDef: from σύν and καλύπτω; to conceal altogether:--cover.

συγκάμπτω.shortDef: from σύν and κάμπτω; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict:--bow down.

συγκαταβαίνω.shortDef: from σύν and καταβαίνω; to descend in company with:--go down with.

συγκατάθεσις.shortDef: from συγκατατίθεμαι; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with:--agreement.

συγκατατίθεμαι.shortDef: middle from σύν and κατατίθημι; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with:--consent.

glosses: from σύν and a compound of κατά and ψηφίζω
συγκαταψηφίζω.shortDef: from σύν and a compound of κατά and ψηφίζω; to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among:--number with.

συγκεράννυμι.shortDef: from σύν and κεράννυμι; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate:--mix with, temper together.

συγκινέω.shortDef: from σπαράσσω and κινέω; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition):--stir up.

συγκλείω.shortDef: from σύν and κλείω; to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to:--conclude, inclose, shut up.

συγκληρονόμος.shortDef: from σύν and κληρονόμος; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common:--fellow (joint)-heir, heir together, heir with.

συγκοινωνέω.shortDef: from σύν and κοινωνέω; to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in:--communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.

συγκοινωνός.shortDef: from σύν and κοινωνός; a co-participant:--companion, partake(-r, -r with).

συγκομίζω.shortDef: from σύν and κομίζω; to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others:--carry.

συγκρίνω.shortDef: from σύν and κρίνω; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance):--compare among (with).

συγκύπτω.shortDef: from σύν and κύπτω; to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by:--bow together.

glosses: from a comparative of σύν and  (to light or happen
συγκυρία.shortDef: from a comparative of σύν and  (to light or happen; from the base of κύριος); concurrence, i.e. accident:--chance.

συγχαίρω.shortDef: from σύν and χαίρω; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate:--rejoice in (with).

glosses: from σύν and  (to pour) or its alternate
συγχέω.shortDef: from σύν and  (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind):--confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.

συγχράομαι.shortDef: from σύν and χράομαι; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common:--have dealings with.

σύγχυσις.shortDef: from συγχέω; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance:--confusion.

συζάω.shortDef: from σύν and ζάω; to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively):--live with.

glosses: from σύν and the base of ζεῦγος
συζεύγνυμι.shortDef: from σύν and the base of ζεῦγος; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage):--join together.

συζητέω.shortDef: from σύν and ζητέω; to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil:--dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).

συζήτησις.shortDef: from συζητέω; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion:--disputation(-ting), reasoning.

συζητητής.shortDef: from συζητέω; a disputant, i.e. sophist:--disputer.

σύζυγος.shortDef: from συζεύγνυμι; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian:--yokefellow.

συζωοποιέω.shortDef: from σύν and ζωοποιέω; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively):--quicken together with.

glosses: of Hebrew origin (שִׁקְמָה) in imitation of συκομωραία
συκάμινος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שִׁקְמָה) in imitation of συκομωραία; a sycamore-fig tree:--sycamine tree.

συκομωραία.shortDef: from σῦκον and  (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree:--sycamore tree. Compare συκάμινος.

σῦκον.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a fig:--fig.

glosses: from a compound of σῦκον and a derivative of φαίνω
συκοφαντέω.shortDef: from a compound of σῦκον and a derivative of φαίνω; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort):--accuse falsely, take by false accusation.

glosses: from the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω
συλαγωγέω.shortDef: from the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce:--spoil.

συλάω.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to strip; probably akin to αἱρέομαι; compare σκῦλον); to despoil:--rob.

συλλαλέω.shortDef: from σύν and λαλέω; to talk together, i.e. converse:--commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.

συλλαμβάνω.shortDef: from σύν and λαμβάνω; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid:--catch, conceive, help, take.

glosses: from σύν and λέγω in its original sense
συλλέγω.shortDef: from σύν and λέγω in its original sense; to collect:--gather (together, up).

συλλογίζομαι.shortDef: from σύν and λογίζομαι; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate:--reason with.

συλλυπέω.shortDef: from σύν and λυπέω; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone:--be grieved.

glosses: from σύν and the base of βάσις
συμβαίνω.shortDef: from σύν and the base of βάσις; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place):--be(-fall), happen (unto).

συμβάλλω.shortDef: from σύν and βάλλω; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack:--confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.

συμβασιλεύω.shortDef: from σύν and βασιλεύω; to be co-regent (figuratively):--reign with.

συμβιβάζω.shortDef: from σύν and  (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of βάσις); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach:--compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.

συμβουλεύω.shortDef: from σύν and βουλεύω; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine:--consult, (give, take) counsel (together).

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος
συμβούλιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court:--consultation, counsel, council.

σύμβουλος.shortDef: from σύν and βουλή; a consultor, i.e. adviser:--counsellor.

συμεών.shortDef: from the same as Σίμων; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites:--Simeon, Simon.

glosses: from a compound of σύν and μανθάνω
συμμαθητής.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and μανθάνω; a co-learner (of Christianity):--fellow disciple.

συμμαρτυρέω.shortDef: from σύν and μαρτυρέω; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence:--testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).

glosses: middle voice from σύν and μερίζω
συμμερίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from σύν and μερίζω; to share jointly, i.e. participate in:--be partaker with.

συμμέτοχος.shortDef: from σύν and μέτοχος; a co-participant:--partaker.

glosses: from a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι
συμμιμητής.shortDef: from a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary:--follower together.

σύμμορφος.shortDef: from σύν and μορφή; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar:--conformed to, fashioned like unto.

συμμορφόω.shortDef: from σύμμορφος; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate:--make conformable unto.

συμπαθέω.shortDef: from συμπαθής; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate:--have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.

συμπαθής.shortDef: from συμπάσχω; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative:--having compassion one of another.

συμπαραγίνομαι.shortDef: from σύν and παραγίνομαι; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid:--come together, stand with.

συμπαρακαλέω.shortDef: from σύν and παρακαλέω; to console jointly:--comfort together.

συμπαραλαμβάνω.shortDef: from σύν and παραλαμβάνω; to take along in company:--take with.

συμπαραμένω.shortDef: from σύν and παραμένω; to remain in company, i.e. still live:--continue with.

συμπάρειμι.shortDef: from σύν and πάρειμι; to be at hand together, i.e. now present:--be here present with.

glosses: from σύν and πάσχω (including its alternate)
συμπάσχω.shortDef: from σύν and πάσχω (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize"):--suffer with.

συμπέμπω.shortDef: from σύν and πέμπω; to despatch in company:--send with.

glosses: from σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω
συμπεριλαμβάνω.shortDef: from σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one:--embrace.

συμπίνω.shortDef: from σύν and πίνω; to partake a beverage in company:--drink with.

συμπληρόω.shortDef: from σύν and πληρόω; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete):--(fully) come, fill up.

συμπνίγω.shortDef: from σύν and πνίγω; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd:--choke, throng.

συμπολίτης.shortDef: from σύν and πολίτης; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian):--fellow- citizen.

συμπορεύομαι.shortDef: from σύν and πορεύομαι; to journey together; by implication, to assemble:--go with, resort.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω
συμπόσιον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests:--company.

συμπρεσβύτερος.shortDef: from σύν and πρεσβύτερος; a co-presbyter:--presbyter, also an elder.

glosses: from σύν and φέρω (including its alternate)
συμφέρω.shortDef: from σύν and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage:--be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).

σύμφημι.shortDef: from σύν and φημί; to say jointly, i.e. assent to:--consent unto.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of φυλή
συμφυλέτης.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of φυλή; a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country:--countryman.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of φύω
σύμφυτος.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of φύω; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to:--planted together.

συμφύω.shortDef: from σύν and φύω; passive, to grow jointly:--spring up with.

συμφωνέω.shortDef: from σύμφωνος; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact):--agree (together, with).

συμφωνία.shortDef: from σύμφωνος; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note):--music.

σύμφωνος.shortDef: from σύν and φωνή; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement):-- consent.

συμψηφίζω.shortDef: from σύν and ψηφίζω; to compute jointly:--reckon.

σύμψυχος.shortDef: from σύν and ψυχή; co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment:--like-minded.

σύν.shortDef: a primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than μετά or παρά), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.:--beside, with. In composition it has similar applications, including completeness.

συνάγω.shortDef: from σύν and ἄγω; to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably):--+ accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.

συναγωγή.shortDef: from (the reduplicated form of) συνάγω; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church:--assembly, congregation, synagogue.

συναγωνίζομαι.shortDef: from σύν and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant):--strive together with.

συναθλέω.shortDef: from σύν and ἀθλέω; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly:--labour with, strive together for.

συναθροίζω.shortDef: from σύν and  (to hoard); to convene:--call (gather) together.

συναίρω.shortDef: from σύν and αἴρω; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account):--reckon, take.

συναιχμάλωτος.shortDef: from σύν and αἰχμάλωτος; a co-captive:--fellowprisoner.

συνακολουθέω.shortDef: from σύν and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany:--follow.

συναλίζω.shortDef: from σύν and  (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene:--assemble together.

συναναβαίνω.shortDef: from σύν and ἀναβαίνω; to ascend in company with:--come up with.

συνανάκειμαι.shortDef: from σύν and ἀνακεῖμαι; to recline in company with (at a meal):--sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).

glosses: from σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι
συναναμίγνυμι.shortDef: from σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with:--(have, keep) company (with).

συναναπαύομαι.shortDef: middle from σύν and ἀναπαύω; to recruit oneself in company with:--refresh with.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of ἀντί
συναντάω.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet with; figuratively, to occur:--befall, meet.

συναντιλαμβάνομαι.shortDef: from σύν and ἀντιλαμβάνομαι; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist):--help.

συναπάγω.shortDef: from σύν and ἀπάγω; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield):--carry (lead) away with, condescend.

συναποθνήσκω.shortDef: from σύν and ἀποθνήσκω; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to:--be dead (die) with.

συναπόλλυμι.shortDef: from σύν and ἀπόλλυμι; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with:--perish with.

συναποστέλλω.shortDef: from σύν and ἀποστέλλω; to despatch (on an errand) in company with:--send with.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ἁρμός and λέγω (in its original sense of laying)
συναρμολογέω.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ἁρμός and λέγω (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly:--be fitly framed (joined) together.

συναρπάζω.shortDef: from σύν and ἁρπάζω; to snatch together, i.e. seize:--catch.

συναυξάνω.shortDef: from σύν and αὐξάνω; to increase (grow up) together:--grow together.

σύνδεσμος.shortDef: from σύν and δεσμόν; a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control:--band, bond.

συνδέω.shortDef: from σύν and δέω; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively):--be bound with.

συνδοξάζω.shortDef: from σύν and δοξάζω; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with:--glorify together.

σύνδουλος.shortDef: from σύν and δοῦλος; a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine):--fellowservant.

συνδρομή.shortDef: from (the alternate of) συντρέχω; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse:--run together.

συνεγείρω.shortDef: from σύν and ἐγείρω; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to:--raise up together, rise with.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of σύν and the base of ἑδραῖος
συνέδριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of σύν and the base of ἑδραῖος; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal:--council.

glosses: from a prolonged form of συνείδω
συνείδησις.shortDef: from a prolonged form of συνείδω; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness:--conscience.

συνείδω.shortDef: from σύν and εἴδω; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of:--consider, know, be privy, be ware of.

σύνειμι.shortDef: from σύν and  (to go); to assemble:--gather together.

συνεισέρχομαι.shortDef: from σύν and εἰσέρχομαι; to enter in company with:--go in with, go with into.

glosses: from σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω
συνέκδημος.shortDef: from σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller:--companion in travel, travel with.

glosses: from a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι
συνεκλεκτός.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι; chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian):--elected together with.

συνελαύνω.shortDef: from σύν and ἐλαύνω; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation):--+ set at one again.

συνεπιμαρτυρέω.shortDef: from σύν and ἐπιμαρτυρέω; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence:--also bear witness.

glosses: middle voice from σύν and a primary  (to follow)
συνέπομαι.shortDef: middle voice from σύν and a primary  (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with:--accompany.

συνεργέω.shortDef: from συνεργός; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate:--help (work) with, work(-er) together.

glosses: from a presumed compound of σύν and the base of ἔργον
συνεργός.shortDef: from a presumed compound of σύν and the base of ἔργον; a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor:--companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.

συνέρχομαι.shortDef: from σύν and ἔρχομαι; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally):--accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.

glosses: from σύν and ἐσθίω (including its alternate)
συνεσθίω.shortDef: from σύν and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to take food in company with:--eat with.

σύνεσις.shortDef: from συνίημι; a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect:--knowledge, understanding.

συνετός.shortDef: from συνίημι; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious:--prudent. Compare φρόνιμος.

συνευδοκέω.shortDef: from σύν and εὐδοκέω; to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with:--allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of a presumed compound of εὖ and a derivative of ἔχω (meaning to be in good condition
συνευωχέω.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of a presumed compound of εὖ and a derivative of ἔχω (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together:--feast with.

συνεφίστημι.shortDef: from σύν and ἐφίστημι; to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly:--rise up together.

συνέχω.shortDef: from σύν and ἔχω; to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy:--constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.

glosses: middle voice from σύν and the base of ἡδονή
συνήδομαι.shortDef: middle voice from σύν and the base of ἡδονή; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning:--delight.

glosses: from a compound of σύν and ἦθος
συνήθεια.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and ἦθος; mutual habituation, i.e. usage:--custom.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of ἡλικία
συνηλικιώτης.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of ἡλικία; a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years:--equal.

συνθάπτω.shortDef: from σύν and θάπτω; to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin):--bury with.

συνθλάω.shortDef: from σύν and thlao (to crush); to dash together, i.e. shatter:--break.

συνθλίβω.shortDef: from σύν and θλίβω; to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides:--throng.

συνθρύπτω.shortDef: from σύν and  (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit:--break.

συνίημι.shortDef: from σύν and  (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously:-- consider, understand, be wise.

glosses: from σύν and ἵστημι (including its collateral forms)
συνιστάω.shortDef: from σύν and ἵστημι (including its collateral forms); to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute:--approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with).

συνοδεύω.shortDef: from σύν and ὁδεύω; to travel in company with:--journey with.

glosses: from a compound of σύν and ὁδός ("synod")
συνοδία.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and ὁδός ("synod"); companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan:--company.

συνοικέω.shortDef: from σύν and οἰκέω; to reside together (as a family):--dwell together.

συνοικοδομέω.shortDef: from σύν and οἰκοδομέω; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively):--build together.

συνομιλέω.shortDef: from σύν and ὁμιλέω; to converse mutually:--talk with.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of ὅριον
συνομορέω.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of ὅριον; to border together, i.e. adjoin:--join hard.

συνοχή.shortDef: from συνέχω; restraint, i.e. (figuratively) anxiety:--anguish, distress.

συντάσσω.shortDef: from σύν and τάσσω; to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct:--appoint.

συντέλεια.shortDef: from συντελέω; entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation):--end.

συντελέω.shortDef: from σύν and τελέω; to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively):--end, finish, fulfil, make.

glosses: from σύν and the base of τομώτερος
συντέμνω.shortDef: from σύν and the base of τομώτερος; to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily):--(cut) short.

συντηρέω.shortDef: from σύν and τηρέω; to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey):--keep, observe, preserve.

glosses: middle voice from σύν and τίθημι
συντίθεμαι.shortDef: middle voice from σύν and τίθημι; to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur:--agree, assent, covenant.

glosses: adverb from a derivative of συντέμνω
συντόμως.shortDef: adverb from a derivative of συντέμνω; concisely (briefly):--a few words.

glosses: from σύν and τρέχω (including its alternate)
συντρέχω.shortDef: from σύν and τρέχω (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively):--run (together, with).

glosses: from σύν and the base of τρίβος
συντρίβω.shortDef: from σύν and the base of τρίβος; to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively):--break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.

σύντριμμα.shortDef: from συντρίβω; concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin:--destruction.

glosses: from σύν and τροφός (in a passive sense)
σύντροφος.shortDef: from σύν and τροφός (in a passive sense); a fellow-nursling, i.e. comrade:--brought up with.

συντυγχάνω.shortDef: from σύν and τυγχάνω; to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach):--come at.

συντύχη.shortDef: from συντυγχάνω; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female:--Syntyche.

συνυποκρίνομαι.shortDef: from σύν and ὑποκρίνομαι; to act hypocritically in concert with:--dissemble with.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ὑπό and the base of ἔργον
συνυπουργέω.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ὑπό and the base of ἔργον; to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist:--help together.

συνωδίνω.shortDef: from σύν and ὠδίνω; to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering):--travail in pain together.

glosses: from a compound of σύν and ὀμνύω
συνωμοσία.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and ὀμνύω; a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot:--comspiracy.

συράκουσαι.shortDef: plural of uncertain derivation; Syracuse, the capital of Sicily:--Syracuse.

συρία.shortDef: probably of Hebrew origin (צֹר); Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia:--Syria.

σύρος.shortDef: from the same as Συρία; a Syran (i.e. probably Tyrian), a native of Syria:--Syrian.

glosses: feminine of a compound of Σύρος and the same as Φοινίκη
συροφοίνισσα.shortDef: feminine of a compound of Σύρος and the same as Φοινίκη; a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria:--Syrophenician.

σύρτις.shortDef: from σύρω; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa:--quicksands.

σύρω.shortDef: probably akin to αἱρέομαι; to trail:--drag, draw, hale.

συσπαράσσω.shortDef: from σύν and σπαράσσω; to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently:--throw down.

glosses: neuter of a compound of σύν and the base of σημαίνω
σύσσημον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of σύν and the base of σημαίνω; a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal:--token.

σύσσωμος.shortDef: from σύν and σῶμα; of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community:--of the same body.

glosses: from a compound of σύν and a derivative of στάσις
συστασιαστής.shortDef: from a compound of σύν and a derivative of στάσις; a fellow-insurgent:--make insurrection with.

συστατικός.shortDef: from a derivative of συνιστάω; introductory, i.e. recommendatory:--of commendation.

συσταυρόω.shortDef: from σύν and σταυρόω; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively):--crucify with.

συστέλλω.shortDef: from σύν and στέλλω; to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval):-- short, wind up.

συστενάζω.shortDef: from σύν and στενάζω; to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity:--groan together.

συστοιχέω.shortDef: from σύν and στοιχέω; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to:--answer to.

συστρατιώτης.shortDef: from σύν and στρατιώτης; a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil:--fellowsoldier.

συστρέφω.shortDef: from σύν and στρέφω; to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd):--gather.

συστροφή.shortDef: from συστρέφω; a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd:--+ band together, concourse.

glosses: from σύν and a derivative of σχῆμα
συσχηματίζω.shortDef: from σύν and a derivative of σχῆμα; to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively):--conform to, fashion self according to.

συχάρ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine:--Sychar.

συχέμ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (שְׁכֶם); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine:--Sychem.

σφαγή.shortDef: from σφάζω; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)):--slaughter.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of σφαγή
σφάγιον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of σφαγή; a victim (in sacrifice):--slain beast.

σφάζω.shortDef: a primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently):--kill, slay, wound.

σφόδρα.shortDef: neuter plural of  (violent; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. in a high degree, much:-- exceeding(-ly), greatly, sore, very.

glosses: adverb from the same as σφόδρα
σφοδρῶς.shortDef: adverb from the same as σφόδρα; very much:--exceedingly.

σφραγίζω.shortDef: from σφραγίς; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest:--(set a, set to) seal up, stop.

σφραγίς.shortDef: probably strengthened from φράσσω; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively:--seal.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as  (a ball
σφυρόν.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as  (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine , a hammer); the ankle (as globular):--ancle bone.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω as adverb
σχεδόν.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω as adverb; nigh, i.e. nearly:--almost.

σχῆμα.shortDef: from the alternate of ἔχω; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition:--fashion.

σχίζω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively):--break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.

σχίσμα.shortDef: from σχίζω; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively:--division, rent, schism.

σχοινίον.shortDef: diminutive of  (a rush or flag-plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally):--small cord, rope.

σχολάζω.shortDef: from σχολή; to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house):--empty, give self.

glosses: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω
σχολή.shortDef: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω; properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment):--school.

σώζω.shortDef: from a primary  (contraction for obsolete , "safe"); to save, i.e. deliver or protect (literally or figuratively):--heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.

σῶμα.shortDef: from σώζω; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively:--bodily, body, slave.

σωματικῶς.shortDef: adverb from σωματικός; corporeally or physically:--bodily.

glosses: from the base of σώζω and πατήρ
σώπατρος.shortDef: from the base of σώζω and πατήρ; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian:--Sopater. Compare Σωσίπατρος.

σωρεύω.shortDef: from another form of σορός; to pile up (literally or figuratively):--heap, load.

glosses: from the base of σώζω and that of σθενόω
σωσθένης.shortDef: from the base of σώζω and that of σθενόω; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian:--Sosthenes.

σωσίπατρος.shortDef: prolongation for Σώπατρος; Sosipatrus, a Christian:--Sosipater.

σωτήρ.shortDef: from σώζω; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ:--saviour.

glosses: feminine of a derivative of σωτήρ as (properly
σωτηρία.shortDef: feminine of a derivative of σωτήρ as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally):--deliver, health, salvation, save, saving.

glosses: neuter of the same as σωτηρία as (properly
σωτήριον.shortDef: neuter of the same as σωτηρία as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence:--salvation.

σωφρονέω.shortDef: from σώφρων; to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate:--be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.

σωφρονίζω.shortDef: from σώφρων; to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct:--teach to be sober.

σωφρονισμός.shortDef: from σωφρονίζω; discipline, i.e. self-control:--sound mind.

σωφρόνως.shortDef: adverb from σώφρων; with sound mind, i.e. moderately:--soberly.

σωφροσύνη.shortDef: from σώφρων; soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control:--soberness, sobriety.

glosses: from the base of σώζω and that of φρήν
σώφρων.shortDef: from the base of σώζω and that of φρήν; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion):--discreet, sober, temperate.

ταβέρναι.shortDef: plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ:--taverns.

ταβιθά.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (compare צְבִיָּה); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female:--Tabitha.

τάγμα.shortDef: from τάσσω; something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession:--order.

τακτός.shortDef: from τάσσω; arranged, i.e. appointed or stated:--set.

ταλαιπωρέω.shortDef: from ταλαίπωρος; to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery:--be afflicted.

glosses: from the base of τάλαντον and a derivative of the base of πεῖρα
ταλαίπωρος.shortDef: from the base of τάλαντον and a derivative of the base of πεῖρα; enduring trial, i.e. miserable:--wretched.

ταλαντιαῖος.shortDef: from τάλαντον; talent-like in weight:--weight of a talent.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of  (to bear
τάλαντον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of  (to bear; equivalent to φέρω); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent":--talent.

ταλιθά.shortDef: of Chaldee origin (compare טָלֶה); the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden):--talitha.

glosses: neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of  (a dispenser or distributor
ταμεῖον.shortDef: neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of  (a dispenser or distributor; akin to , to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. a chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement):--secret chamber, closet, storehouse.

τάξις.shortDef: from τάσσω; regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity:--order.

ταπεινός.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition):--base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly.

glosses: from a compound of ταπεινός and the base of φρήν
ταπεινοφροσύνη.shortDef: from a compound of ταπεινός and the base of φρήν; humiliation of mind, i.e. modesty:--humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind).

ταπεινόω.shortDef: from ταπεινός; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart):--abase, bring low, humble (self).

ταπείνωσις.shortDef: from ταπεινόω; depression (in rank or feeling):--humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile.

ταράσσω.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate (roil water):--trouble.

ταραχή.shortDef: feminine from ταράσσω; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition:--trouble(-ing).

τάραχος.shortDef: masculine from ταράσσω; a disturbance, i.e. (popular) tumult:--stir.

ταρσεύς.shortDef: from Ταρσός; a Tarsean, i.e. native of Tarsus:--of Tarsus.

glosses: perhaps the same as  (a flat basket)
ταρσός.shortDef: perhaps the same as  (a flat basket); Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor:--Tarsus.

ταρταρόω.shortDef: from  (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment:--cast down to hell.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses)
τάσσω.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot):--addict, appoint, determine, ordain, set.

ταῦρος.shortDef: apparently a primary word (compare תּוֹר, "steer"); a bullock:--bull, ox.

glosses: nominative or accusative case neuter plural of οὗτος
ταῦτα.shortDef: nominative or accusative case neuter plural of οὗτος; these things:--+ afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus.

glosses: neuter plural of ὁ and αὐτός as adverb
ταὐτά.shortDef: neuter plural of ὁ and αὐτός as adverb; in the same way:--even thus, (manner) like, so.

glosses: dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of οὗτος
ταύταις.shortDef: dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of οὗτος; (to or with or by, etc.) these:--hence, that, then, these, those.

ταύτῃ.shortDef: dative case, accusative case and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of οὗτος; (towards or of) this:--her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same).

ταφή.shortDef: feminine from θάπτω; burial (the act):--X bury.

τάφος.shortDef: masculine from θάπτω; a grave (the place of interment):--sepulchre, tomb.

glosses: as if neuter plural of ταχύς (adverbially)
τάχα.shortDef: as if neuter plural of ταχύς (adverbially); shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly:--peradventure(-haps).

ταχέως.shortDef: adverb from ταχύς; briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly:--hastily, quickly, shortly, soon, suddenly.

ταχινός.shortDef: from τάχος; curt, i.e. impending:--shortly, swift.

glosses: neuter singular of the comparative of ταχύς (as adverb)
τάχιον.shortDef: neuter singular of the comparative of ταχύς (as adverb); more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily:--out (run), quickly, shortly, sooner.

glosses: neuter plural of the superlative of ταχύς (as adverb)
τάχιστα.shortDef: neuter plural of the superlative of ταχύς (as adverb); most quickly, i.e. (with ὡς prefixed) as soon as possible:--+ with all speed.

τάχος.shortDef: from the same as ταχύς; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with ἐν prefixed) in haste:--+ quickly, + shortly, + speedily.

ταχύ.shortDef: neuter singular of ταχύς (as adverb); shortly, i.e. without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily:--lightly, quickly.

ταχύς.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready:--swift.

glosses: a primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition
τέ.shortDef: a primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly, as correlation of καί):--also, and, both, even, then, whether. Often used in composition, usually as the latter participle.

glosses: akin to the base of τίκτω
τεῖχος.shortDef: akin to the base of τίκτω; a wall (as formative of a house):--wall.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a goal or fixed limit)
τεκμήριον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), i.e. criterion of certainty:--infallible proof.

τεκνίον.shortDef: diminutive of τέκνον; an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts):--little children.

glosses: from a compound of τέκνον and the base of γίνομαι
τεκνογονέω.shortDef: from a compound of τέκνον and the base of γίνομαι; to be a child-bearer, i.e. parent (mother):--bear children.

τεκνογονία.shortDef: from the same as τεκνογονέω; childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties):--childbearing.

τέκνον.shortDef: from the base of τίκτω; a child (as produced):--child, daughter, son.

glosses: from a compound of τέκνον and τρέφω
τεκνοτροφέω.shortDef: from a compound of τέκνον and τρέφω; to be a childrearer, i.e. fulfil the duties of a female parent:--bring up children.

τέκτων.shortDef: from the base of τιμωρία; an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood:--carpenter.

τέλειος.shortDef: from τέλος; complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with ὁ) completeness:--of full age, man, perfect.

τελειότης.shortDef: from τέλειος; (the state) completeness (mentally or morally):--perfection(-ness).

τελειόω.shortDef: from τέλειος; to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character):--consecrate, finish, fulfil, make) perfect.

τελείως.shortDef: adverb from τέλειος; completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering:--to the end.

τελείωσις.shortDef: from φυσιόω; (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution:--perfection, performance.

τελειωτής.shortDef: from τελειόω; a completer, i.e. consummater:--finisher.

glosses: from a compound of τέλος and φέρω
τελεσφορέω.shortDef: from a compound of τέλος and φέρω; to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. to ripen fruit (figuratively):--bring fruit to perfection.

glosses: from a presumed derivative of τελέω
τελευτάω.shortDef: from a presumed derivative of τελέω; to finish life (by implication, of βίος), i.e. expire (demise):--be dead, decease, die.

τελέω.shortDef: from τέλος; to end, i.e. complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt):--accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform.

glosses: from a primary  (to set out for a definite point or goal)
τέλος.shortDef: from a primary  (to set out for a definite point or goal); properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic), purpose); specially, an impost or levy (as paid):--+ continual, custom, end(-ing), finally, uttermost. Compare φόρος.

τελώνης.shortDef: from τέλος and ὠνέομαι; a tax-farmer, i.e. collector of public revenue:--publican.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of τελώνης
τελώνιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of τελώνης; a tax-gatherer's place of business:--receipt of custom.

τέρας.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen:--wonder.

τέρτιος.shortDef: of Latin origin; third; Tertius, a Christian:--Tertius.

τέρτυλλος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman:--Tertullus.

τεσσαρακονταετής.shortDef: from τεσσαράκοντα and ἔτος; of forty years of age:--(+ full, of) forty years (old).

glosses: from τέσσαρες and καί and δέκατος
τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος.shortDef: from τέσσαρες and καί and δέκατος; fourteenth:--fourteenth.

τεταρταῖος.shortDef: from τέσσαρες; pertaining to the fourth day:--four days.

τετράγωνος.shortDef: from τέσσαρες and γωνία; four-cornered, i.e. square:--foursquare.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a tetrad
τετράδιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (a tetrad; from τέσσαρες); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers:--quaternion.

glosses: from the multiplicative adverb of τέσσαρες and χίλιοι
τετρακισχίλιοι.shortDef: from the multiplicative adverb of τέσσαρες and χίλιοι; four times a thousand:--four thousand.

τετρακόσιοι.shortDef: plural from τέσσαρες and ἑκατόν; four hundred:--four hundred.

glosses: neuter of a compound of τέσσαρες and μήν
τετράμηνον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of τέσσαρες and μήν; a four months' space:--four months.

glosses: from τέσσαρες and a derivative of the base of πλεῖστος
τετραπλόος.shortDef: from τέσσαρες and a derivative of the base of πλεῖστος; quadruple:--fourfold.

τετράπους.shortDef: from τέσσαρες and πούς; a quadruped:--fourfooted beast.

τετραρχέω.shortDef: from τετράρχης; to be a tetrarch:--(be) tetrarch.

τετράρχης.shortDef: from τέσσαρες and ἄρχω; the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch"):--tetrarch.

τεφρόω.shortDef: from  (ashes); to incinerate, i.e. consume:--turn to ashes.

τέχνη.shortDef: from the base of τίκτω; art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill:--art, craft, occupation.

τεχνίτης.shortDef: from τέχνη; an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator):--builder, craftsman.

τήκω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to liquefy:--melt.

glosses: adverb from a compound of a derivative of τέλος and αὐγή
τηλαυγῶς.shortDef: adverb from a compound of a derivative of τέλος and αὐγή; in a far-shining manner, i.e. plainly:--clearly.

glosses: from a compound of ὁ with ἡλίκος and οὗτος
τηλικοῦτος.shortDef: from a compound of ὁ with ἡλίκος and οὗτος; such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast:--so great, so mighty.

τηρέω.shortDef: from  (a watch; perhaps akin to θεωρέω); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from φυλάσσω, which is properly to prevent escaping; and from κουστωδία, which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. to note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried):--hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch.

τήρησις.shortDef: from τηρέω; a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison:--hold.

τιβεριάς.shortDef: from Τιβέριος; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine:--Tiberias.

τιβέριος.shortDef: of Latin origin; probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor:--Tiberius.

glosses: a prolonged form of a primary               (which is used only as alternate in                               certain tenses)
τίθημι.shortDef: a prolonged form of a primary               (which is used only as alternate in                               certain tenses); to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from ἵστημι, which properly denotes an upright and active position, while κεῖμαι is properly reflexive and utterly  prostrate):--+ advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.

glosses: a strengthened form of a primary   (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses)
τίκτω.shortDef: a strengthened form of a primary   (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively:--bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.

glosses: perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι
τίλλω.shortDef: perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, and thus to σύρω; to pull off:--pluck.

τιμαῖος.shortDef: probably of Chaldee origin (compare טָמֵא); Timæus (i.e. Timay), an Israelite:--Timæus.
