τιμάω.shortDef: from τίμιος; to prize, i.e. fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere:--honour, value.

τιμή.shortDef: from τίνω; a value, i.e. money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself:--honour, precious, price, some.

τίμιος.shortDef: from τιμή; valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved:--dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.

τιμιότης.shortDef: from τίμιος; expensiveness, i.e. (by implication) magnificence:--costliness.

τιμόθεος.shortDef: from τιμή and θεός; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian:--Timotheus, Timothy.

τίμων.shortDef: from τιμή; valuable; Timon, a Christian:--Timon.

glosses: from a comparative of τιμή and  ouros (a guard)
τιμωρέω.shortDef: from a comparative of τιμή and  ouros (a guard); properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. to avenge (inflict a penalty):--punish.

τιμωρία.shortDef: from τιμωρέω; vindication, i.e. (by implication) a penalty:--punishment.

glosses: strengthened for a primary            (which is only used as an alternate in                        certain tenses)
τίνω.shortDef: strengthened for a primary            (which is only used as an alternate in                        certain tenses); to pay a price, i.e. as a penalty:--be punished with.

τὶς.shortDef: an enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object:--a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever).

τίς.shortDef: probably emphatic of τὶς; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions):--every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.

τίτλος.shortDef: of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard):--title.

glosses: of Latin origin but uncertain significance
τίτος.shortDef: of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian:--Titus.

glosses: probably for the dative case of ὁ
τοί.shortDef: probably for the dative case of ὁ; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth:--(used only with other particles in the comparative, as καίτοιγε, μέντοι, τοιγαροῦν, τοίνυν, etc.)

glosses: from τοί and γάρ and οὖν
τοιγαροῦν.shortDef: from τοί and γάρ and οὖν; truly for then, i.e. consequently:--there-(where-)fore.

τοίνυν.shortDef: from τοί and νῦν; truly now, i.e. accordingly:--then, therefore.

τοιόσδε.shortDef: (including the other inflections); from a derivative of 5104 and δέ; such-like then, i.e. so great:--such.

τοιοῦτος.shortDef: (including the other inflections); from τοί and οὗτος; truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality):--like, such (an one).

τοῖχος.shortDef: another form of τεῖχος; a wall:--wall.

τόκος.shortDef: from the base of τίκτω; interest on money loaned (as a produce):--usury.

τολμάω.shortDef: from  (boldness; probably itself from the base of τέλος through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while θαῤῥέω is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous:--be bold, boldly, dare, durst.

glosses: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of 5111 (as adverb)
τολμηρότερον.shortDef: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of 5111 (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise:--the more boldly.

glosses: comparative of a derivative of the primary  (to cut
τομώτερος.shortDef: comparative of a derivative of the primary  (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than κόπτω, as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen:--sharper.

τόξον.shortDef: from the base of τίκτω; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric):--bow.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of  (a "topaz"
τοπάζιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of  (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite:--topaz.

τόπος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas χώρα is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard:--coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.

τοσοῦτος.shortDef: from  (so much; apparently from ὁ and ὅς) and οὗτος (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space):--as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.

glosses: from (the neuter of) ὁ and ὅτε
τότε.shortDef: from (the neuter of) ὁ and ὅτε; the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution):--that time, then.

τοῦ.shortDef: properly, the genitive case of ὁ; sometimes used for τούτου; of this person:--his.

glosses: contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ἐναντίον
τοὐναντίον.shortDef: contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ἐναντίον; on the contrary:--contrariwise.

glosses: contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ὄνομα
τοὔνομα.shortDef: contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ὄνομα; the name (is):--named.

τουτέστι.shortDef: contraction for τοῦτο and ἐστί; that is:--that is (to say).

glosses: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of οὗτος
τοῦτο.shortDef: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of οὗτος; that thing:--here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).

glosses: dative case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος
τούτοις.shortDef: dative case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things):--such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those.

glosses: accusative case singular masculine of οὗτος
τοῦτον.shortDef: accusative case singular masculine of οὗτος; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition):--him, the same, that, this.

glosses: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος
τούτου.shortDef: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing):--here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus.

glosses: accusative case plural masculine of οὗτος
τούτους.shortDef: accusative case plural masculine of οὗτος; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition):--such, them, these, this.

glosses: dative case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος
τούτῳ.shortDef: dative case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing):--here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this.

glosses: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος
τούτων.shortDef: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things):--such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.

τράγος.shortDef: from the base of τρώγω; a he-goat (as a gnawer):--goat.

glosses: probably contracted from τέσσαρες and πεζῇ
τράπεζα.shortDef: probably contracted from τέσσαρες and πεζῇ; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest):--bank, meat, table.

τραπεζίτης.shortDef: from τράπεζα; a money-broker or banker:--exchanger.

τραῦμα.shortDef: from the base of  (to wound; akin to the base of θραύω, τρίβος, τρίζω, etc.); a wound:--wound.

τραυματίζω.shortDef: from τραῦμα; to inflict a wound:--wound.

τραχηλίζω.shortDef: from τράχηλος; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare):--opened.

glosses: probably from τρέχω (through the idea of mobility)
τράχηλος.shortDef: probably from τρέχω (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life:--neck.

glosses: perhaps strengthened from the base of ῥήγνυμι (as if jagged by rents)
τραχύς.shortDef: perhaps strengthened from the base of ῥήγνυμι (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy):--rock, rough.

τραχωνῖτις.shortDef: from a derivative of τραχύς; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria:--Trachonitis.

τρέμω.shortDef: strengthened from a primary  (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear:--be afraid, trembling.

τρέφω.shortDef: a primary verb (properly, ; but perhaps strengthened from the base of τροπή through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear):--bring up, feed, nourish.

τρέχω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb (properly, ; compare θρίξ); which uses   (the base of δρόμος) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively):--have course, run.

τριακόσιοι.shortDef: plural from τρεῖς and ἑκατόν; three hundred:--three hundred.

τρίβολος.shortDef: from τρεῖς and βέλος; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop):--brier, thistle.

τρίβος.shortDef: from  (to "rub"; akin to , , and the base of τράγος, τραῦμα); a rut or worn track:--path.

glosses: from a compound of τρεῖς and ἔτος
τριετία.shortDef: from a compound of τρεῖς and ἔτος; a three years' period (triennium):--space of three years.

τρίζω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy):--gnash.

glosses: neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and μήν as noun
τρίμηνον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and μήν as noun; a three months' space:--three months.

τρίς.shortDef: adverb from τρεῖς; three times:--three times, thrice.

glosses: neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and στέγη as noun
τρίστεγον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and στέγη as noun; a third roof (story):--third loft.

τρισχίλιοι.shortDef: from τρίς and χίλιοι; three times a thousand:--three thousand.

τρίτος.shortDef: ordinal from τρεῖς; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly:--third(-ly).

τρίχινος.shortDef: from θρίξ; hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair):--of hair.

τρόμος.shortDef: from τρέμω; a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear:--+ tremble(-ing).

glosses: from an apparently primary  to turn
τροπή.shortDef: from an apparently primary  to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. revolution (figuratively, variation):--turning.

τρόπος.shortDef: from the same as τροπή; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character:--(even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.

τροποφορέω.shortDef: from τρόπος and φορέω; to endure one's habits:--suffer the manners.

τροφή.shortDef: from τρέφω; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages):--food, meat.

τρόφιμος.shortDef: from τροφή; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian:--Trophimus.

τροφός.shortDef: from τρέφω; a nourisher, i.e. nurse:--nurse.

τροχιά.shortDef: from τροχός; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct:--path.

τροχός.shortDef: from τρέχω; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects:--course.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity
τρύβλιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl:--dish.

glosses: from a derivative of  (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry)
τρυγάω.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage:--gather.

τρυγών.shortDef: from  (to murmur; akin to τρίζω, but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing):--turtle-dove.

glosses: from a derivative of  (to wear away
τρυμαλιά.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to wear away; akin to the base of τραῦμα, τρίβος and τρώγω); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye:--eye. Compare τρύπημα.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of τρυμαλιά
τρύπημα.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of τρυμαλιά; an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye:--eye.

τρύφαινα.shortDef: from τρυφή; luxurious; Tryphæna, a Christian woman:--Tryphena.

τρυφάω.shortDef: from τρυφή; to indulge in luxury:--live in pleasure.

τρυφή.shortDef: from  (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. luxury or debauchery:--delicately, riot.

τρυφῶσα.shortDef: from τρυφή; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female:--Tryphosa.

τρωάς.shortDef: from  (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor:--Troas.

τρωγύλλιον.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor:--Trogyllium.

glosses: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of τραῦμα and τρίβος through the idea of corrosion or wear
τρώγω.shortDef: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of τραῦμα and τρίβος through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of τρυγών and τρίζω through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat:--eat.

glosses: probably for an obsolete  (for which the middle voice of another alternate  (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses
τυγχάνω.shortDef: probably for an obsolete  (for which the middle voice of another alternate  (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of τίκτω through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with εἰ), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with οὐ, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were):--be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special. Compare τύπτω.

glosses: from a derivative of τύπτω (meaning a drum
τυμπανίζω.shortDef: from a derivative of τύπτω (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death:--torture.

τύπος.shortDef: from τύπτω; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning):--en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.

glosses: a primary verb (in a strengthened form)
τύπτω.shortDef: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from παίω and πατάσσω, which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or πλήσσω with the fist (or a hammer), or ῥαπίζω with the palm; as well as from τυγχάνω, an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience):--beat, smite, strike, wound.

glosses: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of κύριος
τύραννος.shortDef: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of κύριος; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian:--Tyrannus.

τυρβάζω.shortDef: from  (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to θόρυβος); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb:--trouble.

τύριος.shortDef: from Τύρος; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus:--of Tyre.

τύρος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (צֹר): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine:--Tyre.

τυφλός.shortDef: from, τυφόω; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally):--blind.

τυφλόω.shortDef: from τυφλός; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure:--blind.

τυφόω.shortDef: from a derivative of τύφω; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit:--high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.

τύφω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame:--smoke.

τυφωνικός.shortDef: from a derivative of τύφω; stormy (as if smoky):--tempestuous.

τυχικός.shortDef: from a derivative of τυγχάνω; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian:--Tychicus.

ὑακίνθινος.shortDef: from ὑάκινθος; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. deep blue:--jacinth.

ὑάκινθος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon:-- jacinth.

ὑάλινος.shortDef: from ὕαλος; glassy, i.e. transparent:--of glass.

glosses: perhaps from the same as ὑετός (as being transparent like rain)
ὕαλος.shortDef: perhaps from the same as ὑετός (as being transparent like rain); glass:--glass.

ὑβρίζω.shortDef: from ὕβρις; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse:--use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).

ὕβρις.shortDef: from ὑπέρ; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury:--harm, hurt, reproach.

ὑβριστής.shortDef: from ὑβρίζω; an insulter, i.e. maltreater:--despiteful, injurious.

ὑγιαίνω.shortDef: from ὑγιής; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine):--be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).

ὑγιής.shortDef: from the base of αὐξάνω; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine):--sound, whole.

ὑγρός.shortDef: from the base of ὑετός; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh):--green.

ὑδρία.shortDef: from ὕδωρ; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply:--water-pot.

glosses: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω
ὑδροποτέω.shortDef: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages:--drink water.

glosses: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (as if looking watery)
ὑδρωπικός.shortDef: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical":--have the dropsy.

ὕδωρ.shortDef: from the base of ὑετός; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively:--water.

ὑετός.shortDef: from a primary  (to rain); rain, especially a shower:--rain.

glosses: from a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι
υἱοθεσία.shortDef: from a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God):--adoption (of children, of sons).

υἱός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship:--child, foal, son.

ὕλη.shortDef: perhaps akin to ξύλον; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel:--matter.

ὑμᾶς.shortDef: accusative case of ὑμεῖς; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition):--ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own).

ὑμεῖς.shortDef: irregular plural of σύ; you (as subjective of verb):--ye (yourselves), you.

ὑμεναῖος.shortDef: from  (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity:--Hymenæus.

ὑμέτερος.shortDef: from ὑμεῖς; yours, i.e. pertaining to you:--your (own).

ὑμῖν.shortDef: irregular dative case of ὑμεῖς; to (with or by) you:--ye, you, your(-selves).

ὑμνέω.shortDef: from ὕμνος; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song:--sing a hymn (praise unto).

glosses: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of  (to celebrate
ὕμνος.shortDef: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of  (to celebrate; probably akin to ᾄδω; compare עֲבוֹט); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms):--hymn.

ὑμῶν.shortDef: genitive case of ὑμεῖς; of (from or concerning) you:--ye, you, your (own, -selves).

ὑπάγω.shortDef: from ὑπό and ἄγω; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively:--depart, get hence, go (a-)way.

ὑπακοή.shortDef: from ὑπακούω; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission:--obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing).

ὑπακούω.shortDef: from ὑπό and ἀκούω; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority:--hearken, be obedient to, obey.

ὕπανδρος.shortDef: from ὑπό and ἀνήρ; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman:--which hath an husband.

glosses: from ὑπό and a derivative of ἀντί
ὑπαντάω.shortDef: from ὑπό and a derivative of ἀντί; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with:--(go to) meet.

ὑπάντησις.shortDef: from ὑπαντάω; an encounter or concurrence (with εἰς for infinitive, in order to fall in with):--meeting.

ὕπαρξις.shortDef: from ὑπάρχω; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth:--goods, substance.

glosses: neuter plural of present participle active of ὑπάρχω as noun
ὑπάρχοντα.shortDef: neuter plural of present participle active of ὑπάρχω as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions:--goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.

ὑπάρχω.shortDef: from ὑπό and ἄρχομαι; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb):--after, behave, live.

ὑπείκω.shortDef: from ὑπό and  (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender:--submit self.

ὑπεναντίος.shortDef: from ὑπό and ἐναντίος; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent:--adversary, against.

ὑπέρ.shortDef: a primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than:--(+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very. In the comparative, it retains many of the above applications.

glosses: middle voice from ὑπέρ and αἴρω
ὑπεραίρομαι.shortDef: middle voice from ὑπέρ and αἴρω; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty:--exalt self, be exalted above measure.

glosses: from ὑπέρ and the base of ἀκμήν
ὑπέρακμος.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and the base of ἀκμήν; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth:--+ pass the flower of (her) age.

ὑπεράνω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and ἄνω; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank):--far above, over.

ὑπεραυξάνω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and αὐξάνω; to increase above ordinary degree:--grow exceedingly.

glosses: from ὑπέρ and the base of βάσις
ὑπερβαίνω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and the base of βάσις; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach:--go beyond.

glosses: adverb from present participle active of ὑπερβάλλω
ὑπερβαλλόντως.shortDef: adverb from present participle active of ὑπερβάλλω; excessively:--beyond measure.

ὑπερβάλλω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and βάλλω; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent):--exceeding, excel, pass.

ὑπερβολή.shortDef: from ὑπερβάλλω; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with εἰς or κατά) pre- eminently:--abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.

ὑπερείδω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and εἴδω; to overlook, i.e. not punish:--wink at.

glosses: from ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος
ὑπερέκεινα.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος; above those parts, i.e. still farther:--beyond.

ὑπερεκτείνω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and ἐκτείνω; to extend inordinately:--stretch beyond.

glosses: from ὑπέρ and the alternate form of ἐκχέω
ὑπερεκχύνω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and the alternate form of ἐκχέω; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow:--run over.

ὑπερεντυγχάνω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and ἐντυγχάνω; to intercede in behalf of:--make intercession for.

ὑπερέχω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and ἔχω; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority:--better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.

ὑπερήφανος.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and φαίνω; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty:--proud.

ὑπερνικάω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and νικάω; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory:--more than conquer.

ὑπέρογκος.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and ὄγκος; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent:--great swelling.

ὑπεροχή.shortDef: from ὑπερέχω; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character):--authority, excellency.

ὑπερπερισσεύω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and περισσεύω; to super-abound:--abound much more, exceeding.

ὑπερπερισσῶς.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and περισσῶς; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly:--beyond measure.

ὑπερπλεονάζω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and πλεονάζω; to superabound:--be exceeding abundant.

ὑπερυψόω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and ὑψόω; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position:--highly exalt.

ὑπερφρονέω.shortDef: from ὑπέρ and φρονέω; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant:--think more highly.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of ὑπέρ
ὑπερῷον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of ὑπέρ; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story:--upper chamber (room).

ὑπέχω.shortDef: from ὑπό and ἔχω; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience:--suffer.

ὑπήκοος.shortDef: from ὑπακούω; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive:--obedient.

ὑπηρετέω.shortDef: from ὑπηρέτης; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve:--minister (unto), serve.

glosses: from ὑπό and a derivative of  (to row)
ὑπηρέτης.shortDef: from ὑπό and a derivative of  (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable):--minister, officer, servant.

glosses: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to ὑπό through the idea of subsilience)
ὕπνος.shortDef: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to ὑπό through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor:--sleep.

ὑπό.shortDef: a primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)):--among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.

ὑποβάλλω.shortDef: from ὑπό and βάλλω; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion:--suborn.

glosses: from a compound of ὑπό and γράφω
ὑπογραμμός.shortDef: from a compound of ὑπό and γράφω; an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively):--example.

ὑπόδειγμα.shortDef: from ὑποδείκνυμι; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration):--en-(ex-)ample, pattern.

ὑποδείκνυμι.shortDef: from ὑπό and δεικνύω; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish):--show, (fore-)warn.

ὑποδέχομαι.shortDef: from ὑπό and δέχομαι; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably:--receive.

ὑποδέω.shortDef: from ὑπό and δέω; to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals:--bind on, (be) shod.

ὑπόδημα.shortDef: from ὑποδέω; something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal:--shoe.

ὑπόδικος.shortDef: from ὑπό and δίκη; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned:--guilty.

glosses: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and ζυγός
ὑποζύγιον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and ζυγός; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey:--ass.

ὑποζώννυμι.shortDef: from ὑπό and ζώννυμι; to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck):--undergirt.

ὑποκάτω.shortDef: from ὑπό and κάτω; down under, i.e. beneath:--under.

glosses: middle voice from ὑπό and κρίνω
ὑποκρίνομαι.shortDef: middle voice from ὑπό and κρίνω; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend):--feign.

ὑπόκρισις.shortDef: from ὑποκρίνομαι; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"):--condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.

ὑποκριτής.shortDef: from ὑποκρίνομαι; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite":--hypocrite.

ὑπολαμβάνω.shortDef: from ὑπό and λαμβάνω; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume):--answer, receive, suppose.

ὑπολείπω.shortDef: from ὑποτρέχω and λείπω; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive):--be left.

glosses: neuter of a presumed compound of ὑπό and ληνός
ὑπολήνιον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed compound of ὑπό and ληνός; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat:--winefat.

ὑπολιμπάνω.shortDef: a prolonged form for ὑπολείπω; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath:--leave.

ὑπομένω.shortDef: from ὑπό and μένω; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere:--abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.

ὑπομιμνήσκω.shortDef: from ὑπό and μιμνήσκω; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory:--put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.

ὑπόμνησις.shortDef: from ὑπομιμνήσκω; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection:--remembrance.

ὑπομονή.shortDef: from ὑπομένω; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy:--enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting).

ὑπονοέω.shortDef: from ὑπό and νοιέω; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture:--think, suppose, deem.

ὑποπλέω.shortDef: from ὑπό and πλέω; to sail under the lee of:--sail under.

ὑποπνέω.shortDef: from ὑπό and πνέω; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze:--blow softly.

glosses: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and πούς
ὑποπόδιον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and πούς; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively):--footstool.

glosses: from a compound of ὑπό and ἵστημι
ὑπόστασις.shortDef: from a compound of ὑπό and ἵστημι; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively):--confidence, confident, person, substance.

ὑποστέλλω.shortDef: from ὑπό and στέλλω; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve):--draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.

ὑποστολή.shortDef: from ὑποστέλλω; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy:--draw back.

ὑποστρέφω.shortDef: from ὑπό and στρέφω; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively):--come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).

ὑποστρώννυμι.shortDef: from ὑπό and στρώννυμι; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet):--spread.

ὑποτάσσω.shortDef: from ὑπό and τάσσω; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey:--be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.

ὑποτίθημι.shortDef: from ὑπό and τίθημι; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest:--lay down, put in remembrance.

glosses: from ὑπό and τρέχω (including its alternate)
ὑποτρέχω.shortDef: from ὑπό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past:--run under.

glosses: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of τύπος
ὑποτύπωσις.shortDef: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of τύπος; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation:--form, pattern.

ὑποφέρω.shortDef: from ὑπό and φέρω; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship:--bear, endure.

ὑποχωρέω.shortDef: from ὑπό and χωρέω; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly:--go aside, withdraw self.

glosses: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι
ὑπωπιάζω.shortDef: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions):--keep under, weary.

ὗς.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"):--sow.

ὑστερέω.shortDef: from ὕστερος; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient):--come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.

ὑστέρημα.shortDef: from ὑστερέω; a deficit; specially, poverty:--that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.

ὑστέρησις.shortDef: from ὑστερέω; a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury:--want.

ὕστερον.shortDef: neuter of ὕστερος as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually:--afterward, (at the) last (of all).

glosses: comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind)
ὕστερος.shortDef: comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind); later:--latter.

ὑφαντός.shortDef: from  to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted:--woven.

ὑψηλός.shortDef: from ὕψος; lofty (in place or character):--high(-er, -ly) (esteemed).

glosses: from a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν
ὑψηλοφρονέω.shortDef: from a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant:--be highminded.

glosses: superlative from the base of ὕψος
ὕψιστος.shortDef: superlative from the base of ὕψος; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens:--most high, highest.

ὕψος.shortDef: from a derivative of ὑπέρ; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity:--be exalted, height, (on) high.

ὑψόω.shortDef: from ὕψος; to elevate (literally or figuratively):--exalt, lift up.

ὕψωμα.shortDef: from ὑψόω; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively):-- height, high thing.

glosses: a primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω in certain tenses)
φάγω.shortDef: a primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively):--eat, meat.

glosses: prolongation for the base of φῶς
φαίνω.shortDef: prolongation for the base of φῶς; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative):-- appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.

φάλεκ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (פֶּלֶג); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch:--Phalec.

φανερός.shortDef: from φαίνω; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally:--abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).

φανερόω.shortDef: from φανερός; to render apparent (literally or figuratively):--appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).

φανερῶς.shortDef: adverb from φανερός; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly:--evidently, openly.

φανέρωσις.shortDef: from φανερόω; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment:--manifestation.

φανός.shortDef: from φαίνω; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern:--lantern.

φανουήλ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (פְּנוּאֵל); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite:--Phanuel.

φαντάζω.shortDef: from a derivative of φαίνω; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle):--sight.

φαντασία.shortDef: from a derivative of φαντάζω; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"):--pomp.

φάντασμα.shortDef: from φαντάζω; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre:--spirit.

φάραγξ.shortDef: properly, strengthened from the base of πέραν or rather of ῥήγνυμι; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent):--valley.

φαραώ.shortDef: of foreign origin (פַּרְעֹה); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king:--Pharaoh.

φάρες.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (פֶּרֶץ); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite:--Phares.

φαρισαῖος.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (compare פָּרָשׁ); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary:--Pharisee.

φαρμακεία.shortDef: from φαρμακεύς; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively):--sorcery, witchcraft.

φαρμακεύς.shortDef: from  (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician:--sorcerer.

φάσις.shortDef: from φημί (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω); a saying, i.e. report:--tidings.

glosses: prolongation from the same as φημί
φάσκω.shortDef: prolongation from the same as φημί; to assert:--affirm, profess, say.

φάτνη.shortDef: from  (to eat); a crib (for fodder):--manager, stall.

φαῦλος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked:--evil.

glosses: probably akin to the base of φῶς (compare φθέγγομαι)
φέγγος.shortDef: probably akin to the base of φῶς (compare φθέγγομαι); brilliancy:--light.

φείδομαι.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently:--forbear, spare.

φειδομένως.shortDef: adverb from participle of φείδομαι; abstemiously, i.e. stingily:--sparingly.

glosses: by transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (as showing outside the other garments)
φελόνης.shortDef: by transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout):-- cloke.

φέρω.shortDef: a primary verb (for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely,            ;       and   ; to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows):--be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.

φεύγω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish:--escape, flee (away).

φῆλιξ.shortDef: of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman:--Felix.

φήμη.shortDef: from φημί; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"):--fame.

φημί.shortDef: properly, the same as the base of φῶς and φαίνω; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say:--affirm, say. Compare λέγω.

φῆστος.shortDef: of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman:--Festus.

φθάνω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at:--(already) attain, come, prevent.

φθαρτός.shortDef: from φθείρω; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable:--corruptible.

glosses: probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί
φθέγγομαι.shortDef: probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim:--speak.

glosses: probably strengthened from  (to pine or waste)
φθείρω.shortDef: probably strengthened from  (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave):--corrupt (self), defile, destroy.

φθινοπωρινός.shortDef: from derivative of   (to wane; akin to the base of φθείρω) and ὀπώρα (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves):--whose fruit withereth.

φθόγγος.shortDef: from φθέγγομαι; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental):--sound.

φθονέω.shortDef: from φθόνος; to be jealous of:--envy.

glosses: probably akin to the base of φθείρω
φθόνος.shortDef: probably akin to the base of φθείρω; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite):--envy.

φθορά.shortDef: from φθείρω; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively):--corruption, destroy, perish.

φιάλη.shortDef: of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"):--vial.

φιλάγαθος.shortDef: from φίλος and ἀγαθός; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue:--love of good men.

φιλαδέλφεια.shortDef: from  (the same as φιλάδελφος), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor:--Philadelphia.

φιλαδελφία.shortDef: from φιλάδελφος; fraternal affection:--brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.

φιλάδελφος.shortDef: from φίλος and ἀδελφός; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal:--love as brethren.

φίλανδρος.shortDef: from φίλος and ἀνήρ; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife:--love their husbands.

φιλανθρωπία.shortDef: from the same as φιλανθρώπως; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"):--kindness, love towards man.

glosses: adverb from a compound of φίλος and ἄνθρωπος
φιλανθρώπως.shortDef: adverb from a compound of φίλος and ἄνθρωπος; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely:--courteously.

φιλάργυρος.shortDef: from φίλος and ἄργυρος; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:--covetous.

φίλαυτος.shortDef: from φίλος and αὐτός; fond of self, i.e. selfish:--lover of own self.

φιλέω.shortDef: from φίλος; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while ἀγαπάω is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as θέλω and βούλομαι, or as θυμός and νοῦς respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness):--kiss, love.

φιλήδονος.shortDef: from φίλος and ἡδονή; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous:--lover of pleasure.

φιλήμων.shortDef: from φιλέω; friendly; Philemon, a Christian:--Philemon.

φίλητος.shortDef: from φιλέω; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:--Philetus.

φιλιππήσιος.shortDef: from Φίλιπποι; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi:--Philippian.

φίλιπποι.shortDef: plural of Φίλιππος; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:--Philippi.

φίλιππος.shortDef: from φίλος and ἵππος; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites:--Philip.

φιλόθεος.shortDef: from φίλος and θεός; fond of God, i.e. pious:--lover of God.

φιλόλογος.shortDef: from φίλος and λόγος; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:--Philologus.

φιλονεικία.shortDef: from φιλόνεικος; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute:--strife.

φιλόνεικος.shortDef: from φίλος and  (a quarrel; probably akin to νῖκος); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious:--contentious.

φιλόξενος.shortDef: from φίλος and ξένος; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality.

glosses: from a compound of φίλος and πρῶτος
φιλοπρωτεύω.shortDef: from a compound of φίλος and πρῶτος; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction:--love to have the preeminence.

φίλος.shortDef: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):--friend.

φιλόσοφος.shortDef: from φίλος and σοφός; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher":--philosopher.

φιλόστοργος.shortDef: from φίλος and  (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian:--kindly affectioned.

φιλότεκνος.shortDef: from φίλος and τέκνον; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal:--love their children.

glosses: middle voice from a compound of φίλος and τιμή
φιλοτιμέομαι.shortDef: middle voice from a compound of φίλος and τιμή; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something):--labour, strive, study.

φιλοφρόνως.shortDef: adverb from φιλόφρων; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly:--courteously.

φιλόφρων.shortDef: from φίλος and φρήν; friendly of mind, i.e. kind:--courteous.

glosses: active participle of the base of φλόξ
φλέγων.shortDef: active participle of the base of φλόξ; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian:--Phlegon.

φλογίζω.shortDef: from φλόξ; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion):--set on fire.

φλόξ.shortDef: from a primary  (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze:--flame(-ing).

φλυαρέω.shortDef: from φλύαρος; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against.

φλύαρος.shortDef: from  (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater:--tattler.

φοβερός.shortDef: from φόβος; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable:--fearful, terrible.

φοβέω.shortDef: from φόβος; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere:--be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of φοβέω
φόβητρον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of φοβέω; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent:--fearful sight.

glosses: from a primary  (to be put in fear)
φόβος.shortDef: from a primary  (to be put in fear); alarm or fright:--be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.

φοίβη.shortDef: feminine of  (bright; probably akin to the base of φῶς); Phœbe, a Christian woman:--Phebe.

φοινίκη.shortDef: from φοῖνιξ; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine:--Phenice, Phenicia.

φοῖνιξ.shortDef: probably the same as φοῖνιξ; Phœnix, a place in Crete:--Phenice.

φονεύς.shortDef: from φόνος; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος is a special term for a public bandit):--murderer.

φονεύω.shortDef: from φονεύς; to be a murderer (of):--kill, do murder, slay.

φόνος.shortDef: from an obsolete primary  (to slay); murder:--murder, + be slain with, slaughter.

φορέω.shortDef: from φόρος; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment:--bear, wear.

φόρον.shortDef: of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Ἄππιος; a station on the Appian road:--forum.

φόρος.shortDef: from φέρω; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas τέλος is usually a general toll on goods or travel):--tribute.

φορτίζω.shortDef: from φόρτος; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety):--lade, by heavy laden.

φορτίον.shortDef: diminutive of φόρτος; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service:--burden.

φόρτος.shortDef: from φέρω; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship:--lading.

φορτουνᾶτος.shortDef: of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian:--Fortunatus.

glosses: neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω
φραγέλλιον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment:--scourge.

glosses: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum
φραγελλόω.shortDef: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment:--scourge.

φραγμός.shortDef: from φράσσω; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively):--hedge (+ round about), partition.

glosses: probably akin to φράσσω through the idea of defining
φράζω.shortDef: probably akin to φράσσω through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound:-- declare.

glosses: apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν
φράσσω.shortDef: apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence):--stop.

φρέαρ.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison):--well, pit.

φρεναπατάω.shortDef: from φρεναπάτης; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude:--deceive.

φρεναπάτης.shortDef: from φρήν and ἀπάτη; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer:--deceiver.

glosses: probably from an obsolete  (to rein in or curb
φρήν.shortDef: probably from an obsolete  (to rein in or curb; compare φράσσω); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties):--understanding.

φρίσσω.shortDef: apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear):--tremble.

φρονέω.shortDef: from φρήν; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience):--set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.

φρόνημα.shortDef: from φρονέω; (mental) inclination or purpose:--(be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).

φρόνησις.shortDef: from φρονέω; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight:--prudence, wisdom.

φρόνιμος.shortDef: from φρήν; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative):--wise(-r).

φροντίζω.shortDef: from a derivative of φρήν; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:--be careful.

glosses: from a compound of πρό and ὁράω
φρουρέω.shortDef: from a compound of πρό and ὁράω; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect:--keep (with a garrison). Compare τηρέω.

φρυάσσω.shortDef: akin to βρύω, βρύχω; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult:--rage.

glosses: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (to roast or parch
φρύγανον.shortDef: neuter of a presumed derivative of  (to roast or parch; akin to the base of φλόξ); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig:--stick.

φρυγία.shortDef: probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor:--Phrygia.

φύγελλος.shortDef: probably from φεύγω; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian:--Phygellus.

φυγή.shortDef: from φεύγω; a fleeing, i.e. escape:--flight.

φυλακή.shortDef: from φυλάσσω; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively:--cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.

glosses: neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω
φυλακτήριον.shortDef: neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts:-- phylactery.

φύλαξ.shortDef: from φυλάσσω; a watcher or sentry:--keeper.

glosses: probably from φυλή through the idea of isolation
φυλάσσω.shortDef: probably from φυλή through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid:--beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare τηρέω.

φυλή.shortDef: from φύω (compare φύλλον); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan:--kindred, tribe.

φύλλον.shortDef: from the same as φυλή; a sprout, i.e. leaf:--leaf.

glosses: from a prolonged form of  (to mix a liquid with a solid
φύραμα.shortDef: from a prolonged form of  (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough:--lump.

φυσικός.shortDef: from φύσις; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive:--natural. Compare ψυχικός.

φυσικῶς.shortDef: adverb from φυσικός; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively:--naturally.

glosses: from φύσις in the primary sense of blowing
φυσιόω.shortDef: from φύσις in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty):--puff up.

φύσις.shortDef: from φύω; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:--(man-)kind, nature(-al).

φυτεία.shortDef: from φυτεύω; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable:--plant.

φυτεύω.shortDef: from a derivative of φύω; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine:--plant.

φύω.shortDef: a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively:--spring (up).

φωλεός.shortDef: of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place:--hole.

φωνέω.shortDef: from φωνή; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation:--call (for), crow, cry.

glosses: probably akin to φαίνω through the idea of disclosure
φωνή.shortDef: probably akin to φαίνω through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language:--noise, sound, voice.

glosses: from an obsolete  (to shine or make manifest
φῶς.shortDef: from an obsolete  (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω, φημί); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative):--fire, light.

φωστήρ.shortDef: from φῶς; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy:--light.

φωσφόρος.shortDef: from φῶς and φέρω; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively):--day star.

φωτεινός.shortDef: from φῶς; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively):--bright, full of light.

φωτίζω.shortDef: from φῶς; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively):--enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.

χαίρω.shortDef: a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well:--farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.

χαλάω.shortDef: from the base of χάσμα; to lower (as into a void):--let down, strike.

χαλδαῖος.shortDef: probably of Hebrew or (כַּשְׂדִּי); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates:--Chaldæan.

glosses: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of reducing the strength
χαλεπός.shortDef: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious:--fierce, perilous.

glosses: from a compound of χαλινός and the reduplicated form of ἄγω
χαλιναγωγέω.shortDef: from a compound of χαλινός and the reduplicated form of ἄγω; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively):--bridle.

χαλινός.shortDef: from χαλάω; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit):--bit, bridle.

χαλκεύς.shortDef: from χαλκός; a copper-worker or brazier:--coppersmith.

χαλκηδών.shortDef: from χαλκός and perhaps εἶδος; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony":--chalcedony.

χαλκίον.shortDef: diminutive from χαλκός; a copper dish:--brazen vessel.

glosses: neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy)
χαλκολίβανον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre:--fine brass.

glosses: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose)
χαλκός.shortDef: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it):--brass, money.

glosses: adverb perhaps from the base of χάσμα through the idea of a fissure in the soil
χαμαί.shortDef: adverb perhaps from the base of χάσμα through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate:--on (to) the ground.

χαναάν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (כְּנַעַן); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine:--Chanaan.

χανααναῖος.shortDef: from Χαναάν; a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine:--of Canaan.

χαρά.shortDef: from χαίρω; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight:--gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).

χάραγμα.shortDef: from the same as χάραξ; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue):--graven, mark.

χαρακτήρ.shortDef: from the same as χάραξ; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation):--express image.

χάραξ.shortDef: from  (to sharpen to a point; akin to γράφω through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege):--trench.

χαρίζομαι.shortDef: middle voice from χάρις; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue:--deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant.

glosses: accusative case of χάρις as preposition
χάριν.shortDef: accusative case of χάρις as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of:--be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully.

χάρις.shortDef: from χαίρω; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude):--acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).

χάρισμα.shortDef: from χαρίζομαι; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:--(free) gift.

χαριτόω.shortDef: from χάρις; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor:--make accepted, be highly favoured.

χαῤῥάν.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (חָרָן); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia:--Charran.

χάρτης.shortDef: from the same as χάραξ; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over):--paper.

glosses: from a form of an obsolete primary  (to "gape" or "yawn")
χάσμα.shortDef: from a form of an obsolete primary  (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval):--gulf.

glosses: from a form of the same as χάσμα
χεῖλος.shortDef: from a form of the same as χάσμα; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water):--lip, shore.

χειμάζω.shortDef: from the same as χειμών; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale:--be tossed with tempest.

glosses: from the base of χειμών and ῥέω
χείμαῤῥος.shortDef: from the base of χειμών and ῥέω; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent:--brook.

χειμών.shortDef: from a derivative of  (to pour; akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter:--tempest, foul weather, winter.

glosses: perhaps from the base of χειμών in the sense of its congener the base of χάσμα (through the idea of hollowness for grasping)
χείρ.shortDef: perhaps from the base of χειμών in the sense of its congener the base of χάσμα (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument):--hand.

χειραγωγέω.shortDef: from χειραγωγός; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person):--lead by the hand.

glosses: from χείρ and a reduplicated form of ἄγω
χειραγωγός.shortDef: from χείρ and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person):--some to lead by the hand.

glosses: neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω
χειρόγραφον.shortDef: neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)):--handwriting.

glosses: from χείρ and a derivative of ποιέω
χειροποίητος.shortDef: from χείρ and a derivative of ποιέω; manufactured, i.e. of human construction:--made by (make with) hands.

glosses: from a comparative of χείρ and  (to stretch)
χειροτονέω.shortDef: from a comparative of χείρ and  (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint:--choose, ordain.

χείρων.shortDef: irregular comparative of κακός; from an obsolete equivalent  (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally):--sorer, worse.

χερουβίμ.shortDef: plural of Hebrew origin (כְּרוּב); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim):--cherubims.

glosses: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of χάσμα through the idea of deficiency
χήρα.shortDef: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of χάσμα through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively:--widow.

χθές.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto:--yesterday.

χιλίαρχος.shortDef: from χίλιοι and ἄρχω; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel:--(chief, high) captain.

χίλιοι.shortDef: plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand:--thousand.

χίος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean:--Chios.

χιτών.shortDef: of foreign origin (כְּתֹנֶת); a tunic or shirt:--clothes, coat, garment.

glosses: perhaps akin to the base of χάσμα (χαλάω) or χειμών (as descending or empty)
χιών.shortDef: perhaps akin to the base of χάσμα (χαλάω) or χειμών (as descending or empty); snow:--snow.

χλαμύς.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a military cloak:--robe.

glosses: from a derivative probably of χεῖλος
χλευάζω.shortDef: from a derivative probably of χεῖλος; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at:--mock.

glosses: feminine of apparently a primary word
χλόη.shortDef: feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloë, a Christian female:--Chloe.

χλωρός.shortDef: from the same as Χλόη; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored:--green, pale.

χξϛ.shortDef: the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (στίγμα as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral:--six hundred threescore and six.

χοϊκός.shortDef: from χόος; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene:--earthy.

χοῖνιξ.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a chœnix or certain dry measure:--measure.

χολάω.shortDef: from χολή; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"):--be angry.

glosses: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue)
χολή.shortDef: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.):--gall.

χόος.shortDef: from the base of χειμών; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt:--dust.

χοραζίν.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine:--Chorazin.

glosses: from a compound of χορός and ἄγω
χορηγέω.shortDef: from a compound of χορός and ἄγω; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish:--give, minister.

χορός.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir":--dancing.

χορτάζω.shortDef: from χόρτος; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance):--feed, fill, satisfy.

χόρτος.shortDef: apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation:--blade, grass, hay.

χουζᾶς.shortDef: of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod:--Chuza.

glosses: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from χείρ
χράομαι.shortDef: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from χείρ, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner:--entreat, use. Compare χράω; χρή.

glosses: probably the same as the base of χράομαι
χράω.shortDef: probably the same as the base of χράομαι; to loan:--lend.

glosses: from the base of χράομαι or χρή
χρεία.shortDef: from the base of χράομαι or χρή; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution:--business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.

glosses: from a derivative of χράω and ὀφειλέτης
χρεωφειλέτης.shortDef: from a derivative of χράω and ὀφειλέτης; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person:--debtor.

glosses: third person singular of the same as χράομαι or χράω used impersonally
χρή.shortDef: third person singular of the same as χράομαι or χράω used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be:--ought.

χρῄζω.shortDef: from χρεία; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of:--(have) need.

χρηματίζω.shortDef: from χρῆμα; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of χράομαι), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of χρεία) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title:--be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.

χρηματισμός.shortDef: from χρηματίζω; a divine response or revelation:--answer of God.

χρῆσις.shortDef: from χράομαι; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body):--use.

χρηστεύομαι.shortDef: middle voice from χρηστός; to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently:--be kind.

glosses: from a compound of χρηστός and λέγω
χρηστολογία.shortDef: from a compound of χρηστός and λέγω; fair speech, i.e. plausibility:--good words.

χρηστός.shortDef: from χράομαι; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals):--better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind.

χρηστότης.shortDef: from χρηστός; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor):--gentleness, good(-ness), kindness.

χρῖσμα.shortDef: from χρίω; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit:--anointing, unction.

χριστιανός.shortDef: from Χριστός; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ:--Christian.

χριστός.shortDef: from χρίω; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus:--Christ.

glosses: probably akin to χράομαι through the idea of contact
χρίω.shortDef: probably akin to χράομαι through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service:--anoint.

χρονίζω.shortDef: from χρόνος; to take time, i.e. linger:--delay, tarry.

χρόνος.shortDef: of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from καιρός, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from αἰών, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay:--+ years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.

glosses: from a presumed compound of χρόνος and the base of τρίβος
χρονοτριβέω.shortDef: from a presumed compound of χρόνος and the base of τρίβος; to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger):--spend time.

χρύσεος.shortDef: from χρυσός; made of gold:--of gold, golden.

χρυσίον.shortDef: diminutive of χρυσός; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin:--gold.

χρυσοδακτύλιος.shortDef: from χρυσός and δακτύλιος; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry:--with a gold ring.

χρυσόλιθος.shortDef: from χρυσός and λίθος; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite"):--chrysolite.

χρυσόπρασος.shortDef: from χρυσός and  (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase"):--chrysoprase.

glosses: perhaps from the base of χράομαι (through the idea of the utility of the metal)
χρυσός.shortDef: perhaps from the base of χράομαι (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin:--gold.

χρυσόω.shortDef: from χρυσός; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments:--deck.

glosses: probably akin to the base of χράομαι through the idea of handling
χρώς.shortDef: probably akin to the base of χράομαι through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin):--body.

χωλός.shortDef: apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping:--cripple, halt, lame.

glosses: feminine of a derivative of the base of χάσμα through the idea of empty expanse
χώρα.shortDef: feminine of a derivative of the base of χάσμα through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants):--coast, county, fields, ground, land, region. Compare τόπος.

χωρέω.shortDef: from χώρα; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively):--come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.

χωρίζω.shortDef: from χώρα; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away:--depart, put asunder, separate.

χωρίον.shortDef: diminutive of χώρα; a spot or plot of ground:--field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.

χωρίς.shortDef: adverb from χώρα; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition):--beside, by itself, without.

χῶρος.shortDef: of Latin origin; the north-west wind:--north west.

glosses: probably strengthened from  (to rub or touch the surface
ψάλλω.shortDef: probably strengthened from  (to rub or touch the surface; compare ψώχω); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes):--make melody, sing (psalms).

ψαλμός.shortDef: from ψάλλω; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms:--psalm. Compare ᾠδή.

ψευδάδελφος.shortDef: from ψευδής and ἀδελφός; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate:--false brethren.

ψευδαπόστολος.shortDef: from ψευδής and ἀπόστολος; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher:--false teacher.

ψευδής.shortDef: from ψεύδομαι; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked:--false, liar.

ψευδοδιδάσκαλος.shortDef: from ψευδής and διδάσκαλος; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine:--false teacher.

ψευδολόγος.shortDef: from ψευδής and λέγω; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine:--speaking lies.

glosses: middle voice of an apparently primary verb
ψεύδομαι.shortDef: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood:--falsely, lie.

glosses: from ψευδής and a kindred form of μάρτυς
ψευδομάρτυρ.shortDef: from ψευδής and a kindred form of μάρτυς; a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony:--false witness.

ψευδομαρτυρέω.shortDef: from ψευδομάρτυρ; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence:--be a false witness.

ψευδοπροφήτης.shortDef: from ψευδής and προφήτης; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor:--false prophet.

ψευδόχριστος.shortDef: from ψευδής and Χριστός; a spurious Messiah:--false Christ.

ψευδώνυμος.shortDef: from ψευδής and ὄνομα; untruly named:--falsely so called.

ψεῦσμα.shortDef: from ψεύδομαι; a fabrication, i.e. falsehood:--lie.

glosses: from the base of ψάλλω (compare ψῆφος)
ψηλαφάω.shortDef: from the base of ψάλλω (compare ψῆφος); to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for:--feel after, handle, touch.

ψηφίζω.shortDef: from ψῆφος; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute:--count.

ψῆφος.shortDef: from the same as ψηλαφάω; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote:--stone, voice.

ψιθυρισμός.shortDef: from a derivative of  (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to ψεύδομαι); whispering, i.e. secret detraction:--whispering.

ψιθυριστής.shortDef: from the same as ψιθυρισμός; a secret calumniator:--whisperer.

glosses: diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψάλλω (meaning a crumb)
ψιχίον.shortDef: diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψάλλω (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel:--crumb.

ψυχή.shortDef: from ψύχω; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from πνεῦμα, which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from ζωή, which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ and חַי):--heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.

ψυχικός.shortDef: from ψυχή; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from πνευματικός, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from φυσικός, which is the lower or bestial nature):--natural, sensual.

ψύχω.shortDef: a primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from πνέω, which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of ἀήρ, which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by  evaporation) to chill (figuratively):--wax cold.

ψωμίζω.shortDef: from the base of ψωμίον; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish:--(bestow to) feed.

glosses: diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψώχω
ψωμίον.shortDef: diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψώχω; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful:--sop.

glosses: prolongation from the same base as ψάλλω
ψώχω.shortDef: prolongation from the same base as ψάλλω; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand):--rub.

ὦ.shortDef: the subjunctive of εἰμί; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with εἰ and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be:--+ appear, are, (may, might,  should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.

ὠβήδ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (עוֹבֵד); Obed, an Israelite:--Obed.

glosses: from an adverb form of ὅδε
ὧδε.shortDef: from an adverb form of ὅδε; in this same spot, i.e. here or hither:--here, hither, (in) this place, there.

ᾠδή.shortDef: from ᾄδω; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while ὕμνος denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and ψαλμός still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation):--song.

ὠδίν.shortDef: akin to ὀδύνη; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth:--pain, sorrow, travail.

ὠδίνω.shortDef: from ὠδίν; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively):--travail in (birth).

glosses: perhaps from the alternate of φέρω
ὦμος.shortDef: perhaps from the alternate of φέρω; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne):--shoulder.

ὤν.shortDef: present participle of εἰμί; being:--be, come, have.

glosses: middle voice from an apparently primary  (a sum or price)
ὠνέομαι.shortDef: middle voice from an apparently primary  (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier πίμπρημι):-- buy.

ὥρα.shortDef: apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively):--day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time.

ὡραῖος.shortDef: from ὥρα; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)):--beautiful.

glosses: middle voice of an apparently primary verb
ὠρύομαι.shortDef: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar":--roar.

glosses: probably adverb of comparative from ὅς
ὡς.shortDef: probably adverb of comparative from ὅς; which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows):--about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed.

ὡσαννά.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (יָשַׁע and נָא); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration:--hosanna.

glosses: from ὡς and an adverb from αὐτός
ὡσαύτως.shortDef: from ὡς and an adverb from αὐτός; as thus, i.e. in the same way:--even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.

ὡσεί.shortDef: from ὡς and εἰ; as if:--about, as (it had been, it were), like (as).

ὡσηέ.shortDef: of Hebrew origin (הוֹשֵׁעַ); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite:--Osee.

ὥσπερ.shortDef: from ὡς and περ; just as, i.e. exactly like:--(even, like) as.

ὡσπερεί.shortDef: from ὥσπερ and εἰ; just as if, i.e. as it were:--as.

ὥστε.shortDef: from ὡς and τέ; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow):--(insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore.

ὠτίον.shortDef: diminutive of οὖς; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear:--ear.

glosses: from a derivative of the base of ὠφέλιμος
ὠφέλεια.shortDef: from a derivative of the base of ὠφέλιμος; usefulness, i.e. benefit:--advantage, profit.

ὠφελέω.shortDef: from the same as ὠφέλεια; to be useful, i.e. to benefit:--advantage, better, prevail, profit.

ὠφέλιμος.shortDef: from a form of ὄφελος; helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous:--profit(-able).
